chapters.ml: പ്രതിയോഗിയോടുകൂടെ അധികാരിയുടെ അടുക്കൽ പോകുമ്പോൾ വഴിയിൽവെച്ചു അവനോടു നിരന്നുകൊൾവാൻ ശ്രമിക്ക; അല്ലാഞ്ഞാൽ അവൻ നിന്നെ ന്യായാധിപന്റെ മുമ്പിൽ ഇഴെച്ചുകൊണ്ടു പോകയും ന്യായാധിപൻ നിന്നെ കോൽക്കാരന്റെ പക്കൽ ഏല്പിക്കയും കോൽക്കാരൻ തടവിൽ ആക്കുകയും ചെയ്യും.
chapters.niv: As you are going with your adversary to the magistrate, try hard to be reconciled on the way, or your adversary may drag you off to the judge, and the judge turn you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
chapters.nkjv: When you go with your adversary to the magistrate, make every effort along the way to settle with him, lest he drag you to the judge, the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
chapters.kjv: When thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, as thou art in the way, give diligence that thou mayest be delivered from him; lest he hale thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and the officer cast thee into prison.

chapters.ml: ഒടുക്കത്തെ കാശുപോലും കൊടുത്തുതീരുവോളം നീ അവിടെ നിന്നു പുറത്തു വരികയില്ല ” എന്നു ഞാൻ നിന്നോടു പറയുന്നു.
chapters.niv: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny."
chapters.nkjv: I tell you, you shall not depart from there till you have paid the very last mite."
chapters.kjv: I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite.

chapters.ml: ആ സമയത്തു തന്നേ അവിടെ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്ന ചിലർ പീലാത്തൊസ് ചില ഗലീലക്കാരുടെ ചോര അവരുടെ യാഗങ്ങളോടു കലർത്തിയ വർത്തമാനം അവനോടു അറിയിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Now there were some present at that time who told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
chapters.nkjv: There were present at that season some who told Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.
chapters.kjv: There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilæans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു അവൻ ഉത്തരം പറഞ്ഞതു: “ആ ഗലീലക്കാർ ഇതു അനുഭവിക്കായാൽ എല്ലാ ഗലീലക്കാരിലും പാപികൾ ആയിരുന്നു എന്നു നിങ്ങൾക്കു തോന്നുന്നുവോ?
chapters.niv: Jesus answered, "Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans because they suffered this way?
chapters.nkjv: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Do you suppose that these Galileans were worse sinners than all other Galileans, because they suffered such things?
chapters.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilæans were sinners above all the Galilæans, because they suffered such things?

chapters.ml: അല്ലല്ല, മാനസാന്തരപ്പെടാഞ്ഞാൽ നിങ്ങൾ എല്ലാവരും അങ്ങനെതന്നേ നശിച്ചുപോകും” എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു പറയുന്നു.
chapters.niv: I tell you, no! But unless you repent, you too will all perish.
chapters.nkjv: I tell you, no; but unless you repent you will all likewise perish.
chapters.kjv: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

chapters.ml: അല്ല, ശീലോഹാമിലെ ഗോപുരം വീണു മരിച്ചുപോയ ആ പതിനെട്ടുപേർ യെരൂശലേമിൽ പാർക്കുന്ന സകല മനുഷ്യരിലും കുറ്റക്കാർ ആയിരുന്നു എന്നു തോന്നുന്നുവോ?
chapters.niv: Or those eighteen who died when the tower in Siloam fell on them—do you think they were more guilty than all the others living in Jerusalem?
chapters.nkjv: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them, do you think that they were worse sinners than all other men who dwelt in Jerusalem?
chapters.kjv: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?

chapters.ml: അല്ലല്ല, മാനസാന്തരപ്പെടാഞ്ഞാൽ നിങ്ങൾ എല്ലാവരും അങ്ങനെ തന്നേ നശിച്ചുപോകും” എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു പറയുന്നു.
chapters.niv: I tell you, no! But unless you repent, you too will all perish."
chapters.nkjv: I tell you, no; but unless you repent you will all likewise perish."
chapters.kjv: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

chapters.ml: അവൻ ഈ ഉപമയും പറഞ്ഞു: “ഒരുത്തന്നു തന്റെ മുന്തിരിത്തോട്ടത്തിൽ നട്ടിരുന്നോരു അത്തിവൃക്ഷം ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു; അവൻ അതിൽ ഫലം തിരഞ്ഞുവന്നു, കണ്ടില്ലതാനും.
chapters.niv: Then he told this parable: "A man had a fig tree growing in his vineyard, and he went to look for fruit on it but did not find any.
chapters.nkjv: He also spoke this parable: "A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.
chapters.kjv: He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.

chapters.ml: അവൻ തോട്ടക്കാരനോടു: ഞാൻ ഇപ്പോൾ മൂന്നു സംവത്സരമായി ഈ അത്തിയിൽ ഫലം തിരഞ്ഞുവരുന്നു കാണുന്നില്ലതാനും; അതിനെ വെട്ടിക്കളക അതു നിലത്തെ നിഷ്ഫലമാക്കുന്നതു എന്തിന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: So he said to the man who took care of the vineyard, ‘For three years now I’ve been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’
chapters.nkjv: Then he said to the keeper of his vineyard, ‘Look, for three years I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree and find none. Cut it down; why does it use up the ground?’
chapters.kjv: Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു അവൻ: കർത്താവേ, ഞാൻ അതിന്നു ചുറ്റും കിളെച്ചു വളം ഇടുവോളം ഈ ആണ്ടും കൂടെ നിൽക്കട്ടെ.
chapters.niv: " ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone for one more year, and I’ll dig around it and fertilize it.
chapters.nkjv: But he answered and said to him, ‘Sir, let it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
chapters.kjv: And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it :

chapters.ml: മേലാൽ കായിച്ചെങ്കിലോ - ഇല്ലെങ്കിൽ വെട്ടിക്കളയാം” എന്നു ഉത്തരം പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: If it bears fruit next year, fine! If not, then cut it down.’ "
chapters.nkjv: And if it bears fruit, well. But if not, after that you can cut it down.’ "
chapters.kjv: And if it bear fruit, well : and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.

chapters.ml: ഒരു ശബ്ബത്തിൽ അവൻ ഒരു പള്ളിയിൽ ഉപദേശിച്ചുകൊണ്ടിരുന്നു;
chapters.niv: On a Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,
chapters.nkjv: Now He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
chapters.kjv: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.

chapters.ml: അവിടെ പതിനെട്ടു സംവത്സരമായി ഒരു രോഗാത്മാവു ബാധിച്ചിട്ടു ഒട്ടും നിവിരുവാൻ കഴിയാതെ കൂനിയായോരു സ്ത്രീ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: and a woman was there who had been crippled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up at all.
chapters.nkjv: And behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bent over and could in no way raise herself up.
chapters.kjv: And, behold, there was a woman which had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise lift up herself .

chapters.ml: യേശു അവളെ കണ്ടു അടുക്കെ വിളിച്ചു: “സ്ത്രിയേ, നിന്റെ രോഗബന്ധനം അഴിഞ്ഞിരിക്കുന്നു” എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു അവളുടെ മേൽ കൈവെച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When Jesus saw her, he called her forward and said to her, "Woman, you are set free from your infirmity."
chapters.nkjv: But when Jesus saw her, He called her to Him and said to her, "Woman, you are loosed from your infirmity."
chapters.kjv: And when Jesus saw her, he called her to him , and said unto her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

chapters.ml: അവൾ ക്ഷണത്തിൽ നിവിർന്നു ദൈവത്തെ മഹത്വപ്പെടുത്തി.
chapters.niv: Then he put his hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and praised God.
chapters.nkjv: And He laid His hands on her, and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.
chapters.kjv: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.

chapters.ml: യേശു ശബ്ബത്തിൽ സൌഖ്യമാക്കിയതു കൊണ്ടു പള്ളി പ്രമാണി നീരസപ്പെട്ടു പുരുഷാരത്തോടു: വേല ചെയ്‍വാൻ ആറുദിവസമുണ്ടല്ലോ; അതിന്നകം വന്നു സൌഖ്യം വരുത്തിച്ചുകൊൾവിൻ; ശബ്ബത്തിൽ അരുതു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, the synagogue leader said to the people, "There are six days for work. So come and be healed on those days, not on the Sabbath."
chapters.nkjv: But the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath; and he said to the crowd, "There are six days on which men ought to work; therefore come and be healed on them, and not on the Sabbath day."
chapters.kjv: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because that Jesus had healed on the sabbath day, and said unto the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.

chapters.ml: കർത്താവു അവനോടു: “കപടഭക്തിക്കാരേ, നിങ്ങളിൽ ഓരോരുത്തൻ ശബ്ബത്തിൽ തന്റെ കാളയെയോ കഴുതയെയോ തൊട്ടിയിൽ നിന്നു അഴിച്ചു കൊണ്ടുപോയി വെള്ളം കുടിപ്പിക്കുന്നില്ലയോ?
chapters.niv: The Lord answered him, "You hypocrites! Doesn’t each of you on the Sabbath untie your ox or donkey from the stall and lead it out to give it water?
chapters.nkjv: The Lord then answered him and said, "Hypocrite! Does not each one of you on the Sabbath loose his ox or donkey from the stall, and lead it away to water it?
chapters.kjv: The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ സാത്താൻ പതിനെട്ടു സംവത്സരമായി ബന്ധിച്ചിരുന്ന അബ്രാഹാമിന്റെ മകളായ ഇവളെ ശബ്ബത്തുനാളിൽ ഈ ബന്ധനം അഴിച്ചു വിടേണ്ടതല്ലയോ ” എന്നു ഉത്തരം പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Then should not this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be set free on the Sabbath day from what bound her?"
chapters.nkjv: So ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound—think of it—for eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the Sabbath?"
chapters.kjv: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?

chapters.ml: അവൻ ഇതു പറഞ്ഞപ്പോൾ അവന്റെ വിരോധികൾ എല്ലാവരും നാണിച്ചു; അവനാൽ നടക്കുന്ന സകല മഹിമകളാലും പുരുഷാരം ഒക്കെയും സന്തോഷിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When he said this, all his opponents were humiliated, but the people were delighted with all the wonderful things he was doing.
chapters.nkjv: And when He said these things, all His adversaries were put to shame; and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by Him.
chapters.kjv: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ അവൻ പറഞ്ഞതു: “ദൈവരാജ്യം ഏതിനോടു സദൃശം? ഏതിനോടു അതിനെ ഉപമിക്കേണ്ടു?
chapters.niv: Then Jesus asked, "What is the kingdom of God like? What shall I compare it to?
chapters.nkjv: Then He said, "What is the kingdom of God like? And to what shall I compare it?
chapters.kjv: Then said he, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I resemble it?

chapters.ml: ഒരു മനുഷ്യൻ എടുത്തു തന്റെ തോട്ടത്തിൽ ഇട്ട കടുകുമണിയോടു അതു സദൃശം; അതു വളർന്നു വൃക്ഷമായി, ആകാശത്തിലെ പക്ഷികളും വന്നു അതിന്റെ കൊമ്പുകളിൽ വസിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds perched in its branches."
chapters.nkjv: It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and put in his garden; and it grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches."
chapters.kjv: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden; and it grew, and waxed a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.

chapters.ml: പിന്നെയും അവൻ “ദൈവരാജ്യത്തെ ഏതിനോടു ഉപമിക്കേണ്ടു? അതു പുളിച്ചമാവിനോടു തുല്ല്യം;
chapters.niv: Again he asked, "What shall I compare the kingdom of God to?
chapters.nkjv: And again He said, "To what shall I liken the kingdom of God?
chapters.kjv: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?

chapters.ml: അതു ഒരു സ്ത്രീ എടുത്തു മൂന്നുപറ മാവിൽ ചേർത്തു എല്ലാം പുളിച്ചുവരുവോളം അടക്കിവെച്ചു” എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: It is like yeast that a woman took and mixed into about sixty pounds of flour until it worked all through the dough."
chapters.nkjv: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal till it was all leavened."
chapters.kjv: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

chapters.ml: അവൻ പട്ടണംതോറും ഗ്രാമംതോറും സഞ്ചരിച്ചു യെരൂശലേമിലേക്കു യാത്ര ചെയ്തു.
chapters.niv: Then Jesus went through the towns and villages, teaching as he made his way to Jerusalem.
chapters.nkjv: And He went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.
chapters.kjv: And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ ഒരുത്തൻ അവനോടു: കർത്താവേ, രക്ഷിക്കപ്പെടുന്നവർ ചുരുക്കമോ എന്നു ചോദിച്ചതിന്നു അവനോടു പറഞ്ഞതു:
chapters.niv: Someone asked him, "Lord, are only a few people going to be saved?" He said to them,
chapters.nkjv: Then one said to Him, "Lord, are there few who are saved?" And He said to them,
chapters.kjv: Then said one unto him, Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,

chapters.ml: ഇടുക്കുവാതിലൂടെ കടപ്പാൻ പോരാടുവിൻ. പലരും കടപ്പാൻ നോക്കും കഴികയില്ലതാനും” എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു പറയുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "Make every effort to enter through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able to.
chapters.nkjv: "Strive to enter through the narrow gate, for many, I say to you, will seek to enter and will not be able.
chapters.kjv: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.

chapters.ml: വീട്ടുടയവൻ എഴുന്നേറ്റു കതകു അടെച്ചശേഷം നിങ്ങൾ പുറത്തുനിന്നു: കർത്താവേ, തുറന്നു തരേണമേ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞുകൊണ്ടു കതകിന്നു മുട്ടിത്തുടങ്ങുമ്പോൾ: “നിങ്ങൾ എവിടെ നിന്നു എന്നു ഞാൻ അറിയുന്നില്ല,” എന്നു അവൻ ഉത്തരം പറയും.
chapters.niv: Once the owner of the house gets up and closes the door, you will stand outside knocking and pleading, ‘Sir, open the door for us.’ "But he will answer, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’
chapters.nkjv: When once the Master of the house has risen up and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open for us,’ and He will answer and say to you, ‘I do not know you, where you are from,’
chapters.kjv: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:

chapters.ml: അന്നേരം നിങ്ങൾ: നിന്റെ മുമ്പിൽ ഞങ്ങൾ തിന്നുകയും കുടിക്കയും ഞങ്ങളുടെ തെരുക്കളിൽ നീ പഠിപ്പിക്കയും ചെയ്തുവല്ലൊ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞുതുടങ്ങും.
chapters.niv: "Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
chapters.nkjv: then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in Your presence, and You taught in our streets.’
chapters.kjv: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.

chapters.ml: അവനോ: “നിങ്ങൾ എവിടെ നിന്നു എന്നു ഞാൻ അറിയുന്നില്ല എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു പറയുന്നു; അനീതി പ്രവൃത്തിക്കുന്ന ഏവരുമായുള്ളോരേ, എന്നെ വിട്ടുപോകുവിൻ ”എന്നു പറയും.
chapters.niv: "But he will reply, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from. Away from me, all you evildoers!’
chapters.nkjv: But He will say, ‘I tell you I do not know you, where you are from. Depart from Me, all you workers of iniquity.’
chapters.kjv: But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.

chapters.ml: അവിടെ അബ്രാഹാമും യിസ്ഹാക്കും യാക്കോബും സകല പ്രവാചകന്മാരും ദൈവ രാജ്യത്തിൽ ഇരിക്കുന്നതും നിങ്ങളെ പുറത്തു തള്ളിക്കളഞ്ഞതും നിങ്ങൾ കാണുമ്പോൾ കരച്ചലും പല്ലുകടിയും ഉണ്ടാകും.
chapters.niv: "There will be weeping there, and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves thrown out.
chapters.nkjv: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and yourselves thrust out.
chapters.kjv: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.

chapters.ml: കിഴക്കുനിന്നും പടിഞ്ഞാറുനിന്നും തെക്കുനിന്നും വടക്കുനിന്നും അനേകർ വന്നു ദൈവരാജ്യത്തിൽ പന്തിയിലിരിക്കും.
chapters.niv: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will take their places at the feast in the kingdom of God.
chapters.nkjv: They will come from the east and the west, from the north and the south, and sit down in the kingdom of God.
chapters.kjv: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

chapters.ml: മുമ്പന്മാരായ്തീരുന്ന പിമ്പന്മാരുണ്ടു, പിമ്പന്മാരായ്തീരുന്ന മുമ്പന്മാരും ഉണ്ടു.
chapters.niv: Indeed there are those who are last who will be first, and first who will be last."
chapters.nkjv: And indeed there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last."
chapters.kjv: And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.

chapters.ml: ആ നാഴികയിൽ തന്നേ ചില പരീശന്മാർ അടുത്തുവന്നു: ഇവിടം വിട്ടു പൊയ്ക്കാൾക ഹെരോദാവു നിന്നെ കൊല്ലുവാൻ ഇച്ഛിക്കുന്നു എന്നു അവനോടു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: At that time some Pharisees came to Jesus and said to him, "Leave this place and go somewhere else. Herod wants to kill you."
chapters.nkjv: On that very day some Pharisees came, saying to Him, "Get out and depart from here, for Herod wants to kill You."
chapters.kjv: The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.

chapters.ml: അവൻ അവരോടു പറഞ്ഞതു: “നിങ്ങൾ പോയി ആ കുറുക്കനോടു: ഞാൻ ഇന്നും നാളെയും ഭൂതങ്ങളെ പുറത്താക്കുകയും രോഗശാന്തി വരുത്തുകയും മൂന്നാം നാളിൽ സമാപിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യും.
chapters.niv: He replied, "Go tell that fox, ‘I will keep on driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach my goal.’
chapters.nkjv: And He said to them, "Go, tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.’
chapters.kjv: And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.

chapters.ml: എങ്കിലും ഇന്നും നാളെയും മറ്റെന്നാളും ഞാൻ സഞ്ചരിക്കേണ്ടതാകുന്നു; യെരൂശലേമിന്നു പുറത്തുവെച്ചു ഒരു പ്രവാചകൻ നശിച്ചുപോകുന്നതു അസംഭവ്യമല്ലോ ” എന്നു പറവിൻ.
chapters.niv: In any case, I must press on today and tomorrow and the next day—for surely no prophet can die outside Jerusalem!
chapters.nkjv: Nevertheless I must journey today, tomorrow, and the day following; for it cannot be that a prophet should perish outside of Jerusalem.
chapters.kjv: Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.

chapters.ml: യെരൂശലേമേ, യെരൂശലേമേ, പ്രവാചകന്മാരെ കൊല്ലുകയും നിന്റെ അടുക്കൽ അയച്ചിരിക്കുന്നവരെ കല്ലെറികയും ചെയ്യുന്നവളേ, കോഴി തന്റെ കുഞ്ഞുങ്ങളെ ചിറകിൻ കീഴിൽ ചേർക്കുംപോലെ നിന്റെ മക്കളെ എത്രവട്ടം ചേർത്തുകൊൾവാൻ എനിക്കു മനസ്സായിരുന്നു; നിങ്ങൾക്കോ മനസ്സായില്ല.
chapters.niv: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing.
chapters.nkjv: "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the one who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, but you were not willing!
chapters.kjv: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!

chapters.ml: നിങ്ങളുടെ ഭവനം ശൂന്യമായ്ത്തീരും; കർത്താവിന്റെ നാമത്തിൽ വരുന്നവൻ അനുഗ്രഹിക്കപ്പെട്ടവൻ എന്നു നിങ്ങൾ പറയുവോളം നിങ്ങൾ എന്നെ കാണുകയില്ല ” എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു പറയുന്നു.
chapters.niv: Look, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’ "
chapters.nkjv: See! Your house is left to you desolate; and assuredly, I say to you, you shall not see Me until the time comes when you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!’ "
chapters.kjv: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

chapters.ml: പരീശപ്രമാണികളിൽ ഒരുത്തന്റെ വീട്ടിൽ അവൻ ഭക്ഷണം കഴിപ്പാൻ ശബ്ബത്തിൽ ചെന്നപ്പോൾ അവർ അവനെ ഉറ്റുനോക്കിക്കൊണ്ടിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: One Sabbath, when Jesus went to eat in the house of a prominent Pharisee, he was being carefully watched.
chapters.nkjv: Now it happened, as He went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees to eat bread on the Sabbath, that they watched Him closely.
chapters.kjv: And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him.

chapters.ml: മഹോദരമുള്ളോരു മനുഷ്യൻ അവന്റെ മുമ്പിൽ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: There in front of him was a man suffering from abnormal swelling of his body.
chapters.nkjv: And behold, there was a certain man before Him who had dropsy.
chapters.kjv: And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy.

chapters.ml: യേശു ന്യായശാസ്ത്രിമാരോടും പരീശന്മാരോടും: “ശബ്ബത്തിൽ സൌഖ്യമാക്കുന്നതു വിഹിതമോ അല്ലയോ ” എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു. അവരോ മിണ്ടാതിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: Jesus asked the Pharisees and experts in the law, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?"
chapters.nkjv: And Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?"
chapters.kjv: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?

chapters.ml: അവൻ അവനെ തൊട്ടു സൌഖ്യമാക്കി വിട്ടയച്ചു.
chapters.niv: But they remained silent. So taking hold of the man, he healed him and sent him on his way.
chapters.nkjv: But they kept silent. And He took him and healed him, and let him go.
chapters.kjv: And they held their peace. And he took him , and healed him, and let him go;

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ അവരോടു: “നിങ്ങളിൽ ഒരുത്തന്റെ മകനോ കാളയോ ശബ്ബത്തു നാളിൽ കിണറ്റിൽ വീണാൽ ക്ഷണത്തിൽ
chapters.niv: Then he asked them, "If one of you has a child or an ox that falls into a well on the Sabbath day, will you not immediately pull it out?"
chapters.nkjv: Then He answered them, saying, "Which of you, having a donkey or an ox that has fallen into a pit, will not immediately pull him out on the Sabbath day?"
chapters.kjv: And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?

chapters.ml: വലിച്ചെടുക്കയില്ലയോ ” എന്നു ചോദിച്ചതിന്നു പ്രത്യുത്തരം പറവാൻ അവർക്കു കഴിഞ്ഞില്ല.
chapters.niv: And they had nothing to say.
chapters.nkjv: And they could not answer Him regarding these things.
chapters.kjv: And they could not answer him again to these things.

chapters.ml: ക്ഷണിക്കപ്പെട്ടവർ മുഖ്യാസനങ്ങളെ തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കുന്നതു കണ്ടിട്ടു അവൻ അവരോടു ഒരുപമ പറഞ്ഞു:
chapters.niv: When he noticed how the guests picked the places of honor at the table, he told them this parable:
chapters.nkjv: So He told a parable to those who were invited, when He noted how they chose the best places, saying to them:
chapters.kjv: And he put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying unto them,

chapters.ml: ഒരുത്തൻ നിന്നെ കല്യാണത്തിന്നു വിളിച്ചാൽ മുഖ്യാസനത്തിൽ ഇരിക്കരുതു; പക്ഷെ നിന്നിലും മാനമേറിയവനെ അവൻ വിളിച്ചിരിക്കാം.
chapters.niv: "When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not take the place of honor, for a person more distinguished than you may have been invited.
chapters.nkjv: "When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, do not sit down in the best place, lest one more honorable than you be invited by him;
chapters.kjv: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him;

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ നിന്നെയും അവനെയും ക്ഷണിച്ചവൻ വന്നു: ഇവന്നു ഇടം കൊടുക്ക എന്നു നിന്നോടു പറയുമ്പോൾ നീ നാണത്തോടെ ഒടുക്കത്തെ സ്ഥലത്തുപോയി ഇരിക്കേണ്ടിവരും.
chapters.niv: If so, the host who invited both of you will come and say to you, ‘Give this person your seat.’ Then, humiliated, you will have to take the least important place.
chapters.nkjv: and he who invited you and him come and say to you, ‘Give place to this man,’ and then you begin with shame to take the lowest place.
chapters.kjv: And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.

chapters.ml: നിന്നെ വിളിച്ചാൽ ചെന്നു ഒടുക്കത്തെ സ്ഥലത്തു ഇരിക്ക; നിന്നെ ക്ഷണിച്ചവൻ വരുമ്പോൾ നിന്നോടു: സ്നേഹിതാ, മുമ്പോട്ടു വന്നു ഇരിക്ക എന്നുപറവാൻ ഇടവരട്ടെ; അപ്പോൾ പന്തിയിൽ ഇരിക്കുന്നവരുടെ മുമ്പിൽ നിനക്കു മാനം ഉണ്ടാകും.
chapters.niv: But when you are invited, take the lowest place, so that when your host comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all the other guests.
chapters.nkjv: But when you are invited, go and sit down in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes he may say to you, ‘Friend, go up higher.’ Then you will have glory in the presence of those who sit at the table with you.
chapters.kjv: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.

chapters.ml: തന്നെത്താൻ ഉയർത്തുന്നവൻ എല്ലാം താഴ്ത്തപ്പെടും; തന്നെത്താൻ താഴ്ത്തുന്നവൻ ഉയർത്തപ്പെടും.
chapters.niv: For all those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted."
chapters.nkjv: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted."
chapters.kjv: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

chapters.ml: തന്നെ ക്ഷണിച്ചവനോടു അവൻ പറഞ്ഞതു: “നീ ഒരു മുത്താഴമോ അത്താഴമോ കഴിക്കുമ്പോൾ സ്നേഹിതന്മാരേയും സഹോരദരന്മാരെയും ചാർച്ചക്കാരെയും സമ്പത്തുള്ള അയൽക്കാരെയും വിളിക്കരുതു; അവർ നിന്നെ അങ്ങോട്ടും വിളിച്ചിട്ടു നിനക്കു പ്രത്യുപകാരം ചെയ്യും.
chapters.niv: Then Jesus said to his host, "When you give a luncheon or dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers or sisters, your relatives, or your rich neighbors; if you do, they may invite you back and so you will be repaid.
chapters.nkjv: Then He also said to him who invited Him, "When you give a dinner or a supper, do not ask your friends, your brothers, your relatives, nor rich neighbors, lest they also invite you back, and you be repaid.
chapters.kjv: Then said he also to him that bade him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee.

chapters.ml: നീ വിരുന്നു കഴിക്കുമ്പോൾ ദരിദ്രന്മാർ, അംഗഹീനന്മാർ മുടന്തന്മാർ, കുരുടുന്മാർ എന്നിവരെ ക്ഷണിക്ക;
chapters.niv: But when you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind,
chapters.nkjv: But when you give a feast, invite the poor, themaimed, the lame, the blind.
chapters.kjv: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ നീ ഭാഗ്യവാനാകും; നിനക്കു പ്രത്യുപകാരം ചെയ്‍വാൻ അവർക്കു വകയില്ലല്ലോ; നീതിമാന്മാരരുടെ പുനരുത്ഥാനത്തിൽ നിനക്കു പ്രത്യുപകാരം ഉണ്ടാകും.
chapters.niv: and you will be blessed. Although they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."
chapters.nkjv: And you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you; for you shall be repaid at the resurrection of the just."
chapters.kjv: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.

chapters.ml: കൂടെ പന്തിയിരിരുന്നവരിൽ ഒരുത്തൻ ഇതു കേട്ടിട്ടു: ദൈവരാജ്യത്തിൽ ഭക്ഷണം കഴിക്കുന്നവൻ ഭാഗ്യവാൻ എന്നു അവനോടു പറഞ്ഞു;
chapters.niv: When one of those at the table with him heard this, he said to Jesus, "Blessed is the one who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God."
chapters.nkjv: Now when one of those who sat at the table with Him heard these things, he said to Him, "Blessed is he who shall eat bread in the kingdom of God!"
chapters.kjv: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.

chapters.ml: അവനോടു അവൻ പറഞ്ഞതു: “ഒരു മനുഷ്യൻ വലിയോരു അത്താഴം ഒരുക്കി പലരെയും ക്ഷണിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Jesus replied: "A certain man was preparing a great banquet and invited many guests.
chapters.nkjv: Then He said to him, "A certain man gave a great supper and invited many,
chapters.kjv: Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many:

chapters.ml: അത്താഴസമയത്തു അവൻ തന്റെ ദാസനെ അയച്ചു ആ ക്ഷണിച്ചവരോടു: എല്ലാം ഒരുങ്ങിയിരിക്കുന്നു; വരുവിൻ എന്നു പറയിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: At the time of the banquet he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’
chapters.nkjv: and sent his servant at supper time to say to those who were invited, ‘Come, for all things are now ready.’
chapters.kjv: And sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.

chapters.ml: എല്ലാവരും ഒരു പോലെ ഒഴികഴിവു പറഞ്ഞുതുടങ്ങി; ഒന്നാമത്തവൻ അവനോടു: ഞാൻ ഒരു നിലം കൊണ്ടതിനാൽ അതു ചെന്നു കാണേണ്ടുന്ന ആവശ്യം ഉണ്ടു; എന്നോടു ക്ഷമിച്ചുകൊള്ളേണം എന്നു ഞാൻ അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: "But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said, ‘I have just bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please excuse me.’
chapters.nkjv: But they all with one accord began to make excuses. The first said to him, ‘I have bought a piece of ground, and I must go and see it. I ask you to have me excused.’
chapters.kjv: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.

chapters.ml: മറ്റൊരുത്തൻ: ഞാൻ അഞ്ചേർകാളയെ കൊണ്ടിട്ടുണ്ടു; അവയെ ശോധന ചെയ്‍വാൻ പോകുന്നു; എന്നോടു ക്ഷമിച്ചുകൊള്ളേണം എന്നു ഞാൻ അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: "Another said, ‘I have just bought five yoke of oxen, and I’m on my way to try them out. Please excuse me.’
chapters.nkjv: And another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them. I ask you to have me excused.’
chapters.kjv: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.

chapters.ml: വേറൊരുത്തൻ: ഞാൻ ഇപ്പോൾവിവാഹം കഴിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു; വരുവാൻ കഴിവില്ല എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: "Still another said, ‘I just got married, so I can’t come.’
chapters.nkjv: Still another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.’
chapters.kjv: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

chapters.ml: ദാസൻ മടങ്ങിവന്നു യജമാനനോടു അറിയിച്ചു. അപ്പോൾ വീട്ടുടയവൻ കോപിച്ചു ദാസനോടു: നീ വേഗം പട്ടണത്തിലെ വീഥികളിലും ഇടത്തെരുക്കളിലും ചെന്നു ദരിദ്രന്മാർ, അംഗഹീനന്മാർ, കുരുടന്മാർ, മുടന്തന്മാർ, എന്നിവരെ കൂട്ടിക്കൊണ്ടുവരിക എന്നു കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: "The servant came back and reported this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and ordered his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the town and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame.’
chapters.nkjv: So that servant came and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor and themaimed and the lame and the blind.’
chapters.kjv: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ ദാസൻ: യജമാനനേ, കല്പിച്ചതു ചെയ്തിരിക്കുന്നു; ഇനിയും സ്ഥലം ഉണ്ടു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: " ‘Sir,’ the servant said, ‘what you ordered has been done, but there is still room.’
chapters.nkjv: And the servant said, ‘Master, it is done as you commanded, and still there is room.’
chapters.kjv: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.

chapters.ml: യജമാനൻ ദാസനോടു: നീ പെരുവഴികളിലും വേലികൾക്കരികെയും പോയി, എന്റെ വീടുനിറയേണ്ടതിന്നു കണ്ടവരെ അകത്തുവരുവാൻ നിർബ്ബന്ധിക്ക.
chapters.niv: "Then the master told his servant, ‘Go out to the roads and country lanes and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.
chapters.nkjv: Then the master said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
chapters.kjv: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

chapters.ml: ആ ക്ഷണിച്ച പുരുഷന്മാർ ആരും എന്റെ അത്താഴം ആസ്വദിക്കയില്ല എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു പറയുന്നു” എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: I tell you, not one of those who were invited will get a taste of my banquet.’ "
chapters.nkjv: For I say to you that none of those men who were invited shall taste my supper.’ "
chapters.kjv: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.

chapters.ml: ഏറിയ പുരുഷാരം അവനോടുകൂടെ പോകുമ്പോൾ അവൻ തിരിഞ്ഞു അവരോടു പറഞ്ഞതു:
chapters.niv: Large crowds were traveling with Jesus, and turning to them he said:
chapters.nkjv: Now great multitudes went with Him. And He turned and said to them,
chapters.kjv: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said unto them,

chapters.ml: എന്റെ അടുക്കൽ വരികയും അപ്പനെയും അമ്മയെയും ഭാര്യയെയും മക്കളെയും സഹോദരന്മാരെയും സഹോദരികളെയും സ്വന്തജീവനെയും കൂടെ പകെക്കാതിരിക്കയും ചെയ്യുന്നവന്നു എന്റെ ശിഷ്യനായിരിപ്പാൻ കഴികയില്ല.
chapters.niv: "If anyone comes to me and does not hate father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters—yes, even their own life—such a person cannot be my disciple.
chapters.nkjv: "If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he cannot be My disciple.
chapters.kjv: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.

chapters.ml: തന്റെ ക്രൂശു എടുത്തു കൊണ്ടു എന്റെ പിന്നാലെ വരാത്തവന്നു എന്റെ ശിഷ്യനായിരിപ്പാൻ കഴിയില്ല.
chapters.niv: And whoever does not carry their cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
chapters.nkjv: And whoever does not bear his cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple.
chapters.kjv: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

chapters.ml: നിങ്ങളിൽ ആരെങ്കിലും ഒരു ഗോപുരം പണിവാൻ ഇച്ഛിച്ചാൽ ആദ്യം ഇരുന്നു അതു തീർപ്പാൻ വക ഉണ്ടോ എന്നു കണക്കു നോക്കുന്നില്ലയോ?
chapters.niv: "Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. Won’t you first sit down and estimate the cost to see if you have enough money to complete it?
chapters.nkjv: For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not sit down first and count the cost, whether he has enough to finish it—
chapters.kjv: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it ?

chapters.ml: അല്ലെങ്കിൽ അടിസ്ഥാനം ഇട്ടശേഷം തീർപ്പാൻ വകയില്ല എന്നു വന്നേക്കാം;
chapters.niv: For if you lay the foundation and are not able to finish it, everyone who sees it will ridicule you,
chapters.nkjv: lest, after he has laid the foundation, and is not able to finish, all who see it begin to mock him,
chapters.kjv: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it , all that behold it begin to mock him,

chapters.ml: കാണുന്നവർ എല്ലാം; ഈ മനുഷ്യൻ പണിവാൻ തുടങ്ങി, തീർപ്പാനോ വകയില്ല എന്നു പരിഹസിക്കുമല്ലോ.
chapters.niv: saying, ‘This person began to build and wasn’t able to finish.’
chapters.nkjv: saying, ‘This man began to build and was not able to finish’?
chapters.kjv: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

chapters.ml: അല്ല, ഒരു രാജാവു മറ്റൊരു രാജാവിനോടു പട ഏല്പാൻ പുറപ്പെടുംമുമ്പേ ഇരുന്നു, ഇരുപതിനായിരവുമായി വരുന്നവനോടു താൻ പതിനായിരവുമായി എതിർപ്പാൻ മതിയോ എന്നു ആലോചിക്കുന്നില്ലയോ?
chapters.niv: "Or suppose a king is about to go to war against another king. Won’t he first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand men to oppose the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
chapters.nkjv: Or what king, going to make war against another king, does not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
chapters.kjv: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?

chapters.ml: പോരാ എന്നു വരികിൽ മറ്റവൻ ദൂരത്തിരിക്കുമ്പോൾ തന്നേ സ്ഥാനാപതികളെ അയച്ചു സമാധാനത്തിന്നായി അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: If he is not able, he will send a delegation while the other is still a long way off and will ask for terms of peace.
chapters.nkjv: Or else, while the other is still a great way off, he sends a delegation and asks conditions of peace.
chapters.kjv: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ തന്നേ നിങ്ങളിൽ ആരെങ്കിലും തനിക്കുള്ളതു ഒക്കെയും വിട്ടുപിരിയുന്നില്ല എങ്കിൽ അവന്നു എന്റെ ശിഷ്യനായിരിപ്പാൻ കഴികയില്ല.
chapters.niv: In the same way, those of you who do not give up everything you have cannot be my disciples.
chapters.nkjv: So likewise, whoever of you does not forsake all that he has cannot be My disciple.
chapters.kjv: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.

chapters.ml: ഉപ്പു നല്ലതു തന്നേ; ഉപ്പു കാരമില്ലാതെ പോയാൽ എന്തൊന്നുകൊണ്ടു അതിന്നു രസം വരുത്തും?
chapters.niv: "Salt is good, but if it loses its saltiness, how can it be made salty again?
chapters.nkjv: "Salt is good; but if the salt has lost its flavor, how shall it be seasoned?
chapters.kjv: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ നിലത്തിന്നും വളത്തിന്നും കൊള്ളുന്നതല്ല; അതിനെ പുറത്തു കളയും. കേൾപ്പാൻ ചെവി ഉള്ളവൻ കേൾക്കട്ടെ
chapters.niv: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; it is thrown out. "Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."
chapters.nkjv: It is neither fit for the land nor for the dunghill, but men throw it out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear!"
chapters.kjv: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

chapters.ml: ചുങ്കക്കാരും പാപികളും എല്ലാം അവന്റെ വചനം കേൾപ്പാൻ അവന്റെ അടുക്കൽ വന്നു.
chapters.niv: Now the tax collectors and sinners were all gathering around to hear Jesus.
chapters.nkjv: Then all the tax collectors and the sinners drew near to Him to hear Him.
chapters.kjv: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.

chapters.ml: ഇവൻ പാപികളെ കൈക്കൊണ്ടു അവരോടുകൂടി ഭക്ഷിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പരീശന്മാരും ശാസ്ത്രിമാരും പറഞ്ഞു പിറുപിറുത്തു.
chapters.niv: But the Pharisees and the teachers of the law muttered, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
chapters.nkjv: And the Pharisees and scribes complained, saying, "This Man receives sinners and eats with them."
chapters.kjv: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.

chapters.ml: അവരോടു അവൻ ഈ ഉപമ പറഞ്ഞു:
chapters.niv: Then Jesus told them this parable:
chapters.nkjv: So He spoke this parable to them, saying:
chapters.kjv: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,

chapters.ml: നിങ്ങളിൽ ഒരു ആൾക്കു നൂറു ആടുണ്ടു എന്നിരിക്കട്ടെ. അതിൽ ഒന്നു കാണാതെ പോയാൽ അവൻ തൊണ്ണൂറ്റൊമ്പതിനെയും മരുഭൂമിയിൽ വിട്ടേച്ചു. ആ കാണാതെപോയതിനെ കണ്ടെത്തുംവരെ നോക്കി നടക്കാതിരിക്കുമോ?
chapters.niv: "Suppose one of you has a hundred sheep and loses one of them. Doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine in the open country and go after the lost sheep until he finds it?
chapters.nkjv: "What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if he loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one which is lost until he finds it?
chapters.kjv: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?

chapters.ml: കണ്ടു കിട്ടിയാൽ സന്തോഷിച്ചു ചുമലിൽ എടുത്തു വീട്ടിൽ വന്നു സ്നേഹിതന്മാരെയും അയൽക്കാരെയും വിളിച്ചുകൂട്ടി:
chapters.niv: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders
chapters.nkjv: And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
chapters.kjv: And when he hath found it , he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

chapters.ml: കാണാതെ പോയ എന്റെ ആടിനെ കണ്ടുകിട്ടിയതുകൊണ്ടു എന്നോടു കൂടെ സന്തോഷിപ്പിൻ എന്നു അവരോടു പറയും.
chapters.niv: and goes home. Then he calls his friends and neighbors together and says, ‘Rejoice with me; I have found my lost sheep.’
chapters.nkjv: And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’
chapters.kjv: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ തന്നേ മാനസാന്തരം കൊണ്ടു ആവശ്യമില്ലാത്ത തൊണ്ണൂറ്റൊമ്പതു നീതിമാന്മാരെക്കുറിച്ചുള്ളതിനെക്കാൾ മാനസാന്തരപ്പെടുന്ന ഒരു പാപിയെച്ചൊല്ലി സ്വർഗ്ഗത്തിൽ അധികം സന്തോഷം ഉണ്ടാകും” എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു പറയുന്നു.
chapters.niv: I tell you that in the same way there will be more rejoicing in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need to repent.
chapters.nkjv: I say to you that likewise there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine just persons who need no repentance.
chapters.kjv: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.

chapters.ml: അല്ല, ഒരു സ്ത്രീക്കു പത്തു ദ്രഹ്മ ഉണ്ടു എന്നിരിക്കട്ടെ; ഒരു ദ്രഹ്മ കാണാതെ പോയാൽ അവൾ വിളക്കു കത്തിച്ചു വീടു അടിച്ചുവാരി അതുകണ്ടുകിട്ടുംവരെ സൂക്ഷ്മത്തോടെ അന്വേഷിക്കാതിരിക്കുമോ?
chapters.niv: "Or suppose a woman has ten silver coins and loses one. Doesn’t she light a lamp, sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?
chapters.nkjv: "Or what woman, having ten silver coins, if she loses one coin, does not light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?
chapters.kjv: Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it ?

chapters.ml: കണ്ടുകിട്ടിയാൽ സ്നേഹിതമാരെയും അയൽക്കാരത്തികളെയും വിളിച്ചുകൂട്ടി: കാണാതെപോയ ദ്രഹ്മ കണ്ടു കിട്ടിയതുകൊണ്ടു എന്നോടുകൂടെ സന്തോഷിപ്പിൻ എന്നു പറയും.
chapters.niv: And when she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors together and says, ‘Rejoice with me; I have found my lost coin.’
chapters.nkjv: And when she has found it, she calls her friends and neighbors together, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the piece which I lost!’
chapters.kjv: And when she hath found it , she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ തന്നേ മാനസാന്തരപ്പെടുന്ന ഒരു പാപിയെക്കുറിച്ചു ദൈവദൂതന്മാരുടെ മദ്ധ്യേ സന്തോഷം ഉണ്ടാകും” എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു പറയുന്നു.
chapters.niv: In the same way, I tell you, there is rejoicing in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
chapters.nkjv: Likewise, I say to you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
chapters.kjv: Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

chapters.ml: പിന്നെയും അവൻ പറഞ്ഞതു: “ഒരു മനുഷ്യന്നു രണ്ടു പുത്രന്മാർ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: Jesus continued: "There was a man who had two sons.
chapters.nkjv: Then He said: "A certain man had two sons.
chapters.kjv: And he said, A certain man had two sons:

chapters.ml: അവരിൽ ഇളയവൻ അപ്പനോടു: അപ്പാ, വസ്തുവിൽ എനിക്കു വരേണ്ടുന്ന പങ്കു തരേണമേ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു; അവൻ അവർക്കു മുതൽ പകുത്തുകൊടുത്തു.
chapters.niv: The younger one said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.
chapters.nkjv: And the younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me the portion of goods that falls to me.’ So he divided to them his livelihood.
chapters.kjv: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me . And he divided unto them his living.

chapters.ml: ഏറെനാൾ കഴിയുംമുമ്പെ ഇളയമകൻ സകലവും സ്വരൂപിച്ചു ദൂരദേശത്തേക്കു യാത്രയായി അവിടെ ദുർന്നടപ്പുകാരനായി ജീവിച്ചു, വസ്തു നാനാവിധമാക്കിക്കളഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: "Not long after that, the younger son got together all he had, set off for a distant country and there squandered his wealth in wild living.
chapters.nkjv: And not many days after, the younger son gathered all together, journeyed to a far country, and there wasted his possessions with prodigal living.
chapters.kjv: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.

chapters.ml: എല്ലാം ചെലവഴിച്ചശേഷം ആ ദേശത്തു കഠിനക്ഷാമം ഉണ്ടായിട്ടു അവന്നു മുട്ടുവന്നു തുടങ്ങി.
chapters.niv: After he had spent everything, there was a severe famine in that whole country, and he began to be in need.
chapters.nkjv: But when he had spent all, there arose a severe famine in that land, and he began to be in want.
chapters.kjv: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.

chapters.ml: അവൻ ആ ദേശത്തിലേ പൌരന്മാരിൽ ഒരുത്തനെ ചെന്നു ആശ്രയിച്ചു. അവൻ അവനെ തന്റെ വയലിൽ പന്നികളെ മേയ്പാൻ അയച്ചു.
chapters.niv: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him to his fields to feed pigs.
chapters.nkjv: Then he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
chapters.kjv: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.

chapters.ml: പന്നി തിന്നുന്ന വാളവരകൊണ്ടു വയറു നിറെപ്പാൻ അവൻ ആഗ്രഹിച്ചു എങ്കിലും ആരും അവന്നു കൊടുത്തില്ല.
chapters.niv: He longed to fill his stomach with the pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.
chapters.nkjv: And he would gladly have filled his stomach with the pods that the swine ate, and no one gave him anything.
chapters.kjv: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ സുബോധം വന്നിട്ടു അവൻ: എന്റെ അപ്പന്റെ എത്ര കൂലിക്കാർ ഭക്ഷണം കഴിച്ചു ശേഷിപ്പിക്കുന്നു; ഞാനോ വിശപ്പുകൊണ്ടു നശിച്ചുപോകുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "When he came to his senses, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have food to spare, and here I am starving to death!
chapters.nkjv: "But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
chapters.kjv: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ എഴുന്നേറ്റു അപ്പന്റെ അടുക്കൽ ചെന്നു അവനോടു: അപ്പാ, ഞാൻ സ്വർഗ്ഗത്തോടും നിന്നോടും പാപം ചെയ്തിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: I will set out and go back to my father and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
chapters.nkjv: I will arise and go to my father, and will say to him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you,
chapters.kjv: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,

chapters.ml: ഇനി നിന്റെ മകൻ എന്ന പേരിന്നു ഞാൻ യോഗ്യനല്ല; നിന്റെ കൂലിക്കാരിൽ ഒരുത്തനെപ്പോലെ എന്നെ ആക്കേണമേ എന്നു പറയും എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your hired servants.’
chapters.nkjv: and I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants." ’
chapters.kjv: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ അവൻ എഴുന്നേറ്റു അപ്പന്റെ അടുക്കൽ പോയി. ദൂരത്തു നിന്നു തന്നേ അപ്പൻ അവനെ കണ്ടു മനസ്സലിഞ്ഞു ഓടിച്ചെന്നു അവന്റെ കഴുത്തു കെട്ടിപ്പിടിച്ചു അവനെ ചുംബിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: So he got up and went to his father. "But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion for him; he ran to his son, threw his arms around him and kissed him.
chapters.nkjv: "And he arose and came to his father. But when he was still a great way off, his father saw him and had compassion, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
chapters.kjv: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

chapters.ml: മകൻ അവനോടു: അപ്പാ, ഞാൻ സ്വർഗ്ഗത്തോടും നിന്നോടും പാപം ചെയ്തിരിക്കുന്നു; ഇനി നിന്റെ മകൻ എന്നു വിളിക്കപ്പെടുവാൻ യോഗ്യനല്ല എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: "The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
chapters.nkjv: And the son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight, and am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
chapters.kjv: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.

chapters.ml: അപ്പൻ തന്റെ ദാസന്മാരോടു: വേഗം മേല്ത്തരമായ അങ്കി കൊണ്ടുവന്നു ഇവനെ ധരിപ്പിപ്പിൻ; ഇവന്റെ കൈക്കു മോതിരവും കാലിന്നു ചെരിപ്പും ഇടുവിപ്പിൻ.
chapters.niv: "But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
chapters.nkjv: "But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
chapters.kjv: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:

chapters.ml: തടിപ്പിച്ച കാളക്കുട്ടിയെ കൊണ്ടുവന്നു അറുപ്പിൻ; നാം തിന്നു ആനന്ദിക്ക.
chapters.niv: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let’s have a feast and celebrate.
chapters.nkjv: And bring the fatted calf here and kill it, and let us eat and be merry;
chapters.kjv: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it ; and let us eat, and be merry:

chapters.ml: ഈ എന്റെ മകൻ മരിച്ചവനായിരുന്നു; വീണ്ടും ജീവിച്ചു; കാണാതെ പോയിരുന്നു; കണ്ടുകിട്ടിയിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു; അങ്ങനെ അവർ ആനന്ദിച്ചു തുടങ്ങി.
chapters.niv: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’ So they began to celebrate.
chapters.nkjv: for this my son was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’ And they began to be merry.
chapters.kjv: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

chapters.ml: അവന്റെ മൂത്തമകൻ വയലിൽ ആയിരുന്നു; അവൻ വന്നു വീട്ടിനോടു അടുത്തപ്പോൾ വാദ്യവും നൃത്തഘോഷവും കേട്ടു,
chapters.niv: "Meanwhile, the older son was in the field. When he came near the house, he heard music and dancing.
chapters.nkjv: "Now his older son was in the field. And as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
chapters.kjv: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing.

chapters.ml: ബാല്യക്കാരിൽ ഒരുത്തനെ വിളിച്ചു: ഇതെന്തു എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: So he called one of the servants and asked him what was going on.
chapters.nkjv: So he called one of the servants and asked what these things meant.
chapters.kjv: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.

chapters.ml: അവൻ അവനോടു: നിന്റെ സഹോദരൻ വന്നു; നിന്റെ അപ്പൻ അവനെ സൌഖ്യത്തോടെ കിട്ടിയതുകൊണ്ടു തടിപ്പിച്ച കാളക്കുട്ടിയെ അറുത്തു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: ‘Your brother has come,’ he replied, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf because he has him back safe and sound.’
chapters.nkjv: And he said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and because he has received him safe and sound, your father has killed the fatted calf.’
chapters.kjv: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ അവൻ കോപിച്ചു, അകത്തു കടപ്പാൻ മനസ്സില്ലാതെ നിന്നു; അപ്പൻ പുറത്തു വന്നു അവനോടു അപേക്ഷിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: "The older brother became angry and refused to go in. So his father went out and pleaded with him.
chapters.nkjv: "But he was angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and pleaded with him.
chapters.kjv: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.

chapters.ml: അവൻ അവനോടു: ഇത്ര കാലമായി ഞാൻ നിന്നെ സേവിക്കുന്നു; നിന്റെ കല്പന ഒരിക്കലും ലംഘിച്ചിട്ടില്ല; എന്നാൽ എന്റെ ചങ്ങതികളുമായി ആനന്ദിക്കേണ്ടതിന്നു നീ ഒരിക്കലും എനിക്കു ഒരു ആട്ടിൻ കുട്ടിയെ തന്നിട്ടില്ല.
chapters.niv: But he answered his father, ‘Look! All these years I’ve been slaving for you and never disobeyed your orders. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
chapters.nkjv: So he answered and said to his father, ‘Lo, these many years I have been serving you; I never transgressed your commandment at any time; and yet you never gave me a young goat, that I might make merry with my friends.
chapters.kjv: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

chapters.ml: വേശ്യമാരോടു കൂടി നിന്റെ മുതൽ തിന്നുകളഞ്ഞ ഈ നിന്റെ മകൻ വന്നപ്പോഴേക്കോ തടിപ്പിച്ച കാളക്കുട്ടിയെ അവന്നുവേണ്ടി അറുത്തുവല്ലോ എന്നു ഉത്തരം പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: But when this son of yours who has squandered your property with prostitutes comes home, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
chapters.nkjv: But as soon as this son of yours came, who has devoured your livelihood with harlots, you killed the fatted calf for him.’
chapters.kjv: But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു അവൻ അവനോടു: മകനേ, നീ എപ്പോഴും എന്നോടു കൂടെ ഇരിക്കുന്നവല്ലോ; എനിക്കുള്ളതു എല്ലാം നിന്റെതു ആകുന്നു.
chapters.niv: " ‘My son,’ the father said, ‘you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.
chapters.nkjv: "And he said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that I have is yours.
chapters.kjv: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.

chapters.ml: നിന്റെ ഈ സഹോദരനോ മരിച്ചവനായിരുന്നു; വീണ്ടും ജീവച്ചു; കാണാതെ പോയിരുന്നു; കണ്ടു കിട്ടിയിരിക്കുന്നു. ആകയാൽ ആനന്ദിച്ചു സന്തോഷിക്കേണ്ടതാവശ്യമായിരുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: But we had to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’ "
chapters.nkjv: It was right that we should make merry and be glad, for your brother was dead and is alive again, and was lost and is found.’ "
chapters.kjv: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ അവൻ ശിഷ്യന്മാരോടു പറഞ്ഞതു: “ധനവാനായോരു മനുഷ്യന്നു ഒരു കാര്യവിചാരകൻ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു; അവൻ അവന്റെ വസ്തുവക നാനാവിധമാക്കുന്നു എന്നു ചിലർ അവനെ കുറ്റം പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Jesus told his disciples: "There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
chapters.nkjv: He also said to His disciples: "There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and an accusation was brought to him that this man was wasting his goods.
chapters.kjv: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.

chapters.ml: അവൻ അവനെ വിളിച്ചു: നിന്നെക്കൊണ്ടു ഈ കേൾക്കുന്നതു എന്തു? നിന്റെ കാര്യവിചാരത്തിന്റെ കണക്കു ഏല്പിച്ചുതരിക; നീ ഇനി കാര്യവിചാരകനായിരിപ്പാൻ പാടില്ല എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: So he called him in and asked him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your management, because you cannot be manager any longer.’
chapters.nkjv: So he called him and said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.’
chapters.kjv: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.

chapters.ml: എന്നാറെ കാര്യവിചാരകൻ: ഞാൻ എന്തു ചെയ്യേണ്ടു? യജമാനൻ കാര്യവിചാരത്തിൽ നിന്നു എന്നെ നീക്കുവാൻ പോകുന്നു; കിളെപ്പാൻ എനിക്കു പ്രാപ്തിയില്ല; ഇരപ്പാൻ ഞാൻ നാണിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do now? My master is taking away my job. I’m not strong enough to dig, and I’m ashamed to beg—
chapters.nkjv: "Then the steward said within himself, ‘What shall I do? For my master is taking the stewardship away from me. I cannot dig; I am ashamed to beg.
chapters.kjv: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.

chapters.ml: എന്നെ കാര്യവിചാരത്തിൽനിന്നു നീക്കിയാൽ അവർ എന്നെ തങ്ങളുടെ വീടുകളിൽ ചേർത്തുകൊൾവാൻ തക്കവണ്ണം ഞാൻ ചെയ്യേണ്ടതു എന്തു എന്നു എനിക്കു അറിയാം എന്നു ഉള്ളുകൊണ്ടു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: I know what I’ll do so that, when I lose my job here, people will welcome me into their houses.’
chapters.nkjv: I have resolved what to do, that when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.’
chapters.kjv: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ അവൻ യജമാനന്റെ കടക്കാരിൽ ഓരോരുത്തനെ വരുത്തി ഒന്നാമത്തവനോടു: നീ യജമാനന്നു എത്ര കടംപെട്ടിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: "So he called in each one of his master’s debtors. He asked the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
chapters.nkjv: "So he called every one of his master’s debtors to him, and said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
chapters.kjv: So he called every one of his lord’s debtors unto him , and said unto the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?

chapters.ml: നൂറു കുടം എണ്ണ എന്നു അവൻ പറഞ്ഞു. അവൻ അവനോടു: നിന്റെ കൈച്ചീട്ടു വാങ്ങി വേഗം ഇരുന്നു അമ്പതു എന്നു എഴുതുക എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: " ‘Nine hundred gallons of olive oil,’ he replied. "The manager told him, ‘Take your bill, sit down quickly, and make it four hundred and fifty.’
chapters.nkjv: And he said, ‘A hundred measures of oil.’ So he said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’
chapters.kjv: And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.

chapters.ml: അതിന്റെ ശേഷം മറ്റൊരുത്തനോടു: നീ എത്ര കടം പെട്ടിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു. നൂറു പറ കോതമ്പു എന്നു അവൻ പറഞ്ഞു; അവനോടു: നിന്റെ കൈച്ചീട്ടു വാങ്ങി എണ്പതു എന്നു എഴുതുക എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: "Then he asked the second, ‘And how much do you owe?’ " ‘A thousand bushels of wheat,’ he replied. "He told him, ‘Take your bill and make it eight hundred.’
chapters.nkjv: Then he said to another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ So he said, ‘A hundred measures of wheat.’ And he said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’
chapters.kjv: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore.

chapters.ml: ഈ അനീതിയുള്ള കാര്യവിചാരകൻ ബുദ്ധിയോടെ പ്രവർത്തിച്ചതുകൊണ്ടു യജമാനൻ അവനെ പുകഴ്ത്തി; വെളിച്ചമക്കളെക്കാൾ ഈ ലോകത്തിന്റെ മക്കൾ തങ്ങളുടെ തലമുറയിൽ ബുദ്ധിയേറിയവരല്ലോ.
chapters.niv: "The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the people of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the people of the light.
chapters.nkjv: So the master commended the unjust steward because he had dealt shrewdly. For the sons of this world are more shrewd in their generation than the sons of light.
chapters.kjv: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.

chapters.ml: അനീതിയുള്ള മമ്മോനെക്കൊണ്ടു നിങ്ങൾക്കു സ്നേഹിതന്മാരെ ഉണ്ടാക്കിക്കൊൾവിൻ എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു പറയുന്നു. അതു ഇല്ലാതെയാകുമ്പോൾ അവർ നിത്യകൂടാരങ്ങളിൽ നിങ്ങളെ ചേർത്തുകൊൾവാൻ ഇടയാകും.
chapters.niv: I tell you, use worldly wealth to gain friends for yourselves, so that when it is gone, you will be welcomed into eternal dwellings.
chapters.nkjv: "And I say to you, make friends for yourselves by unrighteous mammon, that when you fail, they may receive you into an everlasting home.
chapters.kjv: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.

chapters.ml: അത്യല്പത്തിൽ വിശ്വസ്തനായവൻ അധികത്തിലും വിശ്വസ്തൻ; അത്യല്പത്തിൽ നീതികെട്ടവൻ അധികത്തിലും നീതി കെട്ടവൻ.
chapters.niv: "Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
chapters.nkjv: He who is faithful in what is least is faithful also in much; and he who is unjust in what is least is unjust also in much.
chapters.kjv: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.

chapters.ml: നിങ്ങൾ അനീതിയുള്ള മമ്മോനിൽ വിശ്വസ്തരായില്ല എങ്കിൽ സത്യമായതു നിങ്ങളെ ആർ ഭരമേല്പിക്കും?
chapters.niv: So if you have not been trustworthy in handling worldly wealth, who will trust you with true riches?
chapters.nkjv: Therefore if you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
chapters.kjv: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches ?

chapters.ml: അന്യമായതിൽ വിശ്വസ്തരായില്ല എങ്കിൽ നിങ്ങൾക്കു സ്വന്തമായതു ആർ തരും?
chapters.niv: And if you have not been trustworthy with someone else’s property, who will give you property of your own?
chapters.nkjv: And if you have not been faithful in what is another man’s, who will give you what is your own?
chapters.kjv: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?

chapters.ml: രണ്ടു യജമാനന്മാരെ സേവിപ്പാൻ ഒരു ഭൃത്യന്നും കഴികയില്ല; അവൻ ഒരുവനെ പകെച്ചു മറ്റവനെ സ്നേഹിക്കും; അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഒരുത്തനോടു പറ്റിച്ചേർന്നു മറ്റവനെ നിരസിക്കും. നിങ്ങൾക്കു ദൈവത്തെയും മമ്മോനെയും സേവിപ്പാൻ കഴികയില്ല.
chapters.niv: "No one can serve two masters. Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money."
chapters.nkjv: "No servant can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will be loyal to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon."
chapters.kjv: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

chapters.ml: ഇതൊക്കെയും ദ്രവ്യാഗ്രഹികളായ പരീശന്മാർ കേട്ടു അവനെ പരിഹസിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all this and were sneering at Jesus.
chapters.nkjv: Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they derided Him.
chapters.kjv: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.

chapters.ml: അവൻ അവരോടു പറഞ്ഞതു: “നിങ്ങൾ നിങ്ങളെ തന്നേ മനുഷ്യരുടെ മുമ്പാകെ നീതീകരിക്കുന്നവർ ആകുന്നു; ദൈവമോ നിങ്ങളുടെ ഹൃദയം അറിയുന്നു; മനുഷ്യരുടെ ഇടയിൽ ഉന്നതമായതു ദൈവത്തിന്റെ മുമ്പാകെ അറെപ്പത്രേ.
chapters.niv: He said to them, "You are the ones who justify yourselves in the eyes of others, but God knows your hearts. What people value highly is detestable in God’s sight.
chapters.nkjv: And He said to them, "You are those who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is highly esteemed among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
chapters.kjv: And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.

chapters.ml: ന്യായപ്രമാണത്തിന്റെയും പ്രവാചകന്മാരുടെയും കാലം യോഹന്നാൻ വരെ ആയിരുന്നു; അന്നുമുതൽ ദൈവരാജ്യത്തെ സുവിശേഷിച്ചുവരുന്നു; എല്ലാവരും ബലാൽക്കാരേണ അതിൽ കടപ്പാൻ നോക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the good news of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing their way into it.
chapters.nkjv: "The law and the prophets were until John. Since that time the kingdom of God has been preached, and everyone is pressing into it.
chapters.kjv: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.

chapters.ml: ന്യായപ്രമാണത്തിൽ ഒരു പുള്ളി വീണുപോകുന്നതിനെക്കാൾ ആകാശവും ഭൂമിയും ഒഴിഞ്ഞുപോകുന്നതു എളുപ്പം.
chapters.niv: It is easier for heaven and earth to disappear than for the least stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.
chapters.nkjv: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one tittle of the law to fail.
chapters.kjv: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.

chapters.ml: ഭാര്യയെ ഉപേക്ഷിച്ചു മറ്റൊരുത്തിയെ വിവാഹം കഴിക്കുന്നവൻ എല്ലാം വ്യഭിചാരം ചെയ്യുന്നു; ഭർത്താവു ഉപേക്ഷിച്ചവളെ വിവാഹം കഴിക്കുന്നവനും വ്യഭിചാരം ചെയ്യുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and the man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
chapters.nkjv: "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery; and whoever marries her who is divorced from her husband commits adultery.
chapters.kjv: Whosoever putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and whosoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband committeth adultery.

chapters.ml: ധനവാനായോരു മനുഷ്യൻ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു; അവൻ ധൂമ്രവസ്ത്രവും പട്ടും ധരിച്ചു ദിനമ്പ്രതി ആഡംബരത്തോടെ സുഖിച്ചുകൊണ്ടിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "There was a rich man who was dressed in purple and fine linen and lived in luxury every day.
chapters.nkjv: "There was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen and fared sumptuously every day.
chapters.kjv: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:

chapters.ml: ലാസർ എന്നു പേരുള്ളോരു ദരിദ്രൻ വ്രണം നിറഞ്ഞവനായി അവന്റെ പടിപ്പുരക്കൽ കിടന്നു
chapters.niv: At his gate was laid a beggar named Lazarus, covered with sores
chapters.nkjv: But there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, full of sores, who was laid at his gate,
chapters.kjv: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,

chapters.ml: ധനവാന്റെ മേശയിൽ നിന്നു വീഴുന്നതു തിന്നു വിശപ്പടക്കുവാൻ ആഗ്രഹിച്ചു; നായ്ക്കളും വന്നു അവന്റെ വ്രണം നക്കും.
chapters.niv: and longing to eat what fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
chapters.nkjv: desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table. Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
chapters.kjv: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.

chapters.ml: ആ ദരിദ്രൻ മരിച്ചപ്പോൾ ദൂതന്മാർ അവനെ അബ്രാഹാമിന്റെ മടിയിലേക്കു കൊണ്ടുപോയി.
chapters.niv: "The time came when the beggar died and the angels carried him to Abraham’s side. The rich man also died and was buried.
chapters.nkjv: So it was that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
chapters.kjv: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;

chapters.ml: ധനവാനും മരിച്ചു അടക്കപ്പെട്ടു; പാതാളത്തിൽ യാതന അനുഭവിക്കുമ്പോൾ മേലോട്ടു നോക്കി ദൂരത്തു നിന്നു അബ്രാഹാമിനെയും അവന്റെ മടിയിൽ ലാസരിനെയും കണ്ടു:
chapters.niv: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus by his side.
chapters.nkjv: And being in torments in Hades, he lifted up his eyes and saw Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
chapters.kjv: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.

chapters.ml: അബ്രാഹാംപിതാവേ, എന്നോടു കനിവുണ്ടാകേണമേ; ലാസർ വിരലിന്റെ അറ്റം വെള്ളത്തിൽ മുക്കി എന്റെ നാവിനെ തണുപ്പിക്കേണ്ടതിന്നു അവനെ അയക്കേണമേ; ഞാൻ ഈ ജ്വാലയിൽ കിടന്നു വേദന അനുഭവിക്കുന്നു എന്നു വിളിച്ചു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: So he called to him, ‘Father Abraham, have pity on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in agony in this fire.’
chapters.nkjv: "Then he cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.’
chapters.kjv: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.

chapters.ml: അബ്രാഹാം: മകനേ, നിന്റെ ആയുസ്സിൽ നീ നന്മയും ലാസർ അവ്വണ്ണം തിന്മയും പ്രാപിച്ചു എന്നു ഓർക്ക; ഇപ്പോൾ അവൻ ഇവിടെ ആശ്വസിക്കുന്നു: നീയോ വേദന അനുഭവിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "But Abraham replied, ‘Son, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things, but now he is comforted here and you are in agony.
chapters.nkjv: But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things; but now he is comforted and you are tormented.
chapters.kjv: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.

chapters.ml: അത്രയുമല്ല ഞങ്ങൾക്കും നിങ്ങൾക്കും നടുവെ വലിയോരു പിളർപ്പുണ്ടാക്കിയിരിക്കുന്നു. ഇവിടെ നിന്നു നിങ്ങളുടെ അടുക്കൽ കടന്നുവരുവാൻ ഇച്ഛിക്കുന്നവർക്കു കഴിവില്ല; അവിടെനിന്നു ഞങ്ങളുടെ അടുക്കൽ കടന്നു വരുവാനും പാടില്ല എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been set in place, so that those who want to go from here to you cannot, nor can anyone cross over from there to us.’
chapters.nkjv: And besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, so that those who want to pass from here to you cannot, nor can those from there pass to us.’
chapters.kjv: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു അവൻ: എന്നാൽ പിതാവേ, അവനെ എന്റെ അപ്പന്റെ വീട്ടിൽ അയക്കേണമെന്നു ഞാൻ അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു;
chapters.niv: "He answered, ‘Then I beg you, father, send Lazarus to my family,
chapters.nkjv: "Then he said, ‘I beg you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house,
chapters.kjv: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house:

chapters.ml: എനിക്കു അഞ്ചു സഹോദരന്മാർ ഉണ്ടു; അവരും ഈ യാതനാസ്ഥലത്തു വരാതിരിപ്പാൻ അവൻ അവരോടു സാക്ഷ്യം പറയട്ടെ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also come to this place of torment.’
chapters.nkjv: for I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, lest they also come to this place of torment.’
chapters.kjv: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.

chapters.ml: അബ്രാഹാം അവനോടു: അവർക്കു മോശെയും പ്രവാചകന്മാരും ഉണ്ടല്ലോ; അവരുടെ വാക്കു അവർ കേൾക്കട്ടെ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: "Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to them.’
chapters.nkjv: Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.’
chapters.kjv: Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു അവൻ: അല്ലല്ല, അബ്രാഹാം പിതാവേ, മരിച്ചവരിൽനിന്നു ഒരുത്തൻ എഴുന്നേറ്റു അവരുടെ അടുക്കൽ ചെന്നു എങ്കിൽ അവർ മാനസാന്തരപ്പെടും എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: " ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent.’
chapters.nkjv: And he said, ‘No, father Abraham; but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
chapters.kjv: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.

chapters.ml: അവൻ അവനോടു: അവർ മോശെയുടെയും പ്രവാചകന്മാരുടെയും വാക്കു കേൾക്കാഞ്ഞാൽ മരിച്ചവരിൽ നിന്നു ഒരുത്തൻ എഴുന്നേറ്റു ചെന്നാലും വിശ്വസിക്കയില്ല എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: "He said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.’ "
chapters.nkjv: But he said to him, ‘If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded though one rise from the dead.’ "
chapters.kjv: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.

chapters.ml: അവൻ തന്റെ ശിഷ്യന്മാരോടു പറഞ്ഞതു: “ഇടർച്ചകൾ വരാതിരിക്കുന്നതു അസാദ്ധ്യം; എങ്കിലും അവ വരുത്തുന്നവന്നു അയ്യോ കഷ്ടം.
chapters.niv: Jesus said to his disciples: "Things that cause people to stumble are bound to come, but woe to anyone through whom they come.
chapters.nkjv: Then He said to the disciples, "It is impossible that no offenses should come, but woe to him through whom they do come!
chapters.kjv: Then said he unto the disciples, It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him , through whom they come!

chapters.ml: അവൻ ഈ ചെറിയവരിൽ ഒരുത്തന്നു ഇടർച്ച വരുത്തുന്നതിനെക്കാൾ ഒരു തിരിക്കല്ലു അവന്റെ കഴുത്തിൽ കെട്ടി അവനെ കടലിൽ എറിഞ്ഞുകളയുന്നതു അവന്നു നന്നു.
chapters.niv: It would be better for them to be thrown into the sea with a millstone tied around their neck than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
chapters.nkjv: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones.
chapters.kjv: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones.

chapters.ml: സൂക്ഷിച്ചുകൊൾവിൻ; സഹോദരൻ പിഴച്ചാൽ അവനെ ശാസിക്ക; അവൻ മാനസാന്തരപ്പെട്ടാൽ അവനോടു ക്ഷമിക്ക.
chapters.niv: So watch yourselves. "If your brother or sister sins against you, rebuke them; and if they repent, forgive them.
chapters.nkjv: Take heed to yourselves. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
chapters.kjv: Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.

chapters.ml: ദിവസത്തിൽ ഏഴുവട്ടം നിന്നോടു പിഴെക്കയും ഏഴുവട്ടവും നിന്റെ അടുക്കൽ വന്നു: ഞാൻ മാനസാന്തരപ്പെടുന്നു എന്നു പറകയും ചെയ്താൽ അവനോടു ക്ഷമിക്ക.
chapters.niv: Even if they sin against you seven times in a day and seven times come back to you saying ‘I repent,’ you must forgive them."
chapters.nkjv: And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day returns to you, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him."
chapters.kjv: And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.

chapters.ml: അപ്പൊസ്തലന്മാർ കർത്താവിനോടു: ഞങ്ങൾക്കു വിശ്വാസം വർദ്ധിപ്പിച്ചുതരേണമേ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: The apostles said to the Lord, "Increase our faith!"
chapters.nkjv: And the apostles said to the Lord, "Increase our faith."
chapters.kjv: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു കർത്താവു പറഞ്ഞതു: “നിങ്ങൾക്കു കടകുമണിയോളം വിശ്വാസം ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ ഈ കാട്ടത്തിയോടു: വേരോടെ പറിഞ്ഞു കടലിൽ നട്ടുപോക എന്നു പറഞ്ഞാൽ അതു നിങ്ങളെ അനുസരിക്കും.
chapters.niv: He replied, "If you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
chapters.nkjv: So the Lord said, "If you have faith as a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be pulled up by the roots and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
chapters.kjv: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you.

chapters.ml: നിങ്ങളിൽ ആർക്കെങ്കിലും ഉഴുകയോ മേയ്ക്കയോ ചെയ്യുന്ന ഒരു ദാസൻ ഉണ്ടെന്നിരിക്കട്ടെ. അവൻ വയലിൽനിന്നു വരുമ്പോൾ: നീ ക്ഷണത്തിൽ വന്നു ഊണിന്നു ഇരിക്ക എന്നു അവനോടു പറയുമോ? അല്ല:
chapters.niv: "Suppose one of you has a servant plowing or looking after the sheep. Will he say to the servant when he comes in from the field, ‘Come along now and sit down to eat’?
chapters.nkjv: And which of you, having a servant plowing or tending sheep, will say to him when he has come in from the field, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?
chapters.kjv: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat?

chapters.ml: എനിക്കു അത്താഴം ഒരുക്കുക; ഞാൻ തിന്നുകുടിച്ചു തീരുവോളം അരകെട്ടി എനിക്കു ശുശ്രൂഷചെയ്ക; പിന്നെ നീയും തിന്നു കുടിച്ചുകൊൾക എന്നു പറകയില്ലയോ?
chapters.niv: Won’t he rather say, ‘Prepare my supper, get yourself ready and wait on me while I eat and drink; after that you may eat and drink’?
chapters.nkjv: But will he not rather say to him, ‘Prepare something for my supper, and gird yourself and serve me till I have eaten and drunk, and afterward you will eat and drink’?
chapters.kjv: And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?

chapters.ml: തന്നോടു കല്പിച്ചതു ദാസൻ ചെയ്തതുകൊണ്ടു അവന്നു നന്ദിപറയുമോ?
chapters.niv: Will he thank the servant because he did what he was told to do?
chapters.nkjv: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I think not.
chapters.kjv: Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not.

chapters.ml: അവ്വണ്ണം നിങ്ങളോടു കല്പിച്ചതു ഒക്കെയും ചെയ്തശേഷം: ഞങ്ങൾ പ്രയോജനം ഇല്ലാത്ത ദാസന്മാർ; ചെയ്യേണ്ടതേ ചെയ്തിട്ടുള്ളു എന്നു നിങ്ങളും പറവിൻ.
chapters.niv: So you also, when you have done everything you were told to do, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’ "
chapters.nkjv: So likewise you, when you have done all those things which you are commanded, say, ‘We are unprofitable servants. We have done what was our duty to do.’ "
chapters.kjv: So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.

chapters.ml: അവൻ യെരൂശലേമിലേക്കു യാത്രചെയ്കയിൽ ശമര്യക്കും ഗലീലെക്കും നടുവിൽകൂടി കടക്കുമ്പോൾ
chapters.niv: Now on his way to Jerusalem, Jesus traveled along the border between Samaria and Galilee.
chapters.nkjv: Now it happened as He went to Jerusalem that He passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
chapters.kjv: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.

chapters.ml: ഒരു ഗ്രാമത്തിൽ ചെല്ലുന്നേരം കുഷ്ഠരോഗികളായ പത്തു പുരുഷന്മാർ അവന്നു എതിർപെട്ടു
chapters.niv: As he was going into a village, ten men who had leprosy met him. They stood at a distance
chapters.nkjv: Then as He entered a certain village, there met Him ten men who were lepers, who stood afar off.
