chapters.kjv: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.

chapters.ml: അവൻ അവരെ വന്ദനം ചെയ്തു തന്റെ ശുശ്രൂഷയാൽ ദൈവം ജാതികളുടെ ഇടയിൽ ചെയ്യിച്ചതു ഓരോന്നായി വിവരിച്ചു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Paul greeted them and reported in detail what God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
chapters.nkjv: When he had greeted them, he told in detail those things which God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
chapters.kjv: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.

chapters.ml: അവർ കേട്ടു ദൈവത്തെ മഹത്വപ്പെടുത്തി. പിന്നെ അവനോടു പറഞ്ഞതു: സഹോദരാ, യെഹൂദന്മാരുടെ ഇടയിൽ വിശ്വസിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നവർ എത്ര ആയിരം ഉണ്ടു എന്നു നീ കാണുന്നുവല്ലോ; അവർ എല്ലാവരും ന്യായപ്രമാണതല്പരന്മാർ ആകുന്നു.
chapters.niv: When they heard this, they praised God. Then they said to Paul: "You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.
chapters.nkjv: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord. And they said to him, "You see, brother, how many myriads of Jews there are who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law;
chapters.kjv: And when they heard it , they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:

chapters.ml: മക്കളെ പരിച്ഛേദന ചെയ്യരുതു എന്നും നമ്മുടെ മര്യാദ അനുസരിച്ചു നടക്കരുതു എന്നും നീ ജാതികളുടെ ഇടയിലുള്ള സകല യെഹൂദന്മാരോടും പറഞ്ഞു മോശെയെ ഉപേക്ഷിച്ചുകളവാൻ ഉപദേശിക്കുന്നു എന്നു അവർ നിന്നെക്കുറിച്ചു ധരിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: They have been informed that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to turn away from Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or live according to our customs.
chapters.nkjv: but they have been informed about you that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children nor to walk according to the customs.
chapters.kjv: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.

chapters.ml: ആകയാൽ എന്താകുന്നു വേണ്ടതു? നീ വന്നിട്ടുണ്ടു എന്നു അവർ കേൾക്കും നിശ്ചയം.
chapters.niv: What shall we do? They will certainly hear that you have come,
chapters.nkjv: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.
chapters.kjv: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.

chapters.ml: ഞങ്ങൾ നിന്നോടു ഈ പറയുന്നതു ചെയ്ക; നേർച്ചയുള്ള നാലു പുരുഷന്മാർ ഞങ്ങളുടെ ഇടയിൽ ഉണ്ടു.
chapters.niv: so do what we tell you. There are four men with us who have made a vow.
chapters.nkjv: Therefore do what we tell you: We have four men who have taken a vow.
chapters.kjv: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;

chapters.ml: അവരെ കൂട്ടിക്കൊണ്ടു അവരോടുകൂടെ നിന്നെ ശുദ്ധിവരുത്തി അവരുടെ തല ക്ഷൌരം ചെയ്യേണ്ടതിന്നു അവർക്കു വേണ്ടി ചെലവു ചെയ്ക; എന്നാൽ നിന്നെക്കൊണ്ടു കേട്ടതു ഉള്ളതല്ല എന്നും നീയും ന്യായപ്രമാണത്തെ ആചരിച്ചു ക്രമമായി നടക്കുന്നവൻ എന്നും എല്ലാവരും അറിയും.
chapters.niv: Take these men, join in their purification rites and pay their expenses, so that they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know there is no truth in these reports about you, but that you yourself are living in obedience to the law.
chapters.nkjv: Take them and be purified with them, and pay their expenses so that they may shave their heads, and that all may know that those things of which they were informed concerning you are nothing, but that you yourself also walk orderly and keep the law.
chapters.kjv: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.

chapters.ml: വിശ്വസിച്ചിരിക്കുന്ന ജാതികളെ സംബന്ധിച്ചോ അവർ വിഗ്രഹാർപ്പിതവും രക്തവും ശ്വാസംമുട്ടിച്ചത്തതും പരസംഗവും മാത്രം ഒഴിഞ്ഞിരിക്കേണം എന്നു വിധിച്ചു എഴുതി അയച്ചിട്ടുണ്ടല്ലോ.
chapters.niv: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they should abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals and from sexual immorality."
chapters.nkjv: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written and decided that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from things offered to idols, from blood, from things strangled, and from sexual immorality."
chapters.kjv: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ പൌലൊസ് ആ പുരുഷന്മാരെ കൂട്ടിക്കൊണ്ടു പിറ്റെന്നാൾ അവരോടുകൂടെ തന്നെ ശുദ്ധിവരുത്തി ദൈവാലയത്തിൽ ചെന്നു; അവരിൽ ഓരോരുത്തന്നുവേണ്ടി വഴിപാടു കഴിപ്പാനുള്ള ശുദ്ധീകരണകാലം തികഞ്ഞു എന്നു ബോധിപ്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: The next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he went to the temple to give notice of the date when the days of purification would end and the offering would be made for each of them.
chapters.nkjv: Then Paul took the men, and the next day, having been purified with them, entered the temple to announce the expiration of the days of purification, at which time an offering should be made for each one of them.
chapters.kjv: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.

chapters.ml: ആ ഏഴു ദിവസം തീരാറായപ്പോൾ ആസ്യയിൽ നിന്നു വന്ന യെഹൂദന്മാർ അവനെ ദൈവാലയത്തിൽ കണ്ടിട്ടു പുരുഷാരത്തെ ഒക്കെയും ഇളക്കി അവനെ പിടിച്ചു;
chapters.niv: When the seven days were nearly over, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,
chapters.nkjv: Now when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews from Asia, seeing him in the temple, stirred up the whole crowd and laid hands on him,
chapters.kjv: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,

chapters.ml: യിസ്രായേൽപുരുഷന്മാരേ, സഹായിപ്പിൻ ഇവൻ ആകുന്നു ജനത്തിന്നും ന്യായപ്രമാണത്തിന്നും ഈ സ്ഥലത്തിന്നും വിരോധമായി എല്ലായിടത്തും എല്ലാവരെയും ഉപദേശിക്കുന്നവൻ; അവൻ യവനന്മാരെയും ദൈവാലയത്തിൽ കൂട്ടിക്കൊണ്ടുവന്നു ഈ വിശുദ്ധ സ്ഥലം തീണ്ടിച്ചുകളഞ്ഞു എന്നു വിളിച്ചുകൂകി.
chapters.niv: shouting, "Fellow Israelites, help us! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people and our law and this place. And besides, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place."
chapters.nkjv: crying out, "Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, the law, and this place; and furthermore he also brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place."
chapters.kjv: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.

chapters.ml: അവർ മുമ്പെ എഫെസ്യനായ ത്രോഫിമോസിനെ അവനോടുകൂടെ നഗരത്തിൽ കണ്ടതിനാൽ പൌലൊസ് അവനെ ദൈവാലത്തിൽ കൂട്ടിക്കൊണ്ടുവന്നു എന്നു നിരൂപിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: (They had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with Paul and assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple.)
chapters.nkjv: (For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
chapters.kjv: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

chapters.ml: നഗരം എല്ലാം ഇളകി ജനം ഓടിക്കൂടി പൌലൊസിനെ പിടിച്ചു ദൈവാലയത്തിന്നു പുറത്തേക്കു ഇഴെച്ചു കൊണ്ടുപോയി; ഉടനെ വാതിലുകൾ അടെച്ചുകളഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: The whole city was aroused, and the people came running from all directions. Seizing Paul, they dragged him from the temple, and immediately the gates were shut.
chapters.nkjv: And all the city was disturbed; and the people ran together, seized Paul, and dragged him out of the temple; and immediately the doors were shut.
chapters.kjv: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.

chapters.ml: അവർ അവനെ കൊല്ലുവാൻ ശ്രമിക്കുമ്പോൾ യെരൂശലേം ഒക്കെയും കലക്കത്തിൽ ആയി എന്നു പട്ടാളത്തിന്റെ സഹസ്രാധിപന്നു വർത്തമാനം എത്തി.
chapters.niv: While they were trying to kill him, news reached the commander of the Roman troops that the whole city of Jerusalem was in an uproar.
chapters.nkjv: Now as they were seeking to kill him, news came to the commander of the garrison that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
chapters.kjv: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

chapters.ml: അവൻ ക്ഷണത്തിൽ പടയാളികളെയും ശതാധിപന്മാരെയും കൂട്ടിക്കൊണ്ടു അവരുടെ നേരെ പാഞ്ഞുവന്നു; അവർ സഹസ്രാധിപനെയും പടയാളികളെയും കണ്ടപ്പോൾ പൌലൊസിനെ അടിക്കുന്നതു നിറുത്തി.
chapters.niv: He at once took some officers and soldiers and ran down to the crowd. When the rioters saw the commander and his soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
chapters.nkjv: He immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down to them. And when they saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
chapters.kjv: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.

chapters.ml: സഹസ്രാധിപൻ അടത്തുവന്നു അവനെ പിടിച്ചു രണ്ടു ചങ്ങലവെപ്പാൻ കല്പിച്ചു; ആർ എന്നും എന്തു ചെയ്തു എന്നും ചോദിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: The commander came up and arrested him and ordered him to be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.
chapters.nkjv: Then the commander came near and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and he asked who he was and what he had done.
chapters.kjv: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.

chapters.ml: പുരുഷാരത്തിൽ ചിലർ ഇങ്ങനെയും ചിലർ അങ്ങനെയും നിലവിളിച്ചുകൊണ്ടിരുന്നു; ആരവാരം ഹേതുവായി നിശ്ചയം ഒന്നും അറിഞ്ഞുകൂടായ്കയാൽ അവനെ കോട്ടയിലേക്കു കൊണ്ടുപോകുവാൻ കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Some in the crowd shouted one thing and some another, and since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be taken into the barracks.
chapters.nkjv: And some among the multitude cried one thing and some another. So when he could not ascertain the truth because of the tumult, he commanded him to be taken into the barracks.
chapters.kjv: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.

chapters.ml: പടിക്കെട്ടിന്മേൽആയപ്പോൾ: അവനെ കൊന്നുകളക എന്നു ആർത്തുകൊണ്ടു ജനസമൂഹം പിൻചെല്ലുകയാൽ
chapters.niv: When Paul reached the steps, the violence of the mob was so great he had to be carried by the soldiers.
chapters.nkjv: When he reached the stairs, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob.
chapters.kjv: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.

chapters.ml: പുരുഷാരത്തിന്റെ ബലാൽക്കാരം പേടിച്ചിട്ടു പടയാളികൾ അവനെ എടുക്കേണ്ടിവന്നു.
chapters.niv: The crowd that followed kept shouting, "Get rid of him!"
chapters.nkjv: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, "Away with him!"
chapters.kjv: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.

chapters.ml: കോട്ടയിൽ കടക്കുമാറായപ്പോൾ പൌലൊസ് സഹസ്രാധിപനോടു: എനിക്കു നിന്നോടു ഒരു വാക്കു പറയാമോ എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു. അതിന്നു അവൻ: നിനക്കു യവനഭാഷ അറിയാമോ?
chapters.niv: As the soldiers were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, "May I say something to you?" "Do you speak Greek?" he replied.
chapters.nkjv: Then as Paul was about to be led into the barracks, he said to the commander, "May I speak to you?" He replied, "Can you speak Greek?
chapters.kjv: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?

chapters.ml: കുറെ നാൾ മുമ്പെ കലഹം ഉണ്ടാക്കി നാലായിരം കട്ടാരക്കാരെ മരുഭൂമിയിലേക്കു കൂട്ടിക്കൊണ്ടുപോയ മിസ്രയീമ്യൻ നീ അല്ലയോ എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: "Aren’t you the Egyptian who started a revolt and led four thousand terrorists out into the wilderness some time ago?"
chapters.nkjv: Are you not the Egyptian who some time ago stirred up a rebellion and led the four thousand assassins out into the wilderness?"
chapters.kjv: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു പൌലൊസ്: ഞാൻ കിലിക്യയിൽ തർസൊസ് എന്ന പ്രസിദ്ധനഗരത്തിലെ പൌരനായോരു യെഹൂദൻ ആകുന്നു. ജനത്തോടു സംസാരിപ്പാൻ അനുവദിക്കേണം എന്നു അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Paul answered, "I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Please let me speak to the people."
chapters.nkjv: But Paul said, "I am a Jew from Tarsus, in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city; and I implore you, permit me to speak to the people."
chapters.kjv: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.

chapters.ml: അവൻ അനുവദിച്ചപ്പോൾ പൌലൊസ് പടിക്കെട്ടിന്മേൽ നിന്നുകൊണ്ടു ജനത്തോടു ആംഗ്യം കാട്ടി, വളരെ മൌനമായ ശേഷം എബ്രായഭാഷയിൽ വിളിച്ചുപറഞ്ഞതാവിതു:
chapters.niv: After receiving the commander’s permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. When they were all silent, he said to them in Aramaic :
chapters.nkjv: So when he had given him permission, Paul stood on the stairs and motioned with his hand to the people. And when there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,
chapters.kjv: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,

chapters.ml: സഹോദരന്മാരും പിതാക്കന്മാരുമായുള്ളോരേ, എനിക്കു ഇന്നു നിങ്ങളോടുള്ള പ്രതിവാദം കേട്ടുകൊൾവിൻ.
chapters.niv: "Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense."
chapters.nkjv: "Brethren and fathers, hear my defense before you now."
chapters.kjv: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ എബ്രായഭാഷയിൽ സംസാരിക്കുന്നതു കേട്ടിട്ടു അവർ അധികം മൌനമായി നിന്നു. അവൻ പറഞ്ഞതെന്തെന്നാൽ:
chapters.niv: When they heard him speak to them in Aramaic, they became very quiet. Then Paul said:
chapters.nkjv: And when they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they kept all the more silent. Then he said:
chapters.kjv: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ കിലിക്യയിലെ തർസൊസിൽ ജനിച്ച യെഹൂദനും ഈ നഗരത്തിൽ വളർന്നു ഗമാലിയേലിന്റെ കാൽക്കൽ ഇരുന്നു പിതാക്കനാരുടെ ന്യായപ്രമാണം സൂക്ഷ്മതയോടെ അഭ്യസിച്ചവനുമാകയാൽ നിങ്ങൾ എല്ലാവരും ഇന്നു ഇരിക്കുന്നതുപോലെ ദൈവസേവയിൽ എരിവുള്ളവനായിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city. I studied under Gamaliel and was thoroughly trained in the law of our ancestors. I was just as zealous for God as any of you are today.
chapters.nkjv: "I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, taught according to the strictness of our fathers’ law, and was zealous toward God as you all are today.
chapters.kjv: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ പുരുഷന്മാരെയും സ്ത്രീകളെയും പിടിച്ചു കെട്ടി തടവിൽ ഏല്പിച്ചും ഈ മാർഗ്ഗക്കാരെ കൊല്ലുവാനും മടിക്കാതെ ഉപദ്രവിച്ചുംവന്നു.
chapters.niv: I persecuted the followers of this Way to their death, arresting both men and women and throwing them into prison,
chapters.nkjv: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women,
chapters.kjv: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു മഹാപുരോഹിതനും മൂപ്പന്മാരുടെ സംഘം ഒക്കെയും എനിക്കു സാക്ഷികൾ; അവരോടു സഹോദരന്മാർക്കായി എഴുത്തു വാങ്ങിക്കൊണ്ടു ദമസ്കൊസിൽ പാർക്കുന്നവരെയും പിടിച്ചുകെട്ടി ദണ്ഡനത്തിന്നായി യെരൂശലേമിലേക്കു കൊണ്ടുവരേണ്ടതിന്നു ഞാൻ അവിടേക്കു യാത്രയായി.
chapters.niv: as the high priest and all the Council can themselves testify. I even obtained letters from them to their associates in Damascus, and went there to bring these people as prisoners to Jerusalem to be punished.
chapters.nkjv: as also the high priest bears me witness, and all the council of the elders, from whom I also received letters to the brethren, and went to Damascus to bring in chains even those who were there to Jerusalem to be punished.
chapters.kjv: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ പ്രയാണം ചെയ്തു ദമസ്കൊസിനോടു അടുത്തപ്പോൾ ഏകദേശം ഉച്ചെക്കു പെട്ടെന്നു ആകശത്തുനിന്നു വലിയോരു വെളിച്ചം എന്റെ ചുറ്റും മിന്നി.
chapters.niv: "About noon as I came near Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.
chapters.nkjv: "Now it happened, as I journeyed and came near Damascus at about noon, suddenly a great light from heaven shone around me.
chapters.kjv: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ നിലത്തു വീണു: ശൌലേ, ശൌലെ, നീ എന്നെ ഉപദ്രവിക്കുന്നതു എന്തു എന്നു എന്നോടു പറയുന്ന ഒരു ശബ്ദം കേട്ടു.
chapters.niv: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul! Saul! Why do you persecute me?’
chapters.nkjv: And I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?’
chapters.kjv: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

chapters.ml: കർത്താവേ, നീ ആർ എന്നു ഞാൻ ചോദിച്ചതിന്നു: നീ ഉപദ്രവിക്കുന്ന നസറായനായ യേശു ആകുന്നു ഞാൻ എന്നു അവൻ എന്നോടു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: " ‘Who are you, Lord?’ I asked. " ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,’ he replied.
chapters.nkjv: So I answered, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And He said to me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting.’
chapters.kjv: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.

chapters.ml: എന്നോടു കൂടെയുള്ളവർ വെളിച്ചം കണ്ടു എങ്കിലും എന്നോടു സംസാരിക്കുന്നവന്റെ ശബ്ദം കേട്ടില്ല.
chapters.niv: My companions saw the light, but they did not understand the voice of him who was speaking to me.
chapters.nkjv: "And those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they did not hear the voice of Him who spoke to me.
chapters.kjv: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.

chapters.ml: കർത്താവേ ഞാൻ എന്തു ചെയ്യേണം എന്നു ചോദിച്ചുതിന്നു കർത്താവു എന്നോടു; എഴുന്നേറ്റു ദമസ്കൊസിലേക്കു പോക; നീ ചെയ്യേണ്ടതിന്നു വിധിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നതെല്ലാം അവിടെ നിന്നോടു പറയും എന്നു കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: " ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ I asked. " ‘Get up,’ the Lord said, ‘and go into Damascus. There you will be told all that you have been assigned to do.’
chapters.nkjv: So I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ And the Lord said to me, ‘Arise and go into Damascus, and there you will be told all things which are appointed for you to do.’
chapters.kjv: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.

chapters.ml: ആ വെളിച്ചത്തിന്റെ തേജസ്സു ഹേതുവായിട്ടു കണ്ണു കാണായ്കയാൽ കൂടെയുള്ളവർ എന്നെ കൈക്കു പിടിച്ചു നടത്തി; അങ്ങനെ ഞാൻ ദമസ്കൊസിൽ എത്തി.
chapters.niv: My companions led me by the hand into Damascus, because the brilliance of the light had blinded me.
chapters.nkjv: And since I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.
chapters.kjv: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.

chapters.ml: അവിടെ പാർക്കുന്ന സകല യെഹൂദന്മാരാലും നല്ല സാക്ഷ്യം കൊണ്ടവനായി ന്യായപ്രമാണപ്രകാരം ഭക്തിയുള്ള പുരുഷനായ അനന്യാസ് എന്നൊരുത്തൻ എന്റെ അടുക്കൽ വന്നുനിന്നു;
chapters.niv: "A man named Ananias came to see me. He was a devout observer of the law and highly respected by all the Jews living there.
chapters.nkjv: "Then a certain Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good testimony with all the Jews who dwelt there,
chapters.kjv: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there ,

chapters.ml: സഹോദരനായ ശൌലെ, കാഴ്ചപ്രാപിക്ക എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു; ആ നാഴികയിൽ തന്നേ ഞാൻ കാഴ്ച പ്രാപിച്ചു അവനെ കണ്ടു.
chapters.niv: He stood beside me and said, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ And at that very moment I was able to see him.
chapters.nkjv: came to me; and he stood and said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight.’ And at that same hour I looked up at him.
chapters.kjv: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ അവൻ എന്നോടു: നമ്മുടെ പിതാക്കന്മാരുടെ ദൈവം നിന്നെ തന്റെ ഇഷ്ടം അറിവാനും നീതിമാനായവനെ കാണ്മാനും അവന്റെ വായിൽ നിന്നും വചനം കേൾപ്പാനും നിയമിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "Then he said: ‘The God of our ancestors has chosen you to know his will and to see the Righteous One and to hear words from his mouth.
chapters.nkjv: Then he said, ‘The God of our fathers has chosen you that you should know His will, and see the Just One, and hear the voice of His mouth.
chapters.kjv: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.

chapters.ml: നീ കാണ്കയും കേൾക്കയും ചെയ്തതിന്നു സകലമനുഷ്യർക്കും നീ അവന്റെ സാക്ഷിയായിത്തീരും.
chapters.niv: You will be his witness to all people of what you have seen and heard.
chapters.nkjv: For you will be His witness to all men of what you have seen and heard.
chapters.kjv: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.

chapters.ml: ഇനി താമസിക്കുന്നതു എന്തു? എഴുന്നേറ്റു അവന്റെ നാം വിളിച്ചു പ്രാർത്ഥിച്ചു സ്നാനം ഏറ്റു നിന്റെ പാപങ്ങളെ കഴുകിക്കളക എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized and wash your sins away, calling on his name.’
chapters.nkjv: And now why are you waiting? Arise and be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.’
chapters.kjv: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ ഞാൻ യെരൂശലേമിൽ മടങ്ങിച്ചെന്നു ദൈവാലയത്തിൽ പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കുന്നേരം ഒരു വിവശതയിൽ ആയി അവനെ കണ്ടു:
chapters.niv: "When I returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance
chapters.nkjv: "Now it happened, when I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, that I was in a trance
chapters.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;

chapters.ml: നീ ബദ്ധപ്പെട്ടു വേഗം യെരൂശലേം വിട്ടുപോക; നീ എന്നെക്കുറിച്ചു പറയുന്ന സാക്ഷ്യം അവർ കൈക്കൊൾകയില്ല എന്നു എന്നോടു കല്പിച്ചു
chapters.niv: and saw the Lord speaking to me. ‘Quick!’ he said. ‘Leave Jerusalem immediately, because the people here will not accept your testimony about me.’
chapters.nkjv: and saw Him saying to me, ‘Make haste and get out of Jerusalem quickly, for they will not receive your testimony concerning Me.’
chapters.kjv: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു ഞാൻ: കർത്താവേ, നിന്നിൽ വിശ്വസിക്കുന്നവരെ ഞാൻ തടവിൽ ആക്കുകയും പള്ളിതോറും അടിപ്പിക്കയും ചെയ്തു എന്നും
chapters.niv: " ‘Lord,’ I replied, ‘these people know that I went from one synagogue to another to imprison and beat those who believe in you.
chapters.nkjv: So I said, ‘Lord, they know that in every synagogue I imprisoned and beat those who believe on You.
chapters.kjv: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:

chapters.ml: നിന്റെ സാക്ഷിയായ സ്തെഫാനൊസിന്റെ രക്തം ചൊരിഞ്ഞപ്പോൾ ഞാനും സമ്മതിച്ചു അരികെ നിന്നു അവനെ കൊല്ലുന്നവരുടെ വസ്ത്രം കാത്തുകൊണ്ടിരുന്നു എന്നും അവർ അറിയുന്നുവല്ലോ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: And when the blood of your martyr Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and guarding the clothes of those who were killing him.’
chapters.nkjv: And when the blood of Your martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by consenting to his death, and guarding the clothes of those who were killing him.’
chapters.kjv: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.

chapters.ml: അവൻ എന്നോടു: നീ പോക; ഞാൻ നിന്നെ ദൂരത്തു ജാതികളുടെ അടുക്കലേക്കു അയക്കും എന്നു കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: "Then the Lord said to me, ‘Go; I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’ "
chapters.nkjv: Then He said to me, ‘Depart, for I will send you far from here to the Gentiles.’ "
chapters.kjv: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.

chapters.ml: ഈ വാക്കോളം അവർ അവന്നു ചെവികൊടുത്തു; പിന്നെ: ഇങ്ങനെത്തവനെ ഭൂമിയിൽനിന്നു നീക്കിക്കളക; അവൻ ജീവിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നതു യോഗ്യമല്ല എന്നു നിലവിളിച്ചു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: The crowd listened to Paul until he said this. Then they raised their voices and shouted, "Rid the earth of him! He’s not fit to live!"
chapters.nkjv: And they listened to him until this word, and then they raised their voices and said, "Away with such a fellow from the earth, for he is not fit to live!"
chapters.kjv: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.

chapters.ml: അവർ കൂക്കലിട്ടും വസ്ത്രം കീറിക്കളഞ്ഞും പൂഴി വാരി മേലോട്ടു എറിഞ്ഞും കൊണ്ടിരിക്കുമ്പോൾ
chapters.niv: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and flinging dust into the air,
chapters.nkjv: Then, as they cried out and tore off their clothes and threw dust into the air,
chapters.kjv: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,

chapters.ml: അവർ ഇങ്ങനെ അവന്റെ നേരെ ആർക്കുവാൻ സംഗതി എന്തു എന്നു അറിയേണ്ടതിന്നു ചമ്മട്ടികൊണ്ടു അവനോടു ചോദ്യം ചെയ്യേണം എന്നു സഹസ്രാധിപൻ പറഞ്ഞു അവനെ കോട്ടയിലേക്കു കൊണ്ടുപോകുവാൻ കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: the commander ordered that Paul be taken into the barracks. He directed that he be flogged and interrogated in order to find out why the people were shouting at him like this.
chapters.nkjv: the commander ordered him to be brought into the barracks, and said that he should be examined under scourging, so that he might know why they shouted so against him.
chapters.kjv: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.

chapters.ml: തന്നെ വാറു കൊണ്ടു കെട്ടുമ്പോൾ പൌലൊസ് അരികെ നില്ക്കുന്ന ശതാധിപനോടു: റോമപൌരനും വിസ്താരം കഴിയാത്തവനുമായ മനുഷ്യനെ ചമ്മട്ടി കൊണ്ടു അടിക്കുന്നതു വിഹിതമോ എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: As they stretched him out to flog him, Paul said to the centurion standing there, "Is it legal for you to flog a Roman citizen who hasn’t even been found guilty?"
chapters.nkjv: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said to the centurion who stood by, "Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and uncondemned?"
chapters.kjv: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?

chapters.ml: ഇതു കേട്ടിട്ടു ശതാധിപൻ ചെന്നു സഹസ്രാധിപനോടു: നീ എന്തു ചെയ്‍വാൻ പോകുന്നു? ഈ മനുഷ്യൻ റോമപൌരൻ ആകുന്നു എന്നു ബോധിപ്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and reported it. "What are you going to do?" he asked. "This man is a Roman citizen."
chapters.nkjv: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the commander, saying, "Take care what you do, for this man is a Roman."
chapters.kjv: When the centurion heard that , he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.

chapters.ml: സഹസ്രാധിപൻ വന്നു: നീ റോമപൌരൻ തന്നേയോ? എന്നോടു പറക എന്നു ചോദിച്ചതിന്നു:
chapters.niv: The commander went to Paul and asked, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" "Yes, I am," he answered.
chapters.nkjv: Then the commander came and said to him, "Tell me, are you a Roman?" He said, "Yes."
chapters.kjv: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.

chapters.ml: അതെ എന്നു അവൻ പറഞ്ഞു. ഞാൻ ഏറിയ മുതൽ കൊടുത്തു ഈ പൌരത്വം സമ്പാദിച്ചു എന്നു സഹസ്രാധിപൻ പറഞ്ഞതിന്നു: ഞാനോ അങ്ങനെ ജനിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പൌലൊസ് പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Then the commander said, "I had to pay a lot of money for my citizenship." "But I was born a citizen," Paul replied.
chapters.nkjv: The commander answered, "With a large sum I obtained this citizenship." And Paul said, "But I was born acitizen."
chapters.kjv: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.

chapters.ml: ഭേദ്യം ചെയ്‍വാൻ ഭാവിച്ചവർ ഉടനെ അവനെ വിട്ടുമാറി; സഹസ്രാധിപനും അവൻ റോമപൌരൻ എന്നു അറിഞ്ഞപ്പോൾ അവനെ ബന്ധിച്ചതുകൊണ്ടു ഭയപ്പെട്ടു.
chapters.niv: Those who were about to interrogate him withdrew immediately. The commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put Paul, a Roman citizen, in chains.
chapters.nkjv: Then immediately those who were about to examine him withdrew from him; and the commander was also afraid after he found out that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
chapters.kjv: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.

chapters.ml: ﻿പിറ്റെന്നു യെഹൂദന്മാർ പൌലൊസിന്മേൽ ചുമത്തുന്ന കുറ്റത്തിന്റെ സൂക്ഷ്മം അറിവാൻ ഇച്ഛിച്ചിട്ടു അവൻ മഹാപുരോഹിതന്മാരും ന്യായാധിപസംഘം ഒക്കെയും കൂടി വരുവാൻ കല്പിച്ചു അവനെ കെട്ടഴിച്ചു താഴെ കൊണ്ടുചെന്നു അവരുടെ മുമ്പിൽ നിറുത്തി.
chapters.niv: The commander wanted to find out exactly why Paul was being accused by the Jews. So the next day he released him and ordered the chief priests and all the members of the Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul and had him stand before them.
chapters.nkjv: The next day, because he wanted to know for certain why he was accused by the Jews, he released him from his bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down and set him before them.
chapters.kjv: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.

chapters.ml: പൌലൊസ് ന്യായാധിപസംഘത്തെ ഉറ്റുനോക്കി: സഹോദരന്മാരേ, ഞാൻ ഇന്നേ ദിവസത്തോളവും കേവലം നല്ല മനസ്സാക്ഷിയോടുംകൂടെ ദൈവത്തിന്റെ മുമ്പാകെ നടന്നിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Paul looked straight at the Sanhedrin and said, "My brothers, I have fulfilled my duty to God in all good conscience to this day."
chapters.nkjv: Then Paul, looking earnestly at the council, said, "Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day."
chapters.kjv: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ മഹാപുരോഹിതനായ അനന്യാസ് അരികെ നില്ക്കുന്നവരോടു അവന്റെ വായിക്കു അടിപ്പാൻ കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: At this the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.
chapters.nkjv: And the high priest Ananias commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.
chapters.kjv: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.

chapters.ml: പൌലൊസ് അവനോടു: ദൈവം നിന്നെ അടിക്കും വെള്ള തേച്ച ചുവരേ; നീ ന്യായപ്രമാണപ്രകാരം എന്നെ വിസ്തരിപ്പാൻ ഇരിക്കയും ന്യായപ്രമാണത്തിന്നു വിരോധമായി എന്നെ അടിപ്പാൻ കല്പിക്കയും ചെയ്യുന്നുവോ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Then Paul said to him, "God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit there to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck!"
chapters.nkjv: Then Paul said to him, "God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! For you sit to judge me according to the law, and do you command me to be struck contrary to the law?"
chapters.kjv: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?

chapters.ml: അരികെ നില്ക്കുന്നവർ: നീ ദൈവത്തിന്റെ മഹാപുരോഹിതനെ ശകാരിക്കുന്നുവോ എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Those who were standing near Paul said, "How dare you insult God’s high priest!"
chapters.nkjv: And those who stood by said, "Do you revile God’s high priest?"
chapters.kjv: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു പെലൊസ്: സഹോദരന്മാരേ, മഹാപുരോഹിതൻ എന്നു ഞാൻ അറിഞ്ഞില്ല; “നിന്റെ ജനത്തിന്റെ അധിപതിയെ ദുഷിക്കരുതു എന്നു എഴുതിയിരിക്കുന്നുവല്ലോ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Paul replied, "Brothers, I did not realize that he was the high priest; for it is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’ "
chapters.nkjv: Then Paul said, "I did not know, brethren, that he was the high priest; for it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’ "
chapters.kjv: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ ന്യായാധിപസംഘത്തിൽ ഒരു പക്ഷം സദൂക്യരും ഒരുപക്ഷം പരീശന്മാരും ആകുന്നു എന്നു പൌലൊസ് അറിഞ്ഞു: സഹോദരന്മാരേ, ഞാൻ ഒരു പരീശനും പരീശന്മാരുടെ മകനും ആകുന്നു; മരിച്ചവരുടെ പ്രത്യാശയെയും പുനരുത്ഥാനത്തെയും കുറിച്ചു ഞാൻ വിസ്താരത്തിലായിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു വിളിച്ചു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and the others Pharisees, called out in the Sanhedrin, "My brothers, I am a Pharisee, descended from Pharisees. I stand on trial because of the hope of the resurrection of the dead."
chapters.nkjv: But when Paul perceived that one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, "Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee; concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!"
chapters.kjv: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

chapters.ml: അവൻ ഇതു പറഞ്ഞപ്പോൾ പരീശന്മാരും സദൂക്യരും തമ്മിൽ ഇടഞ്ഞു സംഘം ഛിദ്രിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When he said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.
chapters.nkjv: And when he had said this, a dissension arose between the Pharisees and the Sadducees; and the assembly was divided.
chapters.kjv: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.

chapters.ml: പുനരുത്ഥാനം ഇല്ല ദൂതനും ആത്മാവും ഇല്ല എന്നു സദൂക്യർ പറയുന്നു; പരീശന്മാരോ രണ്ടും ഉണ്ടെന്നു പ്രമാണിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: (The Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, and that there are neither angels nor spirits, but the Pharisees believe all these things.)
chapters.nkjv: For Sadducees say that there is no resurrection—and no angel or spirit; but the Pharisees confess both.
chapters.kjv: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ വലിയോരു നിലവിളി ഉണ്ടായി; പരീശപക്ഷത്തിലെ ശാസ്ത്രിമാരിൽ ചിലർ എഴുന്നേറ്റു വാദിച്ചു: ഈ മനുഷ്യനിൽ ഞങ്ങൾ ഒരു കുറ്റവും കാണുന്നില്ല; ഒരാത്മാവോ ഒരു ദൂതനോ അവനോടു സംസാരിച്ചു എന്നു വന്നേക്കാം എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: There was a great uproar, and some of the teachers of the law who were Pharisees stood up and argued vigorously. "We find nothing wrong with this man," they said. "What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?"
chapters.nkjv: Then there arose a loud outcry. And the scribes of the Pharisees’ party arose and protested, saying, "We find no evil in this man; but if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against God."
chapters.kjv: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ വലിയ ഇടച്ചൽ ആയതുകൊണ്ടു അവർ പൌലൊസിനെ ചീന്തിക്കളയും എന്നു സഹസ്രാധിപൻ പേടിച്ചു, പടയാളികൾ ഇറങ്ങിവന്നു അവനെ അവരുടെ നടുവിൽ നിന്നു പിടിച്ചെടുത്തു കോട്ടയിൽ കൊണ്ടുപോകുവാൻ കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: The dispute became so violent that the commander was afraid Paul would be torn to pieces by them. He ordered the troops to go down and take him away from them by force and bring him into the barracks.
chapters.nkjv: Now when there arose a great dissension, the commander, fearing lest Paul might be pulled to pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the barracks.
chapters.kjv: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.

chapters.ml: രാത്രിയിൽ കർത്താവു അവന്റെ അടുക്കൽ നിന്നു: ധൈര്യമായിരിക്ക; നീ എന്നെക്കുറിച്ചു യെരൂശലേമിൽ സാക്ഷീകരിച്ചതുപോലെ റോമയിലും സാക്ഷീകരിക്കേണ്ടതാകുന്നു എന്നു അരുളിച്ചെയ്തു.
chapters.niv: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, "Take courage! As you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so you must also testify in Rome."
chapters.nkjv: But the following night the Lord stood by him and said, "Be of good cheer, Paul; for as you have testified for Me in Jerusalem, so you must also bear witness at Rome."
chapters.kjv: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.

chapters.ml: നേരം വെളുത്തപ്പോൾ ചില യെഹൂദന്മാർ തമ്മിൽ യോജിച്ചു പൌലൊസിനെ കൊന്നുകളയുവോളം ഒന്നും തിന്നുകയോ കുടിക്കയോ ചെയ്കയില്ല എന്നു ശപഥം ചെയ്തു.
chapters.niv: The next morning some Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
chapters.nkjv: And when it was day, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under an oath, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
chapters.kjv: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

chapters.ml: ഈ ശപഥം ചെയ്തവർ നാല്പതിൽ അധികംപേർ ആയിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: More than forty men were involved in this plot.
chapters.nkjv: Now there were more than forty who had formed this conspiracy.
chapters.kjv: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.

chapters.ml: അവർ മഹാപുരോഹിതന്മാരുടെയും മൂപ്പന്മാരുടെയും അടുക്കൽ ചെന്നു: ഞങ്ങൾ പൌലൊസിനെ കൊന്നുകളയുവോളം ഒന്നും ആസ്വദിക്കയില്ല എന്നൊരു കഠിനശപഥം ചെയ്തിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: They went to the chief priests and the elders and said, "We have taken a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.
chapters.nkjv: They came to the chief priests and elders, and said, "We have bound ourselves under a great oath that we will eat nothing until we have killed Paul.
chapters.kjv: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.

chapters.ml: ആകയാൽ നിങ്ങൾ അവന്റെ കാര്യം അധികം സൂക്ഷമത്തോടെ പരിശോധിക്കേണം എന്നുള്ള ഭാവത്തിൽ അവനെ നിങ്ങളുടെ അടുക്കൽ താഴെ കൊണ്ടുവരുവാൻ ന്യായാധിപസംഘവുമായി സഹസ്രാധിപനോടു അപേക്ഷിപ്പിൻ; എന്നാൽ അവൻ സമീപിക്കും മുമ്പെ ഞങ്ങൾ അവനെ ഒടുക്കിക്കളവാൻ ഒരുങ്ങിയിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him before you on the pretext of wanting more accurate information about his case. We are ready to kill him before he gets here."
chapters.nkjv: Now you, therefore, together with the council, suggest to the commander that he be brought down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to make further inquiries concerning him; but we are ready to kill him before he comes near."
chapters.kjv: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.

chapters.ml: ഈ പതിയിരിപ്പിനെക്കുറിച്ചു പൌലൊസിന്റെ പെങ്ങളുടെ മകൻ കേട്ടിട്ടു ചെന്നു കോട്ടയിൽ കടന്നു പൌലൊസിനോടു അറിയിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard of this plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.
chapters.nkjv: So when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their ambush, he went and entered the barracks and told Paul.
chapters.kjv: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

chapters.ml: പൌലൊസ് ശതാധിപന്മാരിൽ ഒരുത്തനെ വിളിച്ചു: ഈ യൌവനക്കാരന്നു സഹസ്രാധിപനോടു ഒരു കാര്യം അറിയിപ്പാനുള്ളതിനാൽ അവനെ അങ്ങോട്ടു കൊണ്ടു പോകേണം എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, "Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him."
chapters.nkjv: Then Paul called one of the centurions to him and said, "Take this young man to the commander, for he has something to tell him."
chapters.kjv: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him , and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.

chapters.ml: അവൻ അവനെ കൂട്ടി സഹസ്രാധിപന്റെ അടുക്കൽ കൊണ്ടുചെന്നു: തടവുകാരനായ പൌലൊസ് എന്നെ വിളിച്ചു, നിന്നോടു ഒരു കാര്യം പറവാനുള്ള ഈ യൌവനക്കാരനെ നിന്റെ അടുക്കൽ കൊണ്ടുവരുവാൻ എന്നോടു അപേക്ഷിച്ചു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: So he took him to the commander. The centurion said, "Paul, the prisoner, sent for me and asked me to bring this young man to you because he has something to tell you."
chapters.nkjv: So he took him and brought him to the commander and said, "Paul the prisoner called me to him and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to say to you."
chapters.kjv: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him , and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.

chapters.ml: സഹസ്രാധിപൻ അവനെ കൈക്കു പിടിച്ചു മാറിനിന്നു: എന്നോടു ബോധിപ്പിപ്പാനുള്ളതു എന്തു എന്നു സ്വകാര്യമായി ചോദിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside and asked, "What is it you want to tell me?"
chapters.nkjv: Then the commander took him by the hand, went aside, and asked privately, "What is it that you have to tell me?"
chapters.kjv: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him , What is that thou hast to tell me?

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു അവൻ: യെഹൂദന്മാർ പൌലൊസിനെക്കുറിച്ചു അധികം സൂക്ഷമത്തോടെ വിസ്താരം കഴിക്കേണമെന്നുള്ള ഭാവത്തിൽ വന്നു നാളെ അവനെ ന്യായാധിപസംഘത്തിലേക്കു കൊണ്ടുവരേണ്ടതിന്നു നിന്നോടു അപേക്ഷിപ്പാൻ ഒത്തു കൂടിയിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: He said: "Some Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul before the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of wanting more accurate information about him.
chapters.nkjv: And he said, "The Jews have agreed to ask that you bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though they were going to inquire more fully about him.
chapters.kjv: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

chapters.ml: നീ അവരെ വിശ്വസിച്ചു പോകരുതു; അവരിൽ നാല്പതിൽ അധികം പേർ അവനെ ഒടുക്കിക്കളയുവോളം ഒന്നും തിന്നുകയോ കുടിക്കയോ ചെയ്കയില്ല എന്നു ശപഥംചെയ്തു അവന്നായി പതിയിരിക്കുന്നു; നിന്റെ വാഗ്ദത്തം കിട്ടും എന്നു ആശിച്ചു അവർ ഇപ്പോൾ ഒരുങ്ങി നില്ക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Don’t give in to them, because more than forty of them are waiting in ambush for him. They have taken an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him. They are ready now, waiting for your consent to their request."
chapters.nkjv: But do not yield to them, for more than forty of them lie in wait for him, men who have bound themselves by an oath that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him; and now they are ready, waiting for the promise from you."
chapters.kjv: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.

chapters.ml: നീ ഇതു എന്നോടു അറിയിച്ചു എന്നു ആരോടും മിണ്ടരുതു എന്നു സഹസ്രാധിപൻ കല്പിച്ചു യൌവനക്കാരനെ പറഞ്ഞയച്ചു.
chapters.niv: The commander dismissed the young man with this warning: "Don’t tell anyone that you have reported this to me."
chapters.nkjv: So the commander let the young man depart, and commanded him, "Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me."
chapters.kjv: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ അവൻ ശതാധിപന്മാരിൽ രണ്ടുപേരെ വരുത്തി: ഈ രാത്രിയിൽ മൂന്നാം മണിനേരത്തു കൈസര്യക്കു പോകുവാൻ ഇരുനൂറു കാലാളെയും എഴുപതു കുതിരച്ചേവകരെയും ഇരുനൂറു കുന്തക്കാരെയും ഒരുക്കുവിൻ.
chapters.niv: Then he called two of his centurions and ordered them, "Get ready a detachment of two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea at nine tonight.
chapters.nkjv: And he called for two centurions, saying, "Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea at the third hour of the night;
chapters.kjv: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Cæsarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;

chapters.ml: പൌലൊസിനെ കയറ്റി ദേശാധിപതിയായ ഫേലിക്സിന്റെ അടുക്കൽ ക്ഷേമത്തോട എത്തിപ്പാൻ മൃഗവാഹനങ്ങളെയും സംഭരിപ്പിൻ എന്നു കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Provide horses for Paul so that he may be taken safely to Governor Felix."
chapters.nkjv: and provide mounts to set Paul on, and bring him safely to Felix the governor."
chapters.kjv: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

chapters.ml: താഴെ പറയുന്ന വിധത്തിൽ ഒരു എഴുത്തും എഴുതി:
chapters.niv: He wrote a letter as follows:
chapters.nkjv: He wrote a letter in the following manner:
chapters.kjv: And he wrote a letter after this manner:

chapters.ml: ക്ളൌദ്യൊസ് ലുസിയാസ് രാജശ്രീ ഫേലിക്സ് ദേശാധിപതിക്കു വന്ദനം.
chapters.niv: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.
chapters.nkjv: Claudius Lysias, To the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.
chapters.kjv: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.

chapters.ml: ഈ പുരുഷനെ യെഹൂദന്മാർ പിടിച്ചു കൊല്ലുവാൻ ഭാവിച്ചപ്പോൾ റോമപൌരൻ എന്നു അറിഞ്ഞു ഞാൻ പട്ടാളത്തോടും കൂടെ നേരിട്ടു ചെന്നു അവനെ വിടുവിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: This man was seized by the Jews and they were about to kill him, but I came with my troops and rescued him, for I had learned that he is a Roman citizen.
chapters.nkjv: This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be killed by them. Coming with the troops I rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.
chapters.kjv: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

chapters.ml: അവന്റെമേൽ കുറ്റം ചുമത്തുന്ന സംഗതി ഗ്രഹിപ്പാൻ ഇച്ഛിച്ചിട്ടു അവരുടെ ന്യായാധിപസംഘത്തിലേക്കു അവനെ കൊണ്ടുചെന്നു.
chapters.niv: I wanted to know why they were accusing him, so I brought him to their Sanhedrin.
chapters.nkjv: And when I wanted to know the reason they accused him, I brought him before their council.
chapters.kjv: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ അവരുടെ ന്യായപ്രമാണം സംബന്ധിച്ചുള്ള തർക്കങ്ങളെക്കുറിച്ചു കുറ്റം ചുമത്തുന്നതല്ലാതെ മരണത്തിന്നോ ചങ്ങലെക്കോ യോഗ്യമായതു ഒന്നും ഇല്ല എന്നു കണ്ടു.
chapters.niv: I found that the accusation had to do with questions about their law, but there was no charge against him that deserved death or imprisonment.
chapters.nkjv: I found out that he was accused concerning questions of their law, but had nothing charged against him deserving of death or chains.
chapters.kjv: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

chapters.ml: അനന്തരം ഈ പുരുഷന്റെ നേരെ അവർ കൂട്ടുകെട്ടു ഉണ്ടാക്കുന്നു എന്നു തുമ്പുകിട്ടിയപ്പോൾ ഞാൻ തൽക്ഷണം അവനെ നിന്റെ അടുക്കലേക്കു അയച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു; അവന്റെ നേരെയുള്ള അന്യായം സന്നിധാനത്തിൽ ബോധിപ്പിപ്പാൻ വാദികളോടു കല്പിച്ചുമിരിക്കുന്നു; ശുഭമായിരിക്കട്ടെ.
chapters.niv: When I was informed of a plot to be carried out against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also ordered his accusers to present to you their case against him.
chapters.nkjv: And when it was told me that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him immediately to you, and also commanded his accusers to state before you the charges against him. Farewell.
chapters.kjv: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.

chapters.ml: പടയാളികൾ കല്പനപ്രകാരം പൌലൊസിനെ കൂട്ടി രാത്രിയിൽ അന്തിപത്രിസോളം കൊണ്ടുചെന്നു,
chapters.niv: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul with them during the night and brought him as far as Antipatris.
chapters.nkjv: Then the soldiers, as they were commanded, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
chapters.kjv: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.

chapters.ml: പിറ്റെന്നാൾ കുതിരച്ചേവകരെ അവനോടുകൂടെ അയച്ചു കോട്ടയിലേക്കു മടങ്ങിപോന്നു.
chapters.niv: The next day they let the cavalry go on with him, while they returned to the barracks.
chapters.nkjv: The next day they left the horsemen to go on with him, and returned to the barracks.
chapters.kjv: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:

chapters.ml: മറ്റവർ കൈസര്യയിൽ എത്തി ദേശാധിപതിക്കു എഴുത്തു കൊടുത്തു പൌലൊസിനെയും അവന്റെ മുമ്പിൽ നിർത്തി.
chapters.niv: When the cavalry arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
chapters.nkjv: When they came to Caesarea and had delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.
chapters.kjv: Who, when they came to Cæsarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

chapters.ml: അവൻ എഴുത്തു വായിച്ചിട്ടു ഏതു സംസ്ഥാനക്കാരൻ എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു. കിലിക്യക്കാരൻ എന്നു കേട്ടാറെ:
chapters.niv: The governor read the letter and asked what province he was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,
chapters.nkjv: And when the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. And when he understood that hewas from Cilicia,
chapters.kjv: And when the governor had read the letter , he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;

chapters.ml: വാദികളും കൂടെ വന്നു ചേരുമ്പോൾ നിന്നെ വിസ്തരിക്കാം എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു ഹെരോദാവിന്റെ ആസ്ഥാനത്തിൽ അവനെ കാത്തുകൊൾവാൻ കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: he said, "I will hear your case when your accusers get here." Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s palace.
chapters.nkjv: he said, "I will hear you when your accusers also have come." And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s Praetorium.
chapters.kjv: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.

chapters.ml: അഞ്ചുനാൾ കഴിഞ്ഞശേഷം മഹാപുരോഹിതനായ അനന്യാസ് മൂപ്പന്മാരോടും തെർത്തുല്ലൊസ് എന്ന ഒരു വ്യവഹാരജ്ഞനോടും കൂടി വന്നു. പൌലൊസിന്റെ നേരെ ദേശാധിപതിയുടെ മുമ്പാകെ അന്യായം ബോധിപ്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Five days later the high priest Ananias went down to Caesarea with some of the elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, and they brought their charges against Paul before the governor.
chapters.nkjv: Now after five days Ananias the high priest came down with the elders and a certain orator named Tertullus. These gave evidence to the governor against Paul.
chapters.kjv: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.

chapters.ml: അവനെ വിളിച്ചാറെ തെർത്തുല്ലൊസ് അന്യായം വിവരിച്ചു പറഞ്ഞതെന്തെന്നാൽ:
chapters.niv: When Paul was called in, Tertullus presented his case before Felix: "We have enjoyed a long period of peace under you, and your foresight has brought about reforms in this nation.
chapters.nkjv: And when he was called upon, Tertullus began his accusation, saying: "Seeing that through you we enjoy great peace, and prosperity is being brought to this nation by your foresight,
chapters.kjv: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him , saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,

chapters.ml: രാജശ്രീ ഫേലിക്സേ, നീമുഖാന്തരം ഞങ്ങൾ വളരെ സമാധാനം അനുഭവിക്കുന്നതും നിന്റെ പരിപാലനത്താൽ ഈ ജാതിക്കു ഏറിയ ഗുണീകരണങ്ങൾ സാധിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നതും ഞങ്ങൾ എപ്പോഴും എല്ലായിടത്തും പൂർണ്ണനന്ദിയോടും കൂടെ അംഗീകരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: Everywhere and in every way, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with profound gratitude.
chapters.nkjv: we accept it always and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
chapters.kjv: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.

chapters.ml: എങ്കിലും നിന്നെ അധികം അസഹ്യപ്പെടുത്തരുതു എന്നുവെച്ചു ക്ഷമയോടെ ചുരുക്കത്തിൽ ഞങ്ങളുടെ അന്യായം കേൾക്കേണം എന്നു അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: But in order not to weary you further, I would request that you be kind enough to hear us briefly.
chapters.nkjv: Nevertheless, not to be tedious to you any further, I beg you to hear, by your courtesy, a few words from us.
chapters.kjv: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.

chapters.ml: ഈ പുരുഷൻ ഒരു ബാധയും ലോകത്തിലുള്ള സകല യെഹൂദന്മാരുടെയും ഇടയിൽ കലഹമുണ്ടാക്കുന്നവനും നസറായമതത്തിന്നു മുമ്പനും എന്നു ഞങ്ങൾ കണ്ടിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "We have found this man to be a troublemaker, stirring up riots among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the Nazarene sect
chapters.nkjv: For we have found this man a plague, a creator of dissension among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.
chapters.kjv: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow , and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:

chapters.ml: അവൻ ദൈവാലയം തീണ്ടിപ്പാനും ശ്രമിച്ചു. അവനെ ഞങ്ങൾ പിടിച്ചു (ഞങ്ങളുടെ ന്യായപ്രമാണപ്രകാരം വിസ്തരിപ്പാൻ വിചാരിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: and even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.
chapters.nkjv: He even tried to profane the temple, and we seized him, and wanted to judge him according to our law.
chapters.kjv: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.

chapters.ml: എങ്കിലും സഹസ്രാധിപനായ ലുസിയാസ് വളരെ ബലത്തോടു വന്നു അവനെ ഞങ്ങളുടെ കയ്യിൽനിന്നു പിടിച്ചുകൊണ്ടുപോയി.
chapters.niv: By examining him yourself you will be able to learn the truth about all these charges we are bringing against him."
chapters.nkjv: But the commander Lysias came by and with great violence took him out of our hands,
chapters.kjv: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us , and with great violence took him away out of our hands,

chapters.ml: അവന്റെ വാദികൾ നിന്റെ മുമ്പാകെ വരുവാൻ കല്പിച്ചു) നീ തന്നേ അവനെ വിസ്തരിച്ചാൽ ഞങ്ങൾ അന്യായം ബോധിപ്പിക്കുന്ന ഈ സകല സംഗതികളും അറിഞ്ഞുകൊൾവാൻ ഇടയാകും.
chapters.niv: The other Jews joined in the accusation, asserting that these things were true.
chapters.nkjv: commanding his accusers to come to you. By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him."
chapters.kjv: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.

chapters.ml: അതു അങ്ങനെ തന്നേ എന്നു യെഹൂദന്മാരും യോജിച്ചു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: When the governor motioned for him to speak, Paul replied: "I know that for a number of years you have been a judge over this nation; so I gladly make my defense.
chapters.nkjv: And the Jews also assented, maintaining that these things were so.
chapters.kjv: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.

chapters.ml: സംസാരിക്കാം എന്നു ദേശാധിപതി ആംഗ്യം കാട്ടിയാറെ പൌലൊസ് ഉത്തരം പറഞ്ഞതു: ഈ ജാതിക്കു നീ അനേകസംവത്സരമായി ന്യായാധിപതി ആയിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു അറികകൊണ്ടു എന്റെ കാര്യത്തിൽ ഞാൻ ധൈര്യത്തോടെ പ്രതിവാദം ചെയ്യുന്നു.
chapters.niv: You can easily verify that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
chapters.nkjv: Then Paul, after the governor had nodded to him to speak, answered: "Inasmuch as I know that you have been for many years a judge of this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself,
chapters.kjv: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ യെരൂശലേമിൽ നമസ്കരിപ്പാൻ പോയിട്ടു പന്ത്രണ്ടു നാളിൽ അധികമായില്ല എന്നു നിനക്കു അറിയാകുന്നതാകുന്നു.
chapters.niv: My accusers did not find me arguing with anyone at the temple, or stirring up a crowd in the synagogues or anywhere else in the city.
chapters.nkjv: because you may ascertain that it is no more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
chapters.kjv: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.

chapters.ml: ദൈവാലയത്തിലോ പള്ളികളിലോ നഗരങ്ങളിലോവെച്ചു ആരോടും വാദിക്കയെങ്കിലും പുരുഷാരത്തിൽ കലഹം ഉണ്ടാക്കുകയെങ്കിലും ചെയ്യുന്നാതായി അവർ എന്നെ കണ്ടില്ല.
chapters.niv: And they cannot prove to you the charges they are now making against me.
chapters.nkjv: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with anyone nor inciting the crowd, either in the synagogues or in the city.
chapters.kjv: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:

chapters.ml: ഇന്നു എന്റെ നേരെ ബോധിപ്പിക്കുന്ന അന്യായം നിന്റെ മുമ്പാകെ തെളിയിപ്പാൻ അവർക്കു കഴിയുന്നതുമല്ല.
chapters.niv: However, I admit that I worship the God of our ancestors as a follower of the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything that is in accordance with the Law and that is written in the Prophets,
chapters.nkjv: Nor can they prove the things of which they now accuse me.
chapters.kjv: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ ഒന്നു ഞാൻ സമ്മതിക്കുന്നു: മതഭേദം എന്നു ഇവർ പറയുന്ന മാർഗ്ഗപ്രകാരം ഞാൻ പിതാക്കന്മാരുടെ ദൈവത്തെ ആരാധിക്കയും ന്യായപ്രമാണത്തിലും പ്രവാചകപുസ്തകങ്ങളിലും എഴുതിയിരിക്കുന്നതു ഒക്കെയും വിശ്വസിക്കയും ചെയ്യുന്നു.
chapters.niv: and I have the same hope in God as these men themselves have, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
chapters.nkjv: But this I confess to you, that according to the Way which they call a sect, so I worship the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the Law and in the Prophets.
chapters.kjv: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:

chapters.ml: നീതിമാന്മാരുടെയും നീതികെട്ടവരുടെയും പുനരുത്ഥാനം ഉണ്ടാകും എന്നു ഇവർ കാത്തിരിക്കുന്നതുപോലെ ഞാനും ദൈവത്തിങ്കൽ ആശവെച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: So I strive always to keep my conscience clear before God and man.
chapters.nkjv: I have hope in God, which they themselves also accept, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and the unjust.
chapters.kjv: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

chapters.ml: അതു കൊണ്ടു എനിക്കു ദൈവത്തോടും മനുഷ്യരോടും കുറ്റമില്ലാത്ത മനസ്സാക്ഷി എല്ലായ്പോഴും ഉണ്ടായിരിപ്പാൻ ഞാൻ ശ്രമിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "After an absence of several years, I came to Jerusalem to bring my people gifts for the poor and to present offerings.
chapters.nkjv: This being so, I myself always strive to have a conscience without offense toward God and men.
chapters.kjv: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.

chapters.ml: പലസംവത്സരം കൂടീട്ടു ഞാൻ എന്റെ ജാതിക്കാർക്കു ധർമ്മം കൊണ്ടുവരുവാനും വഴിപാടു കഴിപ്പാനും വന്നു.
chapters.niv: I was ceremonially clean when they found me in the temple courts doing this. There was no crowd with me, nor was I involved in any disturbance.
chapters.nkjv: "Now after many years I came to bring alms and offerings to my nation,
chapters.kjv: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

chapters.ml: അതു അനുഷ്ഠിക്കുമ്പോൾ അവർ എന്നെ ദൈവാലയത്തിൽവെച്ചു ശുദ്ധീകരണം കഴിഞ്ഞവനായി കണ്ടു; പുരുഷാരത്തോടു കൂടിയല്ല, കലഹത്തോടുകൂടിയുമല്ല.
chapters.niv: But there are some Jews from the province of Asia, who ought to be here before you and bring charges if they have anything against me.
chapters.nkjv: in the midst of which some Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with a mob nor with tumult.
chapters.kjv: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ ആസ്യക്കാരായ ചില യെഹൂദന്മാർ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു; അവർക്കു എന്റെ നേരെ അന്യായം ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ നിന്റെ മുമ്പിൽ വന്നു ബോധിപ്പിക്കേണ്ടതായിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: Or these who are here should state what crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin—
chapters.nkjv: They ought to have been here before you to object if they had anything against me.
chapters.kjv: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.

chapters.ml: അല്ല, ഞാൻ ന്യായാധിപസംഘത്തിന്റെ മുമ്പിൽ നില്ക്കുമ്പോൾ മരിച്ചവരുടെ പുനരുത്ഥാനത്തെക്കുറിച്ചു ഇന്നു നിങ്ങൾ എന്നെ വിസ്തരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു ഞാൻ വിളിച്ചു പറഞ്ഞോരു വാക്കല്ലാതെ
chapters.niv: unless it was this one thing I shouted as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’ "
chapters.nkjv: Or else let those who are here themselves say if they found any wrongdoing in me while I stood before the council,
chapters.kjv: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,

chapters.ml: അവിടെ വെച്ചു എന്റെ പക്കൽ വല്ല കുറ്റവും കണ്ടിട്ടുണ്ടങ്കിൽ ഇവർ തന്നേ പറയട്ടെ
chapters.niv: Then Felix, who was well acquainted with the Way, adjourned the proceedings. "When Lysias the commander comes," he said, "I will decide your case."
chapters.nkjv: unless itis for this one statement which I cried out, standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged by you this day.’ "
chapters.kjv: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

chapters.ml: ഫേലിക്സിന്നു ഈ മാർഗ്ഗം സംബന്ധിച്ചു സൂക്ഷ്മമായ അറിവു ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നിട്ടും: ലുസിയാസ് സഹസ്രാധിപൻ വരുമ്പോൾ ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളുടെ കാര്യം തീർച്ചപ്പെടുത്തും എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു അവധിവെച്ചു,
chapters.niv: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard but to give him some freedom and permit his friends to take care of his needs.
chapters.nkjv: But when Felix heard these things, having more accurate knowledge of the Way, he adjourned the proceedings and said, "When Lysias the commander comes down, I will make a decision on your case."
chapters.kjv: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.

chapters.ml: ശതാധിപനോടു അവനെ തടവിൽ തന്നേ സൂക്ഷിച്ചു ദയകാണിപ്പാനും അവന്റെ സ്നേഹിതന്മാർ അവന്നു ശുശ്രൂഷ ചെയ്യുന്നതു വിരോധിക്കാതിരിപ്പാനും കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Several days later Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He sent for Paul and listened to him as he spoke about faith in Christ Jesus.
chapters.nkjv: So he commanded the centurion to keep Paul and to let him have liberty, and told him not to forbid any of his friends to provide for or visit him.
chapters.kjv: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.

chapters.ml: കുറെനാൾ കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ടു ഫേലിക്സ് യെഹൂദ സ്ത്രീയായ തന്റെ ഭാര്യ ദ്രുസില്ലയുമായി വന്നു, പൌലൊസിനെ വരുത്തി ക്രിസ്തുയേശുവിലുള്ള വിശ്വാസത്തെക്കുറിച്ചു അവന്റെ പ്രസംഗം കേട്ടു.
chapters.niv: As Paul talked about righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and said, "That’s enough for now! You may leave. When I find it convenient, I will send for you."
chapters.nkjv: And after some days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
chapters.kjv: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ അവൻ നീതി, ഇന്ദ്രീയജയം, വരുവാനുള്ള ന്യായവിധി എന്നിവയെക്കുറിച്ചു സംസാരിക്കുമ്പോൾ ഫേലിക്സ് ഭയപരവശനായി: തൽക്കാലം പോകാം; അവസരം ഉള്ളപ്പോൾ നിന്നെ വിളിപ്പിക്കാം എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: At the same time he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe, so he sent for him frequently and talked with him.
chapters.nkjv: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, "Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you."
chapters.kjv: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.

chapters.ml: പൌലൊസ് തനിക്കു ദ്രവ്യം തരും എന്നു ആശിച്ചു പലപ്പോഴും അവനെ വരുത്തി അവനോടു സംഭാഷിച്ചു പോന്നു.
chapters.niv: When two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, but because Felix wanted to grant a favor to the Jews, he left Paul in prison.
chapters.nkjv: Meanwhile he also hoped that money would be given him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore he sent for him more often and conversed with him.
chapters.kjv: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

chapters.ml: രണ്ടാണ്ടു കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ടു ഫേലിക്സിന്നു പിൻവാഴിയായി പൊർക്ക്യൊസ് ഫെസ്തൊസ് വന്നപ്പോൾ ഫേലിക്സ് യെഹൂദന്മാരുടെ പ്രീതി സമ്പാദിക്കേണം എന്നു വെച്ചു പൌലൊസിനെ തടവുകാരനായി വിട്ടേച്ചുപോയി.
chapters.nkjv: But after two years Porcius Festus succeeded Felix; and Felix, wanting to do the Jews a favor, left Paul bound.
chapters.kjv: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.

chapters.ml: ഫെസ്തൊസ് സംസ്ഥാനത്തിൽ വന്നിട്ടു മൂന്നു നാൾ കഴിഞ്ഞശേഷം കൈസര്യയിൽ നിന്നു യെരൂശലേമിലേക്കു പോയി..
chapters.niv: Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,
chapters.nkjv: Now when Festus had come to the province, after three days he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
chapters.kjv: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cæsarea to Jerusalem.

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ മഹാപുരോഹിതന്മാരും യെഹൂദന്മാരുടെ പ്രധാനികളും പൌലൊസിന്റെ നേരെ അവന്റെ സന്നിധിയിൽ അന്യായം ബോധിപ്പിച്ചു;
chapters.niv: where the chief priests and the Jewish leaders appeared before him and presented the charges against Paul.
chapters.nkjv: Then the high priest and the chief men of the Jews informed him against Paul; and they petitioned him,
chapters.kjv: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,

chapters.ml: ദയചെയ്തു അവനെ യെരൂശലേമിലേക്കു വരുത്തേണ്ടതിന്നു അവർ പൌലൊസിന്നു പ്രതികൂലമായി അവനോടു അപേക്ഷിച്ചു;
chapters.niv: They requested Festus, as a favor to them, to have Paul transferred to Jerusalem, for they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.
chapters.nkjv: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem— while they lay in ambush along the road to kill him.
chapters.kjv: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.

chapters.ml: വഴിയിൽവെച്ചു അവനെ ഒടുക്കിക്കളവാൻ അവർ ഒരു പതിയിരിപ്പുനിർത്തി. അതിന്നു ഫെസ്തൊസ്: പൌലൊസിനെ കൈസര്യയിൽ സൂക്ഷിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു; ഞാൻ വേഗം അവിടേക്കു പോകുന്നുണ്ടു;
chapters.niv: Festus answered, "Paul is being held at Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.
chapters.nkjv: But Festus answered that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself was going there shortly.
chapters.kjv: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Cæsarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither .

chapters.ml: നിങ്ങളിൽ പ്രാപ്തിയുള്ളവർ കൂടെ വന്നു ആ മനുഷ്യന്റെ നേരെ അന്യായം ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ ബോധിപ്പിക്കട്ടെ എന്നു ഉത്തരം പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Let some of your leaders come with me, and if the man has done anything wrong, they can press charges against him there."
chapters.nkjv: "Therefore," he said, "let those who have authority among you go down with me and accuse this man, to see if there is any fault in him."
chapters.kjv: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me , and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.

chapters.ml: അവൻ ഏകദേശം എട്ടു പത്തു ദിവസം അവരുടെ ഇടയിൽ താമസിച്ചശേഷം കൈസര്യക്കു മടങ്ങിപ്പോയി; പിറ്റെന്നു ന്യായാസനത്തിൽ ഇരുന്നു പൌലൊസിനെ വരുത്തുവാൻ കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: After spending eight or ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he convened the court and ordered that Paul be brought before him.
chapters.nkjv: And when he had remained among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea. And the next day, sitting on the judgment seat, he commanded Paul to be brought.
chapters.kjv: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Cæsarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.

chapters.ml: അവൻ വന്നാറെ യെരൂശലേമിൽ നിന്നു വന്ന യെഹൂദന്മാർ ചുറ്റും നിന്നു അവന്റെ നേരെ കഠിനകുറ്റം പലതും ബോധിപ്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When Paul came in, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him. They brought many serious charges against him, but they could not prove them.
chapters.nkjv: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood about and laid many serious complaints against Paul, which they could not prove,
chapters.kjv: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.

chapters.ml: പൌലൊസോ: യെഹൂദന്മാരുടെ ന്യായപ്രമാണത്തോടാകട്ടെ ദൈവാലയത്തോടാകട്ടെ കൈസരോടാകട്ടെ ഞാൻ ഒരു കുറ്റവും ചെയ്തിട്ടില്ല എന്നു പ്രതിവാദിച്ചാറെ ആ കുറ്റങ്ങളെ തെളിയിപ്പാൻ അവർക്കു കഴിഞ്ഞില്ല.
chapters.niv: Then Paul made his defense: "I have done nothing wrong against the Jewish law or against the temple or against Caesar."
chapters.nkjv: while he answered for himself, "Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar have I offended in anything at all."
chapters.kjv: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Cæsar, have I offended any thing at all.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ ഫെസ്തൊസ് യെഹൂദന്മാരുടെ പ്രീതി സമ്പാദിപ്പാൻ ഇച്ഛിച്ചു പൌലൊസിനോടു: യെരൂശലേമിലേക്കു ചെന്നു അവിടെ എന്റെ മുമ്പിൽവെച്ചു ഈ സംഗതികളെക്കുറിച്ചു വിസ്താരംനടപ്പാൻ നിനക്കു സമ്മതമുണ്ടോ എന്നു ചോദിച്ചതിന്നു പൌലൊസ് ഞാൻ കൈസരുടെ ന്യായാസനത്തിന്നു മുമ്പാകെ നില്ക്കുന്നു;
chapters.niv: Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and stand trial before me there on these charges?"
chapters.nkjv: But Festus, wanting to do the Jews a favor, answered Paul and said, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and there be judged before me concerning these things?"
chapters.kjv: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?

chapters.ml: ﻿അവിടെ എന്നെ വിസ്തരിക്കേണ്ടതാകുന്നു; യെഹൂദന്മാരോടു ഞാൻ ഒരു അന്യായവും ചെയ്തിട്ടില്ല; അതു നീയും നല്ലവണ്ണം അറിഞ്ഞിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: Paul answered: "I am now standing before Caesar’s court, where I ought to be tried. I have not done any wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.
chapters.nkjv: So Paul said, "I stand at Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. To the Jews I have done no wrong, as you very well know.
chapters.kjv: Then said Paul, I stand at Cæsar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.

chapters.ml: ﻿ഞാൻ അന്യായം ചെയ്തു മരണയോഗ്യമായതു വല്ലതും പ്രവൃത്തിച്ചിട്ടുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ മരണശിക്ഷ ഏല്ക്കുന്നതിന്നു എനിക്കു വിരോധമില്ല. ഇവർ എന്റെനേരെ ബോധിപ്പിക്കുന്ന അന്യായം നേരല്ല എന്നു വരികിലോ എന്നെ അവർക്കു ഏല്പിച്ചുകൊടുപ്പാൻ ആർക്കും കഴിയുന്നതല്ല;
chapters.niv: If, however, I am guilty of doing anything deserving death, I do not refuse to die. But if the charges brought against me by these Jews are not true, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!"
chapters.nkjv: For if I am an offender, or have committed anything deserving of death, I do not object to dying; but if there is nothing in these things of which these men accuse me, no one can deliver me to them. I appeal to Caesar."
chapters.kjv: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ കൈസരെ അഭയംചൊല്ലുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു. അപ്പോൾ ഫെസ്തൊസ് തന്റെ ആലോചന സഭയോടു സംസാരിച്ചിട്ടു: കൈസരെ നീ അഭയം ചൊല്ലിയിരിക്കുന്നു; കൈസരുടെ അടുക്കലേക്കു നീ പോകും എന്നു ഉത്തരം പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: After Festus had conferred with his council, he declared: "You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!"
chapters.nkjv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, "You have appealed to Caesar? To Caesar you shall go!"
chapters.kjv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Cæsar? unto Cæsar shalt thou go.

chapters.ml: ഒട്ടുനാൾ കഴിഞ്ഞശേഷം അഗ്രിപ്പാരാജാവും ബെർന്നീക്കയും ഫെസ്തോസിനെ വന്ദനം ചെയ്‍വാൻ കൈസര്യയിൽ എത്തി.
chapters.niv: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.
chapters.nkjv: And after some days King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.
chapters.kjv: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cæsarea to salute Festus.

chapters.ml: കുറെ നാൾ അവിടെ പാർക്കുമ്പോൾ ഫെസ്തൊസ് പൌലൊസിന്റെ സംഗതി രാജാവിനോടു വിവരിച്ചു പറഞ്ഞതു: ഫേലിക്സ് വിട്ടേച്ചുപോയോരു തടവുകാരൻ ഉണ്ടു.
chapters.niv: Since they were spending many days there, Festus discussed Paul’s case with the king. He said: "There is a man here whom Felix left as a prisoner.
chapters.nkjv: When they had been there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying: "There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix,
chapters.kjv: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ യെരൂശലേമിൽ ചെന്നപ്പോൾ യെഹൂദന്മാരുടെ മഹാപുരോഹീതന്മാരും മൂപ്പന്മാരും എന്റെ അടുക്കൽ വന്നു അവന്റെ നേരെ അന്യായം ബോധിപ്പിച്ചു. വിധിക്കു അപേക്ഷിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews brought charges against him and asked that he be condemned.
chapters.nkjv: about whom the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, when I was in Jerusalem, asking for a judgment against him.
chapters.kjv: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me , desiring to have judgment against him.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ പ്രതിവാദികളെ അഭിമുഖമായി കണ്ടു അന്യായത്തെക്കുറിച്ചു പ്രതിവാദിപ്പാൻ ഇടകിട്ടുംമുമ്പെ യാതൊരു മനുഷ്യനെയും ഏല്പിച്ചു കൊടുക്കുന്നതു റോമക്കാർക്കു മര്യാദയല്ല എന്നു ഞാൻ അവരോടു ഉത്തരം പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: "I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand over anyone before they have faced their accusers and have had an opportunity to defend themselves against the charges.
chapters.nkjv: To them I answered, ‘It is not the custom of the Romans to deliver any man to destruction before the accused meets the accusers face to face, and has opportunity to answer for himself concerning the charge against him.’
chapters.kjv: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.

chapters.ml: ആകയാൽ അവർ ഇവിടെ വന്നു കൂടിയാറെ ഞാൻ ഒട്ടും താമസിയാതെ പിറ്റെന്നു തന്നേ ന്യായാസനത്തിൽ ഇരുന്നു ആ പുരുഷനെ കൊണ്ടുവരുവാൻ കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When they came here with me, I did not delay the case, but convened the court the next day and ordered the man to be brought in.
chapters.nkjv: Therefore when they had come together, without any delay, the next day I sat on the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought in.
chapters.kjv: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.

chapters.ml: വാദികൾ അവന്റെ ചുറ്റും നിന്നു ഞാൻ നിരൂപിച്ചിരുന്ന കുറ്റം
chapters.niv: When his accusers got up to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.
chapters.nkjv: When the accusers stood up, they brought no accusation against him of such things as I supposed,
chapters.kjv: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:

chapters.ml: ഒന്നും ബോധിപ്പിക്കാതെ സ്വന്തമതത്തെക്കുറിച്ചും ജീവിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പൌലൊസ് പറയുന്ന മരിച്ചുപോയ യേശു എന്നൊരുവനെക്കുറിച്ചും ചില തർക്കസംഗതികളെ കൊണ്ടുവന്നതേയുള്ളു.
chapters.niv: Instead, they had some points of dispute with him about their own religion and about a dead man named Jesus who Paul claimed was alive.
chapters.nkjv: but had some questions against him about their own religion and about a certain Jesus, who had died, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
chapters.kjv: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

chapters.ml: ഇങ്ങനെയുള്ള വിഷയങ്ങളിൽ വിചാരണ നടത്തേണ്ടതു എങ്ങനെയെന്നു ഞാൻ അറിയായ്കയാൽ: നിനക്കു യെരൂശലേമിലേക്കു പോയി അവിടെ ഈ സംഗതികളെക്കുറിച്ചു വിസ്താരം നടപ്പാൻ സമ്മതമുണ്ടോ എന്നു ചോദിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: I was at a loss how to investigate such matters; so I asked if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and stand trial there on these charges.
