chapters.nkjv: And because I was uncertain of such questions, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.
chapters.kjv: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ പൌലൊസ് ചക്രവർത്തിതിരുമനസ്സിലെ വിധിക്കായി തന്നെ സൂക്ഷിക്കേണം എന്നു അഭയംചൊല്ലുകയാൽ കൈസരുടെ അടുക്കൽ അയക്കുവോളം അവനെ സൂക്ഷിപ്പാൻ കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: But when Paul made his appeal to be held over for the Emperor’s decision, I ordered him held until I could send him to Caesar."
chapters.nkjv: But when Paul appealed to be reserved for the decision of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I could send him to Caesar."
chapters.kjv: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cæsar.

chapters.ml: ആ മനുഷ്യന്റെ പ്രസംഗം കേൾപ്പാൻ എനിക്കും ആഗ്രഹമുണ്ടായിരുന്നു എന്നു അഗ്രിപ്പാവു ഫെസ്തൊസിനോടു പറഞ്ഞതിന്നു: നാളെ കേൾക്കാം എന്നു അവൻ പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I would like to hear this man myself." He replied, "Tomorrow you will hear him."
chapters.nkjv: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I also would like to hear the man myself." "Tomorrow," he said, "you shall hear him."
chapters.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.

chapters.ml: പിറ്റെന്നു അഗ്രിപ്പാവു ബെർന്നീക്കയുമായി വളരെ ആഡംബരത്തോടെ വന്നു. സഹസ്രാധിപതികളോടും നഗരത്തിലെ പ്രധാനികളോടും കൂടെ വിചാരണമണ്ഡപത്തിൽ വന്നാറെ ഫെസ്തൊസിന്റെ കല്പനയാൽ പൌലൊസിനെ കൊണ്ടുവന്നു.
chapters.niv: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the audience room with the high-ranking military officers and the prominent men of the city. At the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.
chapters.nkjv: So the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and had entered the auditorium with the commanders and the prominent men of the city, at Festus’ command Paul was brought in.
chapters.kjv: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ ഫെസ്തൊസ് പറഞ്ഞതു: അഗ്രിപ്പാരാജാവേ, ഇവിടെ വന്നു കൂടിയിരിക്കുന്ന സകല പുരുഷന്മാരുമായുള്ളോരേ, യെഹൂദന്മാരുടെ സമൂഹം എല്ലാം യെരൂശലേമിലും ഇവിടെയും വെച്ചു എന്നോടു അപേക്ഷിക്കയും അവനെ ജീവനോടെ വെച്ചേക്കരുതു എന്നു നിലവിളിക്കയും ചെയ്ത ഈ മനുഷ്യനെ നിങ്ങൾ കാണുന്നുവല്ലോ.
chapters.niv: Festus said: "King Agrippa, and all who are present with us, you see this man! The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him in Jerusalem and here in Caesarea, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.
chapters.nkjv: And Festus said: "King Agrippa and all the men who are here present with us, you see this man about whom the whole assembly of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying out that he was not fit to live any longer.
chapters.kjv: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

chapters.ml: അവൻ മരണയോഗ്യമായതു ഒന്നും ചെയ്തിട്ടില്ല എന്നു ഞാൻ ഗ്രഹിച്ചു; അവൻ തന്നെയും ചക്രവർത്തിതിരുമനസ്സിലെ അഭയം ചൊല്ലുകയാൽ അവനെ അയക്കേണം എന്നു വിധിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: I found he had done nothing deserving of death, but because he made his appeal to the Emperor I decided to send him to Rome.
chapters.nkjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing deserving of death, and that he himself had appealed to Augustus, I decided to send him.
chapters.kjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.

chapters.ml: അവനെക്കുറിച്ചു തിരുമേനിക്കു എഴുതുവാൻ എനിക്കു നിശ്ചയമായതു ഒന്നുമില്ല; അതുകൊണ്ടു വിസ്താരം കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ടു എഴുതുവാൻ വല്ലതും ഉണ്ടാകേണ്ടതിന്നു അവനെ നിങ്ങളുടെ മുമ്പിലും വിശേഷാൽ അഗ്രിപ്പാരാജാവേ, തിരുമുമ്പിലും വരുത്തിയിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: But I have nothing definite to write to His Majesty about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that as a result of this investigation I may have something to write.
chapters.nkjv: I have nothing certain to write to my lord concerning him. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the examination has taken place I may have something to write.
chapters.kjv: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.

chapters.ml: തടവുകാരനെ അയക്കുമ്പോൾ അവന്റെ പേരിലുള്ള കുറ്റം കാണിക്കാതിരിക്കുന്നതു യുക്തമല്ല എന്നു തോന്നുന്നു.
chapters.niv: For I think it is unreasonable to send a prisoner on to Rome without specifying the charges against him."
chapters.nkjv: For it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner and not to specify the charges against him."
chapters.kjv: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.

chapters.ml: അഗ്രിപ്പാവു പൌലൊസിനോടു: നീന്റെ കാര്യം പറവാൻ അനുവാദം ഉണ്ടു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞപ്പോൾ പൌലൊസ് കൈനീട്ടി പ്രതിവാദിച്ചതെന്തെന്നാൽ:
chapters.niv: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "You have permission to speak for yourself." So Paul motioned with his hand and began his defense:
chapters.nkjv: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "You are permitted to speak for yourself." So Paul stretched out his hand and answered for himself:
chapters.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:

chapters.ml: അഗ്രിപ്പാരാജാവേ, യെഹൂദന്മാർ എന്റെ മേൽ ചുമത്തുന്ന എല്ലാ കുറ്റങ്ങളെയും കുറിച്ചു ഇന്നു തിരുമുമ്പാകെ പ്രതിവാദിപ്പാൻ ഇടവന്നതുകൊണ്ടു,
chapters.niv: "King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today as I make my defense against all the accusations of the Jews,
chapters.nkjv: "I think myself happy, King Agrippa, because today I shall answer for myself before you concerning all the things of which I am accused by the Jews,
chapters.kjv: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:

chapters.ml: വിശേഷാൽ നീ യെഹൂദന്മാരുടെ ഇടയിലെ ആചാരങ്ങളും തർക്കങ്ങളും എല്ലാം അറിയുന്നവൻ ആകയാൽ ഞാൻ ഭാഗ്യവാൻ എന്നു നിരൂപിക്കുന്നു; അതുകൊണ്ടു എന്റെ പ്രതിവാദം ക്ഷമയോടേ കേൾക്കേണമെന്നു അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: and especially so because you are well acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. Therefore, I beg you to listen to me patiently.
chapters.nkjv: especially because you are expert in all customs and questions which have to do with the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.
chapters.kjv: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.

chapters.ml: എന്റെ ജാതിക്കാരുടെ ഇടയിലും യെരൂശലേമിലും ആദിമുതൽ ബാല്യംതുടങ്ങിയുള്ള എന്റെ നടപ്പു യെഹൂദന്മാർ എല്ലാവരും അറിയുന്നു.
chapters.niv: "The Jewish people all know the way I have lived ever since I was a child, from the beginning of my life in my own country, and also in Jerusalem.
chapters.nkjv: "My manner of life from my youth, which was spent from the beginning among my own nation at Jerusalem, all the Jews know.
chapters.kjv: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ നമ്മുടെ മാർഗ്ഗത്തിൽ സൂക്ഷ്മത ഏറിയ മതഭേദപ്രകാരം പരീശനായി ജീവിച്ചു എന്നു അവർ ആദിമുതൽ അറിയുന്നു; അവർക്കു മനസ്സുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ സാക്ഷ്യം പറയാം.
chapters.niv: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I conformed to the strictest sect of our religion, living as a Pharisee.
chapters.nkjv: They knew me from the first, if they were willing to testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
chapters.kjv: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

chapters.ml: ദൈവത്താൽ നമ്മുടെ പിതാക്കന്മാർക്കു ലഭിച്ചതും
chapters.niv: And now it is because of my hope in what God has promised our ancestors that I am on trial today.
chapters.nkjv: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers.
chapters.kjv: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:

chapters.ml: നമ്മുടെ പന്ത്രണ്ടു ഗോത്രങ്ങളും രാപ്പകൽ ശ്രദ്ധയോടെ ആരാധിച്ചുകൊണ്ടു എത്തിപ്പിടിപ്പാൻ ആശിക്കുന്നതും ആയ വാഗ്ദത്തത്തിലുള്ള പ്രത്യാശഹേതുവായിട്ടത്രേ ഞാൻ ഇപ്പോൾ വിസ്താരത്തിൽ ആയിരിക്കുന്നതു. ആ പ്രത്യാശയെച്ചൊല്ലി ആകുന്നു രാജാവേ, യെഹൂദന്മാർ എന്റെമേൽ കുറ്റം ചുമത്തുന്നതു.
chapters.niv: This is the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God day and night. King Agrippa, it is because of this hope that these Jews are accusing me.
chapters.nkjv: To this promise our twelve tribes, earnestly serving God night and day, hope to attain. For this hope’s sake, King Agrippa, I am accused by the Jews.
chapters.kjv: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.

chapters.ml: ദൈവം മരിച്ചവരെ ഉയിർപ്പിക്കുന്നതു വിശ്വാസയോഗ്യമല്ല എന്നു നിങ്ങൾക്കു തോന്നുന്നതു എന്തു?
chapters.niv: Why should any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
chapters.nkjv: Why should it be thought incredible by you that God raises the dead?
chapters.kjv: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?

chapters.ml: നസറായനായ യേശുവിന്റെ നാമത്തിന്നു വിരോധമായി പലതും പ്രവർത്തിക്കേണം എന്നു ഞാനും വിചാരിച്ചു സത്യം.
chapters.niv: "I too was convinced that I ought to do all that was possible to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
chapters.nkjv: "Indeed, I myself thought I must do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
chapters.kjv: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

chapters.ml: അതു ഞാൻ യെരൂശലേമിൽ ചെയ്തിട്ടുമുണ്ടു; മഹാ പുരോഹിതന്മാരോടു അധികാരപത്രം വാങ്ങി വിശുദ്ധന്മാരിൽ പലരെയും തടവിൽ ആക്കി അടെച്ചു; അവരെ നിഗ്രഹിക്കുന്ന സമയം ഞാനും സമ്മതം കൊടുത്തു.
chapters.niv: And that is just what I did in Jerusalem. On the authority of the chief priests I put many of the Lord’s people in prison, and when they were put to death, I cast my vote against them.
chapters.nkjv: This I also did in Jerusalem, and many of the saints I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I cast my vote against them.
chapters.kjv: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them .

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ എല്ലാ പള്ളികളിലും അവരെ പലപ്പോഴും ദണ്ഡിപ്പിച്ചുംകൊണ്ടു ദൂഷണം പറവാൻ നിർബന്ധിക്കയും അവരുടെ നേരെ അത്യന്തം ഭ്രാന്തുപിടിച്ചു അന്യപട്ടണങ്ങളോളവും ചെന്നു അവരെ ഉപദ്രവിക്കയും ചെയ്തു.
chapters.niv: Many a time I went from one synagogue to another to have them punished, and I tried to force them to blaspheme. I was so obsessed with persecuting them that I even hunted them down in foreign cities.
chapters.nkjv: And I punished them often in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
chapters.kjv: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

chapters.ml: ഇങ്ങനെ ചെയ്തുവരികയിൽ ഞാൻ മഹാപുരോഹിതന്മാരുടെ അധികാരത്തോടും ആജ്ഞയോടും കൂടെ ദമസ്കൊസിലേക്കു യാത്രപോകുമ്പോൾ,
chapters.niv: "On one of these journeys I was going to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
chapters.nkjv: "While thus occupied, as I journeyed to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
chapters.kjv: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

chapters.ml: രാജാവേ, നട്ടുച്ചെക്കു ഞാൻ വഴിയിൽവെച്ചു സൂര്യന്റെ പ്രകാശത്തെ കവിഞ്ഞൊരു വെളിച്ചം ആകാശത്തിൽ നിന്നു എന്നെയും എന്നോടു കൂടെ യാത്രചെയ്യുന്നവരെയും ചുറ്റി പ്രകാശിക്കുന്നതു കണ്ടു.
chapters.niv: About noon, King Agrippa, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, blazing around me and my companions.
chapters.nkjv: at midday, O king, along the road I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who journeyed with me.
chapters.kjv: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

chapters.ml: ഞങ്ങൾ എല്ലാവരും നിലത്തു വീണപ്പോൾ: ശൌലെ, ശൌലെ, നീ എന്നെ ഉപദ്രവിക്കുന്നതു എന്തു? മുള്ളിന്റെ നേരെ ഉതെക്കുന്നതു നിനക്കു വിഷമം ആകുന്നു എന്നു എബ്രായഭാഷയിൽ എന്നോടു പറയുന്നൊരു ശബ്ദം ഞാൻ കേട്ടു.
chapters.niv: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me in Aramaic, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
chapters.nkjv: And when we all had fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me and saying in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
chapters.kjv: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

chapters.ml: നീ ആരാകുന്നു കർത്താവേ, എന്നു ഞാൻ ചോദിച്ചതിന്നു കർത്താവു: നീ ഉപദ്രവിക്കുന്ന യേശു തന്നേ ഞാൻ;
chapters.niv: "Then I asked, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ " ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.
chapters.nkjv: So I said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
chapters.kjv: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

chapters.ml: എങ്കിലും എഴുന്നേറ്റു നിവിർന്നു നിൽക്ക; നീ എന്നെ കണ്ടതിന്നും ഇനി ഞാൻ നിനക്കു പ്രത്യക്ഷൻ ആവാനിരിക്കുന്നതിന്നും നിന്നെ ശുശ്രൂഷകനും സാക്ഷിയുമായി നിയമിപ്പാൻ ഞാൻ നിനക്കു പ്രത്യക്ഷനായി.
chapters.niv: ‘Now get up and stand on your feet. I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen and will see of me.
chapters.nkjv: But rise and stand on your feet; for I have appeared to you for this purpose, to make you a minister and a witness both of the things which you have seen and of the things which I will yet reveal to you.
chapters.kjv: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;

chapters.ml: ജനത്തിന്റെയും ജാതികളുടെയും കയ്യിൽനിന്നു ഞാൻ നിന്നെ രക്ഷിക്കും.
chapters.niv: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them
chapters.nkjv: I will deliver you from the Jewish people, as well as from the Gentiles, to whom I now send you,
chapters.kjv: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,

chapters.ml: അവർക്കു പാപമോചനവും എന്നിലുള്ള വിശ്വാസത്താൽ ശുദ്ധീകരിക്കപ്പെട്ടവരുടെ ഇടയിൽ അവകാശവും ലഭിക്കേണ്ടതിന്നു അവരുടെ കണ്ണു തുറപ്പാനും അവരെ ഇരുളിൽനിന്നു വെളിച്ചത്തിലേക്കും സാത്താന്റെ അധികാരത്തിൽ നിന്നു ദൈവത്തിങ്കലേക്കും തിരിപ്പാനും ഞാൻ ഇപ്പോൾ നിന്നെ അവരുടെ അടുക്കൽ അയക്കുന്നു എന്നു കല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: to open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’
chapters.nkjv: to open their eyes, in order to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.’
chapters.kjv: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

chapters.ml: അതുകൊണ്ടു അഗ്രിപ്പാരാജാവേ, ഞാൻ സ്വർഗ്ഗീയദർശനത്തിന്നു അനുസരണക്കേടു കാണിക്കാതെ
chapters.niv: "So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the vision from heaven.
chapters.nkjv: "Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
chapters.kjv: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

chapters.ml: ആദ്യം ദമസ്കൊസിലും യെരൂശലേമിലും യെഹൂദ്യദേശത്തെങ്ങും ഉള്ളവരോടും പിന്നെ ജാതികളോടും മാനസാന്തരപ്പെട്ടു ദൈവത്തിങ്കലേക്കു തിരിഞ്ഞു മാനസാന്തരത്തിന്നു യോഗ്യമായ പ്രവൃത്തികൾ ചെയ്യേണം എന്നു പ്രസംഗിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: First to those in Damascus, then to those in Jerusalem and in all Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I preached that they should repent and turn to God and demonstrate their repentance by their deeds.
chapters.nkjv: but declared first to those in Damascus and in Jerusalem, and throughout all the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent, turn to God, and do works befitting repentance.
chapters.kjv: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.

chapters.ml: ഇതു നിമിത്തം യെഹൂദന്മാർ ദൈവാലയത്തിൽ വെച്ചു എന്നെ പിടിച്ചു കൊല്ലുവാൻ ശ്രമിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: That is why some Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.
chapters.nkjv: For these reasons the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.
chapters.kjv: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me .

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ ദൈവത്തിന്റെ സഹായം ലഭിക്കയാൽ ഞാൻ ഇന്നുവരെ നിൽക്കയും ചെറിയവരോടും വലിയവരോടും സാക്ഷ്യം പറഞ്ഞു പോരുകയും ചെയ്യുന്നു.
chapters.niv: But God has helped me to this very day; so I stand here and testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen—
chapters.nkjv: Therefore, having obtained help from God, to this day I stand, witnessing both to small and great, saying no other things than those which the prophets and Moses said would come—
chapters.kjv: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:

chapters.ml: ﻿ക്രിസ്തു കഷ്ടം അനുഭവിക്കയും മരിച്ചവരുടെ പുനരുത്ഥാനത്തിൽ ആദ്യനായി ജനത്തോടും ജാതികളോടും വെളിച്ചം അറിയിക്കയും ചെയ്യും എന്നു പ്രവാചകന്മാരും മോശെയും ഭാവികാലത്തെക്കുറിച്ചു പ്രസ്താവിച്ചതൊഴികെ വേറെയൊന്നും ഞാൻ പറയുന്നില്ല.
chapters.niv: that the Messiah would suffer and, as the first to rise from the dead, would bring the message of light to his own people and to the Gentiles."
chapters.nkjv: that the Christ would suffer, that He would be the first to rise from the dead, and would proclaim light to the Jewish people and to the Gentiles."
chapters.kjv: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.

chapters.ml: ഇങ്ങനെ പ്രതിവാദിക്കയിൽ ഫെസ്തൊസ്: പൌലൊസേ, നിനക്കു ഭ്രാന്തുണ്ടു; വിദ്യാ ബഹുത്വത്താൽ നിനക്കു ഭ്രാന്തു പിടിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു ഉറക്കെ പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: At this point Festus interrupted Paul’s defense. "You are out of your mind, Paul!" he shouted. "Your great learning is driving you insane."
chapters.nkjv: Now as he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, "Paul, you are beside yourself! Much learning is driving you mad!"
chapters.kjv: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.

chapters.ml: അതിന്നു പൌലൊസ്: രാജശ്രീ ഫെസ്തൊസേ, എനിക്കു ഭ്രാന്തില്ല; ഞാൻ സത്യവും സുബോധവുമായ വാക്കത്രേ സംസാരിക്കുന്നതു.
chapters.niv: "I am not insane, most excellent Festus," Paul replied. "What I am saying is true and reasonable.
chapters.nkjv: But he said, "I am not mad, most noble Festus, but speak the words of truth and reason.
chapters.kjv: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.

chapters.ml: രാജാവിന്നു ഇതിനെക്കുറിച്ചു അറിവുള്ളതുകൊണ്ടു അവനോടു ഞാൻ പ്രാഗത്ഭ്യത്തോടെ സംസാരിക്കുന്നു; അവന്നു ഇതു ഒന്നും മറവായിരിക്കുന്നില്ല എന്നു എനിക്കു നിശ്ചയമുണ്ടു; അതു ഒരു കോണിൽ നടന്നതല്ല.
chapters.niv: The king is familiar with these things, and I can speak freely to him. I am convinced that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.
chapters.nkjv: For the king, before whom I also speak freely, knows these things; for I am convinced that none of these things escapes his attention, since this thing was not done in a corner.
chapters.kjv: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.

chapters.ml: അഗ്രിപ്പാരാജാവേ, പ്രവാചകന്മാരെ വിശ്വസിക്കുന്നുവോ? വിശ്വസിക്കുന്നു എന്നു ഞാൻ അറിയുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do."
chapters.nkjv: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you do believe."
chapters.kjv: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.

chapters.ml: അഗ്രിപ്പാ പൌലൊസിനോടു: ഞാൻ ക്രിസ്ത്യാനിയായിത്തിരുവാൻ നീ എന്നെ അല്പംകൊണ്ടു സമ്മതിപ്പിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു. - അതിന്നു പൌലൊസ്;
chapters.niv: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "Do you think that in such a short time you can persuade me to be a Christian?"
chapters.nkjv: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "You almost persuade me to become a Christian."
chapters.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.

chapters.ml: നീ മാത്രമല്ല, ഇന്നു എന്റെ പ്രസംഗം കേൾക്കുന്നവർ എല്ലാവരും അല്പംകൊണ്ടാകട്ടെ അധികം കൊണ്ടാകട്ടെ ഈ ചങ്ങല ഒഴികെ എന്നെപ്പോലെ ആകേണം എന്നു ഞാൻ ദൈവത്തോടു അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Paul replied, "Short time or long—I pray to God that not only you but all who are listening to me today may become what I am, except for these chains."
chapters.nkjv: And Paul said, "I would to God that not only you, but also all who hear me today, might become both almost and altogether such as I am, except for these chains."
chapters.kjv: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ രാജാവും ദേശാധിപതിയും ബെർന്നീക്കയും അവരോടുകൂടെ ഇരുന്നവരും എഴുന്നേറ്റു മാറി നിന്നു:
chapters.niv: The king rose, and with him the governor and Bernice and those sitting with them.
chapters.nkjv: When he had said these things, the king stood up, as well as the governor and Bernice and those who sat with them;
chapters.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:

chapters.ml: ഈ മനുഷ്യൻ മരണത്തിന്നോ ചങ്ങലെക്കോ യോഗ്യമായതു ഒന്നും ചെയ്തിട്ടില്ല എന്നു തമ്മിൽ പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: After they left the room, they began saying to one another, "This man is not doing anything that deserves death or imprisonment."
chapters.nkjv: and when they had gone aside, they talked among themselves, saying, "This man is doing nothing deserving of death or chains."
chapters.kjv: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

chapters.ml: കൈസരെ അഭയം ചൊല്ലിയിരുന്നില്ലെങ്കിൽ അവനെ വിട്ടയപ്പാൻ കഴിയുമായിരുന്നു എന്നു അഗ്രിപ്പാവു ഫെസ്തൊസിനോടു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."
chapters.nkjv: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."
chapters.kjv: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.

chapters.ml: ഞങ്ങൾ കപ്പൽ കയറി ഇതല്യെക്കു പോകേണം എന്നു കല്പനയായപ്പോൾ പൌലൊസിനെയും മറ്റു ചില തടവുകാരെയും ഔഗുസ്ത്യപട്ടാളത്തിലെ ശതാധിപനായ യൂലിയൊസിനെ ഏല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
chapters.nkjv: And when it was decided that we should sail to Italy, they delivered Paul and some other prisoners to one named Julius, a centurion of the Augustan Regiment.
chapters.kjv: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ ഞങ്ങൾ ആസ്യക്കര പറ്റി ഓടുവാനുള്ള ഒരു അദ്രമുത്ത്യകപ്പലിൽ കയറി നീക്കി; തെസ്സലൊനിക്കയിൽ നിന്നുള്ള മക്കെദോന്യക്കാരനായ അരിസ്തർഹൊസും ഞങ്ങളോടുകൂടെ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: We boarded a ship from Adramyttium about to sail for ports along the coast of the province of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
chapters.nkjv: So, entering a ship of Adramyttium, we put to sea, meaning to sail along the coasts of Asia. Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, was with us.
chapters.kjv: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

chapters.ml: പിറ്റെന്നു ഞങ്ങൾ സീദോനിൽ എത്തി; യൂലിയൊസ് പൌലൊസിനോടു ദയ കാണിച്ചു, സ്നേഹിതന്മാരുടെ അടുക്കൽ പോയി സൽക്കാരം കൈക്കൊൾവാൻ അനുവദിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: The next day we landed at Sidon; and Julius, in kindness to Paul, allowed him to go to his friends so they might provide for his needs.
chapters.nkjv: And the next day we landed at Sidon. And Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him liberty to go to his friends and receive care.
chapters.kjv: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.

chapters.ml: അവിടെ നിന്നു ഞങ്ങൾ നീക്കി, കാറ്റു പ്രതികൂലമാകയാൽ കുപ്രൊസ് ദ്വീപിന്റെ മറപറ്റി ഓടി;
chapters.niv: From there we put out to sea again and passed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
chapters.nkjv: When we had put to sea from there, we sailed under theshelterof Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
chapters.kjv: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

chapters.ml: കിലിക്യ പംഫുല്യ കടൽവഴിയായി ചെന്നു ലുക്കിയയിലെ മുറാപ്പട്ടണത്തിൽ എത്തി.
chapters.niv: When we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.
chapters.nkjv: And when we had sailed over the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, acity of Lycia.
chapters.kjv: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

chapters.ml: അവിടെ ശതാധിപൻ ഇതല്യെക്കു പോകുന്ന ഒരു അലെക്സന്ത്രിയക്കപ്പൽ കണ്ടു ഞങ്ങളെ അതിൽ കയറ്റി.
chapters.niv: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
chapters.nkjv: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italy, and he put us on board.
chapters.kjv: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.

chapters.ml: പിന്നെ ഞങ്ങൾ ബഹുദിവസം പതുക്കെ ഓടി, ക്നീദൊസ് തൂക്കിൽ പ്രയാസത്തോടെ എത്തി, കാറ്റു സമ്മതിക്കായ്കയാൽ ക്രേത്തദ്വീപിന്റെ മറപറ്റി ശല്മോനെക്കു നേരെ ഓടി,
chapters.niv: We made slow headway for many days and had difficulty arriving off Cnidus. When the wind did not allow us to hold our course, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
chapters.nkjv: When we had sailed slowly many days, and arrived with difficulty off Cnidus, the wind not permitting us to proceed, we sailed under theshelterof Crete off Salmone.
chapters.kjv: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;

chapters.ml: കരപറ്റി പ്രയാസത്തോടെ ലസയ്യപട്ടണത്തിന്റെ സമീപത്തു ശുഭതുറമുഖം എന്നു പേരുള്ള സ്ഥലത്തു എത്തി.
chapters.niv: We moved along the coast with difficulty and came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
chapters.nkjv: Passing it with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
chapters.kjv: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.

chapters.ml: ഇങ്ങനെ വളരെ നാൾ ചെന്നശേഷം നോമ്പും കഴിഞ്ഞിരിക്കെ കപ്പലോട്ടം വൈഷമ്യം ആകകൊണ്ടു പൌലൊസ്:
chapters.niv: Much time had been lost, and sailing had already become dangerous because by now it was after the Day of Atonement. So Paul warned them,
chapters.nkjv: Now when much time had been spent, and sailing was now dangerous because the Fast was already over, Paul advised them,
chapters.kjv: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them ,

chapters.ml: പുരുഷന്മാരേ, ഈ യാത്രയിൽ ചരക്കിന്നും കപ്പലിന്നും മാത്രമല്ല നമ്മുടെ പ്രാണങ്ങൾക്കും ഏറിയ കഷ്ടനഷ്ടങ്ങൾ വരും എന്നു ഞാൻ കാണുന്നു എന്നു അവരെ പ്രബോധിപ്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: "Men, I can see that our voyage is going to be disastrous and bring great loss to ship and cargo, and to our own lives also."
chapters.nkjv: saying, "Men, I perceive that this voyage will end with disaster and much loss, not only of the cargo and ship, but also our lives."
chapters.kjv: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.

chapters.ml: ശതാധിപനോ പൌലൊസ് പറഞ്ഞതിനെക്കാൾ മാലുമിയുടെയും കപ്പലുടമസ്ഥന്റെയും വാക്കു അധികം വിശ്വസിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: But the centurion, instead of listening to what Paul said, followed the advice of the pilot and of the owner of the ship.
chapters.nkjv: Nevertheless the centurion was more persuaded by the helmsman and the owner of the ship than by the things spoken by Paul.
chapters.kjv: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.

chapters.ml: ആ തുറമുഖം ശീതകാലം കഴിപ്പാൻ തക്കതല്ലായ്കയാൽ അവിടെ നിന്നു നീക്കി തെക്കുപടിഞ്ഞാറായും വടക്കുപടിഞ്ഞാറായും തുറന്നു കിടക്കുന്ന ഫൊയ്നീക്യ എന്ന ക്രേത്തതുറമുഖത്തു കഴിവുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ ചെന്നു ശീതകാലം കഴിക്കേണം എന്നു മിക്കപേരും ആലോചന പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided that we should sail on, hoping to reach Phoenix and winter there. This was a harbor in Crete, facing both southwest and northwest.
chapters.nkjv: And because the harbor was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised to set sail from there also, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete opening toward the southwest and northwest, and winter there.
chapters.kjv: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.

chapters.ml: തെക്കൻ കാറ്റു മന്ദമായി ഊതുകയാൽ താല്പര്യം സാധിച്ചു എന്നു തോന്നി, അവർ അവിടെ നിന്നു നങ്കൂരം എടുത്തു ക്രേത്ത ദ്വീപിന്റെ മറപറ്റി ഓടി.
chapters.niv: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they saw their opportunity; so they weighed anchor and sailed along the shore of Crete.
chapters.nkjv: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their desire, putting out to sea, they sailed close by Crete.
chapters.kjv: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence , they sailed close by Crete.

chapters.ml: കുറെ കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ടു അതിന്നു വിരോധമായി ഈശാനമൂലൻ എന്ന കൊടങ്കാറ്റു അടിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Before very long, a wind of hurricane force, called the Northeaster, swept down from the island.
chapters.nkjv: But not long after, a tempestuous head wind arose, called Euroclydon.
chapters.kjv: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.

chapters.ml: കപ്പൽ കാറ്റിന്റെ നേരെ നില്പാൻ കഴിയാതവണ്ണം കുടുങ്ങുകയാൽ ഞങ്ങൾ കൈവിട്ടു അങ്ങനെ പാറിപ്പോയി.
chapters.niv: The ship was caught by the storm and could not head into the wind; so we gave way to it and were driven along.
chapters.nkjv: So when the ship was caught, and could not head into the wind, we let her drive.
chapters.kjv: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.

chapters.ml: ക്ളൌദ എന്ന ചെറിയ ദ്വീപിന്റെ മറപറ്റി ഓടീട്ടു പ്രയാസത്തോടെ തോണി കൈവശമാക്കി.
chapters.niv: As we passed to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were hardly able to make the lifeboat secure,
chapters.nkjv: And running under theshelterof an island called Clauda, we secured the skiff with difficulty.
chapters.kjv: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:

chapters.ml: അതു വലിച്ചുകയറ്റീട്ടു അവർ കപ്പൽ ചുറ്റിക്കെട്ടിയും മറ്റും ഉറപ്പുവരുത്തി; പിന്നെ മണത്തിട്ടമേൽ അകപ്പെടും എന്നു പേടിച്ചു പായി ഇറക്കി അങ്ങനെ പാറിപ്പോയി.
chapters.niv: so the men hoisted it aboard. Then they passed ropes under the ship itself to hold it together. Because they were afraid they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and let the ship be driven along.
chapters.nkjv: When they had taken it on board, they used cables to undergird the ship; and fearing lest they should run aground on the Syrtis Sands, they struck sail and so were driven.
chapters.kjv: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.

chapters.ml: ഞങ്ങൾ കൊടുങ്കാറ്റിനാൽ അത്യന്തം അലയുകകൊണ്ടു പിറ്റെന്നു അവർ ചരക്കു പുറത്തുകളഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: We took such a violent battering from the storm that the next day they began to throw the cargo overboard.
chapters.nkjv: And because we were exceedingly tempest-tossed, the next day they lightened the ship.
chapters.kjv: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;

chapters.ml: മൂന്നാം നാൾ അവർ സ്വന്തകയ്യാൽ കപ്പൽകോപ്പും കടലിൽ ഇട്ടുകളഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
chapters.nkjv: On the third day we threw the ship’s tackle overboard with our own hands.
chapters.kjv: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.

chapters.ml: വളരെ നാളായിട്ടു സൂര്യനെയോ നക്ഷത്രങ്ങളെയോ കാണാതെയും വല്ലാത്ത കൊടുങ്കാറ്റു അടിച്ചുകൊണ്ടും ഇരിക്കയാൽ ഞങ്ങൾ രക്ഷപ്പെടും എന്നുള്ള ആശ ഒക്കെയും അറ്റുപോയി.
chapters.niv: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the storm continued raging, we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
chapters.nkjv: Now when neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small tempest beat on us, all hope that we would be saved was finally given up.
chapters.kjv: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us , all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.

chapters.ml: അവർ വളരെ പട്ടിണി കിടന്നശേഷം പൌലോസ് അവരുടെ നടുവിൽ നിന്നുകൊണ്ടു പറഞ്ഞതു: പുരുഷന്മാരേ, എന്റെ വാക്കു അനുസരിച്ചു ക്രേത്തയിൽനിന്നു നീക്കാതെയും ഈ കഷ്ട നഷ്ടങ്ങൾ സമ്പാദിക്കാതെയും ഇരിക്കേണ്ടതായിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: After they had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up before them and said: "Men, you should have taken my advice not to sail from Crete; then you would have spared yourselves this damage and loss.
chapters.nkjv: But after long abstinence from food, then Paul stood in the midst of them and said, "Men, you should have listened to me, and not have sailed from Crete and incurred this disaster and loss.
chapters.kjv: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.

chapters.ml: എങ്കിലും ഇപ്പോൾ ധൈര്യത്തോടിരിപ്പാൻ ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു; കപ്പലിന്നു അല്ലാതെ നിങ്ങളിൽ ആരുടെയും പ്രാണന്നു ഹാനി വരികയില്ല.
chapters.niv: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because not one of you will be lost; only the ship will be destroyed.
chapters.nkjv: And now I urge you to take heart, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
chapters.kjv: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.

chapters.ml: എന്റെ ഉടയവനും ഞാൻ സേവിച്ചുവരുന്നവനുമായ ദൈവത്തിന്റെ ദൂതൻ ഈ രാത്രിയിൽ എന്റെ അടുക്കൽനിന്നു:
chapters.niv: Last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me
chapters.nkjv: For there stood by me this night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve,
chapters.kjv: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,

chapters.ml: പൌലൊസേ, ഭയപ്പെടരുതു; നീ കൈസരുടെ മുമ്പിൽ നിൽക്കേണ്ടതാകുന്നു; നിന്നോടുകൂടെ യാത്രചെയ്യുന്നവരെ ഒക്കെയും ദൈവം നിനക്കു ദാനം ചെയ്തിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand trial before Caesar; and God has graciously given you the lives of all who sail with you.’
chapters.nkjv: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must be brought before Caesar; and indeed God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
chapters.kjv: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Cæsar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

chapters.ml: അതുകൊണ്ടു പുരുഷന്മാരേ, ധൈര്യത്തോടിരിപ്പിൻ; എന്നോടു അരുളിച്ചെയ്തതു പോലെ തന്നേ സംഭവിക്കും എന്നു ഞാൻ ദൈവത്തെ വിശ്വസിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: So keep up your courage, men, for I have faith in God that it will happen just as he told me.
chapters.nkjv: Therefore take heart, men, for I believe God that it will be just as it was told me.
chapters.kjv: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

chapters.ml: എങ്കിലും നാം ഒരു ദ്വീപിന്മേൽ മുട്ടി വീഴേണ്ടതാകുന്നു.
chapters.niv: Nevertheless, we must run aground on some island."
chapters.nkjv: However, we must run aground on a certain island."
chapters.kjv: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.

chapters.ml: പതിന്നാലാം രാത്രിയായപ്പോൾ ഞങ്ങൾ അദ്രിയക്കടലിൽ അലയുന്നേരം അർദ്ധരാത്രിയിൽ ഒരു കരെക്കു സമീപിക്കുന്നു എന്നു കപ്പൽക്കാർക്കു തോന്നി.
chapters.niv: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea, when about midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
chapters.nkjv: Now when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven up and down in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors sensed that they were drawing near some land.
chapters.kjv: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;

chapters.ml: അവർ ഈയം ഇട്ടു ഇരുപതു മാറെന്നു കണ്ടു കുറയ അപ്പുറം പോയിട്ടു വീണ്ടും ഈയം ഇട്ടു പതിനഞ്ചു മറ്റൊന്നു കണ്ടു.
chapters.niv: They took soundings and found that the water was a hundred and twenty feet deep. A short time later they took soundings again and found it was ninety feet deep.
chapters.nkjv: And they took soundings and found it to be twenty fathoms; and when they had gone a little farther, they took soundings again and found it to be fifteen fathoms.
chapters.kjv: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.

chapters.ml: പാറ സ്ഥലങ്ങളിൽ അകപ്പെടും എന്നു പേടിച്ചു അവർ അമരത്തു നിന്നു നാലു നങ്കൂരം ഇട്ടു, നേരം വെളുപ്പാൻ ആഗ്രഹിച്ചുകൊണ്ടിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: Fearing that we would be dashed against the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daylight.
chapters.nkjv: Then, fearing lest we should run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern, and prayed for day to come.
chapters.kjv: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ കപ്പൽക്കാർ കപ്പൽ വിട്ടു ഓടിപ്പോകുവാൻ വിചാരിച്ചു അണിയത്തുനിന്നു നങ്കൂരം ഇടുവാൻ പോകുന്നു എന്നുള്ള ഭാവത്തിൽ തോണി കടലിൽ ഇറക്കി.
chapters.niv: In an attempt to escape from the ship, the sailors let the lifeboat down into the sea, pretending they were going to lower some anchors from the bow.
chapters.nkjv: And as the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship, when they had let down the skiff into the sea, under pretense of putting out anchors from the prow,
chapters.kjv: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ പൌലൊസ് ശതാധിപനോടും പടയാളികളോടും: ഇവർ കപ്പലിൽ താമസിച്ചല്ലാതെ നിങ്ങൾക്കു രക്ഷപ്പെടുവാൻ കഴിയുന്നതല്ല എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Then Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay with the ship, you cannot be saved."
chapters.nkjv: Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, "Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved."
chapters.kjv: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.

chapters.ml: പടയാളികൾ തോണിയുടെ കയറു അറുത്തു അതു വീഴിച്ചുകളഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: So the soldiers cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it drift away.
chapters.nkjv: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the skiff and let it fall off.
chapters.kjv: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.

chapters.ml: നേരം വെളുക്കാറായപ്പോൾ പൌലൊസ് എല്ലാവരോടും ഭക്ഷണം കഴിക്കേണ്ടതിന്നു അപേക്ഷിച്ചു: നിങ്ങൾ ഒന്നും ഭക്ഷിക്കാതെ കാത്തുകൊണ്ടു പട്ടിണി കിടക്കുന്നതു ഇന്നു പതിന്നാലാം ദിവസം ആകുന്നുവല്ലോ.
chapters.niv: Just before dawn Paul urged them all to eat. "For the last fourteen days," he said, "you have been in constant suspense and have gone without food—you haven’t eaten anything.
chapters.nkjv: And as day was about to dawn, Paul implored them all to take food, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day you have waited and continued without food, and eaten nothing.
chapters.kjv: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.

chapters.ml: അതുകൊണ്ടു ആഹാരം കഴിക്കേണം എന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളോടു അപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നു; അതു നിങ്ങളുടെ രക്ഷെക്കുള്ളതല്ലോ; നിങ്ങളിൽ ഒരുത്തന്റെയും തലയിലെ ഒരു രോമംപോലും നഷ്ടമാകയില്ല നിശ്ചയം എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: Now I urge you to take some food. You need it to survive. Not one of you will lose a single hair from his head."
chapters.nkjv: Therefore I urge you to take nourishment, for this is for your survival, since not a hair will fall from the head of any of you."
chapters.kjv: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.

chapters.ml: ഇങ്ങനെ പറഞ്ഞിട്ടു അപ്പം എടുത്തു എല്ലാവരും കാൺകെ ദൈവത്തെ വാഴ്ത്തിട്ടു നുറുക്കി തിന്നുതുടങ്ങി.
chapters.niv: After he said this, he took some bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
chapters.nkjv: And when he had said these things, he took bread and gave thanks to God in the presence of them all; and when he had broken it he began to eat.
chapters.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it , he began to eat.

chapters.ml: അപ്പോൾ എല്ലാവരും ധൈര്യപ്പെട്ടു ഭക്ഷണം കഴിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: They were all encouraged and ate some food themselves.
chapters.nkjv: Then they were all encouraged, and also took food themselves.
chapters.kjv: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.

chapters.ml: കപ്പലിൽ ഞങ്ങൾ ആകപ്പാടെ ഇരുനൂറ്റെഴുപത്താറു ആൾ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു.
chapters.niv: Altogether there were 276 of us on board.
chapters.nkjv: And in all we were two hundred and seventy-six persons on the ship.
chapters.kjv: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

chapters.ml: അവർ തിന്നു തൃപ്തിവന്നശേഷം ധാന്യം കടലിൽ കളഞ്ഞു കപ്പലിന്റെ ഭാരം കുറെച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When they had eaten as much as they wanted, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
chapters.nkjv: So when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship and threw out the wheat into the sea.
chapters.kjv: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.

chapters.ml: വെളിച്ചമായപ്പോൾ ഇന്ന ദേശം എന്നു അവർ അറിഞ്ഞില്ല എങ്കിലും കരയുള്ളോരു തുറ കണ്ടു, കഴിയും എങ്കിൽ കപ്പൽ അതിലേക്കു ഓടിക്കേണം എന്നു ഭാവിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they saw a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
chapters.nkjv: When it was day, they did not recognize the land; but they observed a bay with a beach, onto which they planned to run the ship if possible.
chapters.kjv: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.

chapters.ml: നങ്കൂരം അറുത്തു കടലിൽ വിട്ടു ചുക്കാന്റെ കെട്ടും അഴിച്ചു പെരുമ്പായ് കാറ്റുമുഖമായി കൊടുത്തു കരെക്കു നേരെ ഓടി.
chapters.niv: Cutting loose the anchors, they left them in the sea and at the same time untied the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
chapters.nkjv: And they let go the anchors and left them in the sea, meanwhile loosing the rudder ropes; and they hoisted the mainsail to the wind and made for shore.
chapters.kjv: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.

chapters.ml: ഇരുകടൽ കൂടിയോരു സ്ഥലത്തിന്മേൽ ചെന്നു കയറുകയാൽ കപ്പൽ അടിഞ്ഞു അണിയം ഉറെച്ചു ഇളക്കമില്ലാതെയായി; അമരം തിരയുടെ കേമത്താൽ ഉടഞ്ഞുപോയി.
chapters.niv: But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was broken to pieces by the pounding of the surf.
chapters.nkjv: But striking a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the prow stuck fast and remained immovable, but the stern was being broken up by the violence of the waves.
chapters.kjv: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.

chapters.ml: തടവുകാരിൽ ആരും നീന്തി ഓടിപ്പോകാതിരിപ്പാൻ അവരെ കൊല്ലേണം എന്നു പടയാളികൾ ആലോചിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent any of them from swimming away and escaping.
chapters.nkjv: And the soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim away and escape.
chapters.kjv: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

chapters.ml: ശതാധിപനോ പൌലൊസിനെ രക്ഷിപ്പാൻ ഇച്ഛിച്ചിട്ടു അവരുടെ താല്പര്യം തടുത്തു, നീന്തുവാൻ കഴിയുന്നവർ ആദ്യം ചാടി കരെക്കു പറ്റുവാനും
chapters.niv: But the centurion wanted to spare Paul’s life and kept them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
chapters.nkjv: But the centurion, wanting to save Paul, kept them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should jump overboard first and get to land,
chapters.kjv: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea , and get to land:

chapters.ml: ശേഷമുള്ളവർ പലകമേലും കപ്പലിന്റെ ഖണ്ഡങ്ങളുടെ മേലുമായി എത്തുവാനും കല്പിച്ചു; ഇങ്ങനെ എല്ലാവരും കരയിൽ എത്തി രക്ഷപ്പെടുവാൻ സംഗതിവന്നു.
chapters.niv: The rest were to get there on planks or on other pieces of the ship. In this way everyone reached land safely.
chapters.nkjv: and the rest, some on boards and some on parts of the ship. And so it was that they all escaped safely to land.
chapters.kjv: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.

chapters.ml: രക്ഷപ്പെട്ടശേഷം ദ്വീപിന്റെ പേർ മെലിത്ത എന്നു ഞങ്ങൾ ഗ്രഹിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Once safely on shore, we found out that the island was called Malta.
chapters.nkjv: Now when they had escaped, they then found out that the island was called Malta.
chapters.kjv: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.

chapters.ml: അവിടത്തെ ബർബരന്മാർ ഞങ്ങൾക്കു അസാധാരണ ദയ കാണിച്ചു മഴയും ശീതവും നിമിത്തം തീ കൂട്ടി ഞങ്ങളെ ഒക്കെയും കൈക്കൊണ്ടു.
chapters.niv: The islanders showed us unusual kindness. They built a fire and welcomed us all because it was raining and cold.
chapters.nkjv: And the natives showed us unusual kindness; for they kindled a fire and made us all welcome, because of the rain that was falling and because of the cold.
chapters.kjv: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

chapters.ml: പൌലൊസ് കുറെ വിറകു പെറുക്കി തീയിൽ ഇട്ടപ്പൊൾ ഒരു അണലി ചൂടുനിമിത്തം പുറപ്പെട്ടു അവന്റെ കൈക്കു പറ്റി.
chapters.niv: Paul gathered a pile of brushwood and, as he put it on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself on his hand.
chapters.nkjv: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
chapters.kjv: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

chapters.ml: ആ ജന്തു അവന്റെ കൈമേൽ തൂങ്ങുന്നതു ബർബരന്മാർ കണ്ടപ്പോൾ: ഈ മനുഷ്യൻ ഒരു കുലപാതകൻ സംശയമില്ല; കടലിലൽ നിന്നു രക്ഷപ്പെട്ടിട്ടും നീതിദേവി അവനെ ജീവിച്ചിരിപ്പാൻ സമ്മതിക്കുന്നില്ല എന്നു തമ്മിൽ പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: When the islanders saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to each other, "This man must be a murderer; for though he escaped from the sea, the goddess Justice has not allowed him to live."
chapters.nkjv: So when the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, "No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet justice does not allow to live."
chapters.kjv: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.

chapters.ml: അവനോ ആ ജന്തുവിനെ തീയിൽ കുടഞ്ഞു കളഞ്ഞു, ദോഷം ഒന്നും പറ്റിയില്ല.
chapters.niv: But Paul shook the snake off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
chapters.nkjv: But he shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no harm.
chapters.kjv: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.

chapters.ml: അവൻ വീർക്കുകയോ പെട്ടെന്നു ചത്തു വീഴുകയോ ചെയ്യും എന്നു വെച്ചു അവർ കാത്തുനിന്നു; വളരെ നേരം കാത്തുനിന്നിട്ടും അവന്നു ആപത്തു ഒന്നും ഭവിക്കുന്നില്ല എന്നു കണ്ടു മനസ്സു മാറി അവൻ ഒരു ദേവൻ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: The people expected him to swell up or suddenly fall dead; but after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
chapters.nkjv: However, they were expecting that he would swell up or suddenly fall down dead. But after they had looked for a long time and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.
chapters.kjv: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

chapters.ml: ആ സ്ഥലത്തിന്റെ സമീപത്തു പുബ്ളിയൊസ് എന്ന ദ്വീപുപ്രമാണിക്കു ഒരു ജന്മഭൂമി ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു; അവൻ ഞങ്ങളെ ചേർത്തു മൂന്നു ദിവസം ആദരവോടെ അതിഥിസൽക്കാരം ചെയ്തു.
chapters.niv: There was an estate nearby that belonged to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us to his home and showed us generous hospitality for three days.
chapters.nkjv: In that region there was an estate of the leading citizen of the island, whose name was Publius, who received us and entertained us courteously for three days.
chapters.kjv: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.

chapters.ml: പുബ്ളിയൊസിന്റെ അപ്പൻ പനിയും അതിസാരവും പിടിച്ചു കിടപ്പായിരുന്നു. പൌലൊസ് അവന്റെ അടുക്കൽ അകത്തു ചെന്നു പ്രാർത്ഥിച്ചു അവന്റെമേൽ കൈവെച്ചു സൌഖ്യം വരുത്തി.
chapters.niv: His father was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him and, after prayer, placed his hands on him and healed him.
chapters.nkjv: And it happened that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and dysentery. Paul went in to him and prayed, and he laid his hands on him and healed him.
chapters.kjv: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.

chapters.ml: ഇതു സംഭവിച്ചശേഷം ദ്വീപിലെ മറ്റു ദീനക്കാരും വന്നു സൌഖ്യം പ്രാപിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: When this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured.
chapters.nkjv: So when this was done, the rest of those on the island who had diseases also came and were healed.
chapters.kjv: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:

chapters.ml: അവരും ഏറിയ സമ്മാനം തന്നു ഞങ്ങളെ മാനിച്ചു; ഞങ്ങൾ കപ്പൽ കയറുന്ന സമയം ആവശ്യമുള്ളതു കയറ്റിത്തന്നു.
chapters.niv: They honored us in many ways; and when we were ready to sail, they furnished us with the supplies we needed.
chapters.nkjv: They also honored us in many ways; and when we departed, they provided such things as were necessary.
chapters.kjv: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.

chapters.ml: മൂന്നു മാസം കഴിഞ്ഞശേഷം ആ ദ്വീപിൽ ശീതകാലം കഴിച്ചു കിടന്നിരുന്ന അശ്വനി ചിഹ്നമുള്ളോരു അലെക്സന്ത്രിയകപ്പലിൽ ഞങ്ങൾ കയറി പുറപ്പെട്ടു,
chapters.niv: After three months we put out to sea in a ship that had wintered in the island—it was an Alexandrian ship with the figurehead of the twin gods Castor and Pollux.
chapters.nkjv: After three months we sailed in an Alexandrian ship whose figurehead was the Twin Brothers, which had wintered at the island.
chapters.kjv: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

chapters.ml: സുറക്കൂസയിൽ കരെക്കിറിങ്ങി മൂന്നു നാൾ പാർത്തു; അവിടെ നിന്നു ചുറ്റി ഓടി രേഗ്യൊനിൽ എത്തി.
chapters.niv: We put in at Syracuse and stayed there three days.
chapters.nkjv: And landing at Syracuse, we stayed three days.
chapters.kjv: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.

chapters.ml: ഒരു ദിവസം കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ടു തെക്കങ്കാറ്റു അടിച്ചതിനാൽ പിറ്റേന്നു പുത്യൊലിയിൽ എത്തി.
chapters.niv: From there we set sail and arrived at Rhegium. The next day the south wind came up, and on the following day we reached Puteoli.
chapters.nkjv: From there we circled round and reached Rhegium. And after one day the south wind blew; and the next day we came to Puteoli,
chapters.kjv: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:

chapters.ml: അവിടെ സഹോദരന്മാരെ കണ്ടു തങ്ങളോടു കൂടെ ഏഴു നാൾ താമസിക്കേണം എന്നു അവൻ അപേക്ഷിച്ചു; പിന്നെ ഞങ്ങൾ റോമയിൽ എത്തി.
chapters.niv: There we found some brothers and sisters who invited us to spend a week with them. And so we came to Rome.
chapters.nkjv: where we found brethren, and were invited to stay with them seven days. And so we went toward Rome.
chapters.kjv: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.

chapters.ml: അവിടത്തെ സഹോദരന്മാർ ഞങ്ങളുടെ വർത്തമാനം കേട്ടിട്ടു അപ്യപുരവും ത്രിമണ്ഡപവും വരെ ഞങ്ങളെ എതിരേറ്റു വന്നു; അവരെ കണ്ടിട്ടു പൌലൊസ് ദൈവത്തെ വാഴ്ത്തി ധൈര്യം പ്രാപിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: The brothers and sisters there had heard that we were coming, and they traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. At the sight of these people Paul thanked God and was encouraged.
chapters.nkjv: And from there, when the brethren heard about us, they came to meet us as far as Appii Forum and Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
chapters.kjv: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.

chapters.ml: റോമയിൽ എത്തിയശേഷം തനിക്കു കാവലായ പടയാളിയോടുകൂടെ വേറിട്ടു പാർപ്പാൻ പൌലൊസിന്നു അനുവാദം കിട്ടി.
chapters.niv: When we got to Rome, Paul was allowed to live by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
chapters.nkjv: Now when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard; but Paul was permitted to dwell by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
chapters.kjv: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.

chapters.ml: മൂന്നു ദിവസം കഴിഞ്ഞിട്ടു അവൻ യെഹൂദന്മാരിൽ പ്രധാനികളായവരെ വിളിപ്പിച്ചു. അവർ വന്നുകൂടിയപ്പോൾ അവരോടു പറഞ്ഞതു: സഹോദരന്മാരേ, ഞാൻ ജനത്തിന്നോ പിതാക്കന്മാരുടെ ആചാരങ്ങൾക്കോ വിരോധം ഒന്നും ചെയ്തിട്ടില്ലാതിരിക്കെ എന്നെ യെരൂശലേമിൽനിന്നു ബദ്ധനായി റോമക്കാരുടെ കയ്യിൽ ഏല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Three days later he called together the local Jewish leaders. When they had assembled, Paul said to them: "My brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or against the customs of our ancestors, I was arrested in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
chapters.nkjv: And it came to pass after three days that Paul called the leaders of the Jews together. So when they had come together, he said to them: "Men and brethren, though I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, yet I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
chapters.kjv: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

chapters.ml: അവർ വിസ്തരിച്ചാറെ മരണയോഗ്യമായതു ഒന്നും എന്നിൽ കാണായ്കയാൽ എന്നെ വിട്ടയപ്പാൻ അവർക്കു മനസുണ്ടായിരുന്നു
chapters.niv: They examined me and wanted to release me, because I was not guilty of any crime deserving death.
chapters.nkjv: who, when they had examined me, wanted to let me go, because there was no cause for putting me to death.
chapters.kjv: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ യെഹൂദന്മാർ എതിർപറകയാൽ ഞാൻ കൈസരെ അഭയം ചൊല്ലേണ്ടിവന്നു; എന്റെ ജാതിയുടെ നേരെ അന്യായം ബോധിപ്പിപ്പാൻ എനിക്കു യാതൊന്നും ഉണ്ടായിട്ടല്ലതാനും.
chapters.niv: The Jews objected, so I was compelled to make an appeal to Caesar. I certainly did not intend to bring any charge against my own people.
chapters.nkjv: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything of which to accuse my nation.
chapters.kjv: But when the Jews spake against it , I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.

chapters.ml: ഇതു ഹേതുവായി നിങ്ങളെ കണ്ടു സംസാരിക്കേണം എന്നുവെച്ചു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളെ വിളിപ്പിച്ചു. യിസ്രായേലിന്റെ പ്രത്യാശനിമിത്തം ആകുന്നു ഞാൻ ഈ ചങ്ങല ചുമക്കുന്നതു.
chapters.niv: For this reason I have asked to see you and talk with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain."
chapters.nkjv: For this reason therefore I have called for you, to see you and speak with you, because for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain."
chapters.kjv: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you , and to speak with you : because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

chapters.ml: അവർ അവനോടു; നിന്റെ സംഗതിക്കു യെഹൂദ്യയിൽ നിന്നു ഞങ്ങൾക്കു എഴുത്തു വരികയോ സഹോദരന്മാരിൽ ആരും വന്നു നിന്നെക്കൊണ്ടു യാതൊരു ദോഷവുംപറകയോ ചെയ്തിട്ടില്ല.
chapters.niv: They replied, "We have not received any letters from Judea concerning you, and none of our people who have come from there has reported or said anything bad about you.
chapters.nkjv: Then they said to him, "We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor have any of the brethren who came reported or spoken any evil of you.
chapters.kjv: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judæa concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.

chapters.ml: എങ്കിലും ഈ മതഭേദത്തിന്നു എല്ലായിടത്തും വിരോധം പറയുന്നു എന്നു ഞങ്ങൾ അറിയുന്നതിനാൽ നിന്റെ മതം ഇന്നതു എന്നു നീ തന്നേ പറഞ്ഞുകേൾപ്പാൻ ആഗ്രഹിക്കുന്നു എന്നു പറഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: But we want to hear what your views are, for we know that people everywhere are talking against this sect."
chapters.nkjv: But we desire to hear from you what you think; for concerning this sect, we know that it is spoken against everywhere."
chapters.kjv: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.

chapters.ml: ഒരു ദിവസം നിശ്ചയിച്ചിട്ടു പലരും അവന്റെ പാർപ്പിടത്തിൽ അവന്റെ അടുക്കൽ വന്നു; അവരോടു അവൻ ദൈവരാജ്യത്തിന്നു സാക്ഷ്യം പറഞ്ഞു മോശെയുടെ ന്യായപ്രമാണവും പ്രവാചകപുസ്തകങ്ങളും ആധാരമാക്കി യേശുവിനെക്കുറിച്ചു അവർക്കു ബോധം വരുമാറു രാവിലെ തുടങ്ങി സന്ധ്യവരെ വിവരിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: They arranged to meet Paul on a certain day, and came in even larger numbers to the place where he was staying. He witnessed to them from morning till evening, explaining about the kingdom of God, and from the Law of Moses and from the Prophets he tried to persuade them about Jesus.
chapters.nkjv: So when they had appointed him a day, many came to him at his lodging, to whom he explained and solemnly testified of the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus from both the Law of Moses and the Prophets, from morning till evening.
chapters.kjv: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.

chapters.ml: അവൻ പറഞ്ഞതു ചിലർ സമ്മതിച്ചു; ചിലർ വിശ്വസിച്ചില്ല.
chapters.niv: Some were convinced by what he said, but others would not believe.
chapters.nkjv: And some were persuaded by the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.
chapters.kjv: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.

chapters.ml: അവർ തമ്മിൽ യോജിക്കാതെ പിരിഞ്ഞുപോകുമ്പോൾ പൌലൊസ് അവരോടു ഒരു വാക്കു പറഞ്ഞതെന്തെന്നാൽ:
chapters.niv: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: "The Holy Spirit spoke the truth to your ancestors when he said through Isaiah the prophet:
chapters.nkjv: So when they did not agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had said one word: "The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,
chapters.kjv: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,

chapters.ml: “നിങ്ങൾ ചെവികൊണ്ടു കേട്ടിട്ടും ഗ്രഹിക്കാതിരിക്കും; കണ്ണുകൊണ്ടു കണ്ടിട്ടും കാണാതിരിക്കും; കണ്ണുകൊണ്ടു കാണാതെയും ചെവികൊണ്ടു കേൾക്കാതെയും ഹൃദയംകൊണ്ടു ഗ്രഹിച്ചു മനന്തിരിയാതെയും.
chapters.niv: " ‘Go to this people and say, "You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving."
chapters.nkjv: saying, ‘Go to this people and say: "Hearing you will hear, and shall not understand; And seeing you will see, and not perceive;
chapters.kjv: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ അവരെ സൌഖ്യമാക്കാതെയും ഇരിക്കേണ്ടതിന്നു ഈ ജനത്തിന്റെ ഹൃദയം തടിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു. അവരുടെ ചെവി കേൾപ്പാൻ മന്ദമായിരിക്കുന്നു; അവരുടെ കണ്ണു അടെച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു എന്നു ഈ ജനത്തിന്റെ അടുക്കൽ പോയി പറക” എന്നിങ്ങനെ പരിശുദ്ധാത്മാവു യെശയ്യാപ്രവാചകൻ മുഖാന്തരം നിങ്ങളുടെ പിതാക്കന്മാരോടു പറഞ്ഞിരിക്കുന്നതു ശരി തന്നേ.
chapters.niv: For this people’s heart has become calloused; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts and turn, and I would heal them.’
chapters.nkjv: For the hearts of this people have grown dull. Their ears are hard of hearing, And their eyes they have closed, Lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, Lest they should understand with their hearts and turn, So that I should heal them." ’
chapters.kjv: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

chapters.ml: ആകയാൽ ദൈവം തന്റെ ഈ രക്ഷ ജാതികൾക്കു അയച്ചിരിക്കുന്നു; അവർ കേൾക്കും എന്നു നിങ്ങൾ അറിഞ്ഞുകൊൾവിൻ.
chapters.niv: "Therefore I want you to know that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!"
chapters.nkjv: "Therefore let it be known to you that the salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will hear it!"
chapters.kjv: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.

chapters.ml: അവൻ കൂലിക്കു വാങ്ങിയ വീട്ടിൽ രണ്ടു സംവത്സരം മുഴുവൻ പാർത്തു, തന്റെ അടുക്കൽ വരുന്നവരെ ഒക്കെയും കൈക്കൊണ്ടു
chapters.niv: For two whole years Paul stayed there in his own rented house and welcomed all who came to see him.
chapters.nkjv: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed and had a great dispute among themselves.
chapters.kjv: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.

chapters.ml: പൂർണ്ണ പ്രാഗത്ഭ്യത്തോടെ വിഘ്നംകൂടാതെ ദൈവരാജ്യം പ്രസംഗിച്ചും കർത്താവായ യേശുക്രിസ്തുവിനെക്കുറിച്ചു ഉപദേശിച്ചും പോന്നു.
chapters.niv: He proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ—with all boldness and without hindrance!
chapters.nkjv: Then Paul dwelt two whole years in his own rented house, and received all who came to him,
chapters.kjv: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,

chapters.ml: (null)
chapters.nkjv: preaching the kingdom of God and teaching the things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ with all confidence, no one forbidding him.
chapters.kjv: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.

chapters.ml: ദൈവം തന്റെ പുത്രനും നമ്മുടെ കർത്താവുമായ യേശുക്രിസ്തുവിനെക്കുറിച്ചു
chapters.niv: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle and set apart for the gospel of God—
chapters.nkjv: Paul, a bondservant of Jesus Christ, called tobe an apostle, separated to the gospel of God
chapters.kjv: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,

chapters.ml: വിശുദ്ധരേഖകളിൽ തന്റെ പ്രവാചകന്മാർ മുഖാന്തരം മുമ്പുകൂട്ടി വാഗ്ദത്തം ചെയ്ത സുവിശേഷത്തിന്നായി വേർതിരിച്ചു വിളിക്കപ്പെട്ട അപ്പൊസ്തലനും യേശുക്രിസ്തുവിന്റെ ദാസനുമായ പൌലൊസ്
chapters.niv: the gospel he promised beforehand through his prophets in the Holy Scriptures
chapters.nkjv: which He promised before through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,
chapters.kjv: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)

chapters.ml: റോമയിൽ ദൈവത്തിന്നു പ്രിയരും വിളിക്കപ്പെട്ട വിശുദ്ധന്മാരുമായ എല്ലാവർക്കും എഴുതുന്നതു:
chapters.niv: regarding his Son, who as to his earthly life was a descendant of David,
chapters.nkjv: concerning His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,
chapters.kjv: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;

chapters.ml: നമ്മുടെ പിതാവായ ദൈവത്തിങ്കൽനിന്നും കർത്താവായ യേശുക്രിസ്തുവിങ്കൽനിന്നും നിങ്ങൾക്കു കൃപയും സമാധാനവും ഉണ്ടാകട്ടെ.
chapters.niv: and who through the Spirit of holiness was appointed the Son of God in power by his resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.
chapters.nkjv: and declared tobe the Son of God with power according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead.
chapters.kjv: And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:

chapters.ml: ജഡം സംബന്ധിച്ചു ദാവീദിന്റെ സന്തതിയിൽനിന്നു ജനിക്കയും മരിച്ചിട്ടു ഉയിർത്തെഴുന്നേൽക്കയാൽ വിശുദ്ധിയുടെ ആത്മാവു സംബന്ധിച്ചു ദൈവപുത്രൻ എന്നു ശക്തിയോടെ നിർണ്ണയിക്കപ്പെടുകയും ചെയ്തിരിക്കുന്നവനാലല്ലോ ഞങ്ങൾ
chapters.niv: Through him we received grace and apostleship to call all the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith for his name’s sake.
chapters.nkjv: Through Him we have received grace and apostleship for obedience to the faith among all nations for His name,
chapters.kjv: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:

chapters.ml: അവന്റെ നാമത്തിന്നായി സകലജാതികളുടെയും ഇടയിൽ വിശ്വാസത്തിന്നു അനുസരണം വരുത്തേണ്ടതിന്നു കൃപയും അപ്പൊസ്തലത്വവും പ്രാപിച്ചതു.
chapters.niv: And you also are among those Gentiles who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
chapters.nkjv: among whom you also are the called of Jesus Christ;
chapters.kjv: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ:

chapters.ml: അവരിൽ യേശുക്രിസ്തുവിന്നായി വിളിക്കപ്പെട്ട നിങ്ങളും ഉൾപ്പെട്ടിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be his holy people: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.nkjv: To all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called tobe saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.kjv: To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

chapters.ml: നിങ്ങളുടെ വിശ്വാസം സർവ്വലോകത്തിലും പ്രസിദ്ധമായിരിക്കുന്നതിനാൽ ഞാൻ ആദ്യം തന്നേ എന്റെ ദൈവത്തിന്നു യേശുക്രിസ്തുമുഖാന്തരം നിങ്ങൾക്കെല്ലാവർക്കും വേണ്ടി സ്തോത്രം ചെയ്യുന്നു.
chapters.niv: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being reported all over the world.
chapters.nkjv: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.
chapters.kjv: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.

chapters.ml: ഞാൻ ഇടവിടാതെ നിങ്ങളെ ഓർത്തുകൊണ്ടു ദൈവേഷ്ടത്താൽ എപ്പോൾ എങ്കിലും നിങ്ങളുടെ അടുക്കൽ വരുവാൻ സാധിക്കേണ്ടതിന്നു എന്റെ പ്രാർത്ഥനയിൽ എപ്പോഴും യാചിക്കുന്നു
chapters.niv: God, whom I serve in my spirit in preaching the gospel of his Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you
chapters.nkjv: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of His Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers,
chapters.kjv: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;

chapters.ml: എന്നുള്ളതിന്നു അവന്റെ പുത്രനെക്കുറിച്ചുള്ള സുവിശേഷഘോഷണത്തിൽ ഞാൻ എന്റെ ആത്മാവിൽ ആരാധിക്കുന്ന ദൈവം എനിക്കു സാക്ഷി.
chapters.niv: in my prayers at all times; and I pray that now at last by God’s will the way may be opened for me to come to you.
chapters.nkjv: making request if, by some means, now at last I may find a way in the will of God to come to you.
chapters.kjv: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.

chapters.ml: നിങ്ങളുടെ സ്ഥിരീകരണത്തിന്നായി ആത്മികവരം വല്ലതും നിങ്ങൾക്കു നല്കേണ്ടതിന്നു,
chapters.niv: I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to make you strong—
chapters.nkjv: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, so that you may be established—
chapters.kjv: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;

chapters.ml: അതായതു നിങ്ങൾക്കും എനിക്കും ഒത്തൊരുമിച്ചുള്ള വിശ്വാസത്താൽ നിങ്ങളോടുകൂടെ എനിക്കും ആശ്വാസം ലഭിക്കേണ്ടതിന്നു ഞാൻ നിങ്ങളെ കാണ്മാൻ വാഞ്ഛിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.
chapters.nkjv: that is, that I may be encouraged together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.
chapters.kjv: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.

chapters.ml: എന്നാൽ സഹോദരന്മാരേ, എനിക്കു ശേഷം ജാതികളിൽ എന്നപോലെ നിങ്ങളിലും വല്ല ഫലവും ഉണ്ടാകേണ്ടതിന്നു നിങ്ങളുടെ അടുക്കൽ വരുവാൻ പലപ്പോഴും ഭാവിച്ചു എങ്കിലും ഇതുവരെ മുടക്കം വന്നു എന്നു നിങ്ങൾ അറിയാതിരിക്കരുതു എന്നു ഞാൻ ആഗ്രഹിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that I planned many times to come to you (but have been prevented from doing so until now) in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
chapters.nkjv: Now I do not want you to be unaware, brethren, that I often planned to come to you (but was hindered until now), that I might have some fruit among you also, just as among the other Gentiles.
chapters.kjv: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.

chapters.ml: യവനന്മാർക്കും ബർബരന്മാർക്കും ജ്ഞാനികൾക്കും ബുദ്ധിഹീനർക്കും ഞാൻ കടക്കാരൻ ആകുന്നു.
chapters.niv: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.
chapters.nkjv: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to wise and to unwise.
chapters.kjv: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.

chapters.ml: അങ്ങനെ റോമയിലുള്ള നിങ്ങളോടും സുവിശേഷം അറിയിപ്പാൻ എന്നാൽ ആവോളം ഞാൻ ഒരുങ്ങിയിരിക്കുന്നു.
chapters.niv: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
chapters.nkjv: So, as much as is in me, Iam ready to preach the gospel to you who are in Rome also.
chapters.kjv: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.

chapters.ml: സുവിശേഷത്തെക്കുറിച്ചു എനിക്കു ലജ്ജയില്ല; വിശ്വസിക്കുന്ന ഏവന്നും ആദ്യം യെഹൂദന്നും പിന്നെ യവനവന്നും അതു രക്ഷെക്കായി ദൈവശക്തിയാകുന്നുവല്ലോ.
chapters.niv: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes: first to the Jew, then to the Gentile.
chapters.nkjv: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is the power of God to salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first and also for the Greek.
chapters.kjv: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

chapters.ml: അതിൽ ദൈവത്തിന്റെ നീതി വിശ്വാസം ഹേതുവായും വിശ്വാസത്തിന്നായിക്കൊണ്ടും വെളിപ്പെടുന്നു. “നീതിമാൻ വിശ്വാസത്താൽ ജീവിക്കും” എന്നു എഴുതിയിരിക്കുന്നുവല്ലോ.
chapters.niv: For in the gospel the righteousness of God is revealed—a righteousness that is by faith from first to last, just as it is written: "The righteous will live by faith."
chapters.nkjv: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith; as it is written, "The just shall live by faith."
chapters.kjv: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.

chapters.ml: അനീതികൊണ്ടു സത്യത്തെ തടുക്കുന്ന മനുഷ്യരുടെ സകല അഭക്തിക്കും അനീതിക്കും നേരെ ദൈവത്തിന്റെ കോപം സ്വർഗ്ഗത്തിൽ നിന്നു വെളിപ്പെടുന്നു.
chapters.niv: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of people, who suppress the truth by their wickedness,
chapters.nkjv: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,
chapters.kjv: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;

chapters.ml: ദൈവത്തെക്കുറിച്ചു അറിയാകുന്നതു അവർക്കു വെളിവായിരിക്കുന്നു;
chapters.niv: since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.
chapters.nkjv: because what may be known of God is manifest in them, for God has shown it to them.
chapters.kjv: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

chapters.ml: ദൈവം അവർക്കു വെളിവാക്കിയല്ലോ. അവന്റെ നിത്യശക്തിയും ദിവ്യത്വവുമായി അവന്റെ അദൃശ്യലക്ഷണങ്ങൾ ലോകസൃഷ്ടിമുതൽ അവന്റെ പ്രവൃത്തികളാൽ ബുദ്ധിക്കു തെളിവായി വെളിപ്പെട്ടുവരുന്നു; അവർക്കു പ്രതിവാദമില്ലാതിരിക്കേണ്ടതിന്നു തന്നേ.
chapters.niv: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities—his eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse.
chapters.nkjv: For since the creation of the world His invisible attributes are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even His eternal power and Godhead, so that they are without excuse,
chapters.kjv: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

chapters.ml: അവർ ദൈവത്തെ അറിഞ്ഞിട്ടും അവനെ ദൈവമെന്നു ഓർത്തു മഹത്വീകരിക്കയോ നന്ദി കാണിക്കയോ ചെയ്യാതെ തങ്ങളുടെ നിരൂപണങ്ങളിൽ വ്യർത്ഥരായിത്തീർന്നു, അവരുടെ വിവേകമില്ലാത്ത ഹൃദയം ഇരുണ്ടുപോയി.
chapters.niv: For although they knew God, they neither glorified him as God nor gave thanks to him, but their thinking became futile and their foolish hearts were darkened.
chapters.nkjv: because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God, nor were thankful, but became futile in their thoughts, and their foolish hearts were darkened.
chapters.kjv: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

chapters.ml: ജ്ഞാനികൾ എന്നു പറഞ്ഞുകൊണ്ടു അവർ മൂഢരായിപ്പോയി;
chapters.niv: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools
chapters.nkjv: Professing to be wise, they became fools,
chapters.kjv: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

chapters.ml: അക്ഷയനായ ദൈവത്തിന്റെ തേജസ്സിനെ അവർ ക്ഷയമുള്ള മനുഷ്യൻ, പക്ഷി, നാൽക്കാലി, ഇഴജാതി എന്നിവയുടെ രൂപസാദൃശ്യമായി മാറ്റിക്കളഞ്ഞു.
chapters.niv: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images made to look like a mortal human being and birds and animals and reptiles.
chapters.nkjv: and changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like corruptible man—and birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.
chapters.kjv: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

chapters.ml: അതുകൊണ്ടു ദൈവം അവരെ തങ്ങളുടെ ഹൃദയങ്ങളിലെ മോഹങ്ങളിൽ സ്വന്തശരീരങ്ങളെ തമ്മിൽ തമ്മിൽ അവമാനിക്കേണ്ടതിന്നു അശുദ്ധിയിൽ ഏല്പിച്ചു.
chapters.niv: Therefore God gave them over in the sinful desires of their hearts to sexual impurity for the degrading of their bodies with one another.
chapters.nkjv: Therefore God also gave them up to uncleanness, in the lusts of their hearts, to dishonor their bodies among themselves,
chapters.kjv: Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:

chapters.ml: ദൈവത്തിന്റെ സത്യം അവർ വ്യാജമാക്കി മാറ്റിക്കളഞ്ഞു, സൃഷ്ടിച്ചവനെക്കാൾ സൃഷ്ടിയെ ഭജിച്ചു ആരാധിച്ചു; അവൻ എന്നേക്കും വാഴ്ത്തപ്പെട്ടവൻ, ആമേൻ.
chapters.niv: They exchanged the truth about God for a lie, and worshiped and served created things rather than the Creator—who is forever praised. Amen.
chapters.nkjv: who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
chapters.kjv: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.
